docs.content:
= Data Vault Update Action
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

== Description

The **Data Vault Update** workflow action is the main way to load a complete Data Vault model in Apache Hop. You point it at a saved Data Vault Model (`.hdv` file), choose a pipeline run configuration, and the action takes care of the rest.

If the model's Data Vault configuration has **Read-only existing vault** enabled, the action **fails immediately** after loading the model. Hop will not generate DDL, insert sentinels, or run load pipelines. Document the `.hdv` for Business Vault and dimensional layers instead; use **Update resource definition group** to skip that Data Vault job and continue BV/DM.

At runtime the action:

* Loads the model from the `.hdv` file.
* Optionally validates the model before any work is done.
* Optionally ensures unknown and invalid sentinel rows exist in hubs and links (per the model configuration).
* When any table uses orphan policy `QUARANTINE`, creates the shared quarantine table if it is missing.
* Optionally generates DDL (CREATE/ALTER statements) for the model's target database. DDL handling is independent of the data load: you can execute it on the database, write it to a SQL file, require that no DDL is needed, or combine these options.
* Generates update pipelines for every hub, link, and satellite in the model (unless you choose to skip the data load or filter by record source group).
* For **multi-source hubs and links**, also generates a **serial multi-source workflow** that runs each source pipeline one after another so keys written by an earlier source are visible to the next (required when primary keys are enabled).
* Stages free pipelines (satellites, single-source tables) to a folder and runs them through a **parallel orchestrator** (configurable copy count). Multi-source units run as workflows first, then free pipelines.
* Link CDC always sorts the **source** stream in Hop on the link hash key (hash is computed in the pipeline). For the **target** stream the plugin **automatically** chooses either SQL `ORDER BY` with a hop-compatible binary/`C` collation (when the target engine is known and the order is certain to match Hop SortRows) or a Hop Sort Rows transform. Linguistic database collations (PostgreSQL locale/ICU, SQL Server CI, MySQL `*_ci`, and others) can disagree with Java on STRING (decimal-dash) hash keys — for example `0-100-…` vs `0-10-…` — which breaks MergeRows and can re-insert existing keys under a primary key. This is **not PostgreSQL-only**; unknown engines fall back to Sort Rows. There is no user option for this: correctness is automatic.
* Uses a single load date for the entire batch, so every row written during one run of the action receives the same `LOAD_DATE` value.
* Aggregates row counts and errors from all generated pipelines into the workflow action result.

The action uses the same pipeline generation logic as the **Debug** button in the visual Data Vault model editor. What you inspect in the GUI is what runs in the workflow, with the addition of batch load date, optional model checks, sentinel row handling, and flexible DDL options.

== Dialog tabs

The action dialog is organized into three tabs.

image::images/action-data-vault-update.png[Data Vault Update action dialog,align="center"]

=== Model tab

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Action name
|The name of the action as it appears in the workflow. Standard Hop setting; does not affect loading.

|Data Vault Model file
|Path to the `.hdv` file. Variables supported (for example `${PROJECT_HOME}/vault1.hdv`). Required.

|Pipeline run configuration
|Pipeline Run Configuration used to execute every generated update pipeline. Required whenever data load pipelines run. Use the icons next to the field to create or manage run configurations.

|Log model check failures
|When enabled (default: on), runs `DataVaultModel.check()` before generating pipelines or DDL. Warnings are written with `logBasic`; errors are written with `logError`.

|Abort on model check failures
|When enabled (default: on), stops immediately if any check returns an error. Warnings alone do not abort.

|Detailed data type checking
|When enabled (default: on), model check validates source-to-target field type compatibility using the live source schema for database sources. Disable to validate using stored source field metadata only (faster, no database round-trip).

|Prefer last harvest for type checks
|When detailed checking is on (default: on), reuse DISCOVERED layouts from a schema harvest (`${DV_SCHEMA_HARVEST_RUN_ID}` or configured run id) instead of querying each source table. Falls back to live discovery when no harvest is available. See link:metadata-harvesting.adoc[Metadata harvesting].

|Harvest run id / history database
|Optional harvest location for type-check reuse.

|Parallel pipeline copies
|Number of Pipeline Executor copies used to run staged update pipelines in parallel (round-robin distribution). Default is `1` (sequential orchestration with one worker).

|Pipeline staging folder
|Folder where generated update pipelines are written before execution. When empty, defaults to `${java.io.tmpdir}/dv2/<model-name>/`. The folder is removed after a successful run.
|===

=== DDL tab

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Update target database structure
|When enabled (default: on), generates CREATE/ALTER DDL for every table and executes it on the model's target database before running data load pipelines. Disable when you manage schemas externally.

|Target type mapping
|Optional link:target-type-mappings.adoc[Target type mapping] applied before Hop dialect types. Empty uses unique auto-match on the model target connection.

|DDL SQL filename
|Optional path where generated DDL is written when schema changes are needed. Variables supported. The file begins with a `-- Target database: <connection name>` header followed by the statements. DDL is written only when changes are actually required. You can use this without executing DDL on the database.

|Fail if DDL is needed
|Fails immediately if any DDL would be required, before execution or file export. Useful in production or CI/CD to ensure schemas are already current.
|===

=== Source tab

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Record source group
|Optional filter. When set, only record sources whose **Group** field in Data Vault Source metadata matches this value are processed. Leave empty to update all sources. Supports variables (for example `hourly` or `daily`).

|Ensure unknown and invalid records
|When enabled (default: on), checks each hub and link for missing unknown and invalid sentinel rows (per the model configuration) and inserts them before running load pipelines.

|Do not update target database
|When enabled, skips running data load pipelines. DDL generation, file export, and execution (when configured) still run. Use for schema-only maintenance in the same workflow step.
|===

== Typical option combinations

* **Full load (default)** – All Model and DDL defaults on, Source tab options off. Validates the model (with detailed type checking), applies DDL if needed, ensures sentinel rows, stages and runs all pipelines.
* **Fast model check** – Disable **Detailed data type checking** when you only want structural validation and stored-metadata type checks (for example in CI without database connectivity).
* **Parallel load** – Set **Parallel pipeline copies** to `2` or higher on large models to run staged table pipelines concurrently.
* **Schema export only** – Enable **DDL SQL filename**, disable **Update target database structure**, enable **Do not update target database**. Writes DDL to a file without loading data.
* **Partial load by feed group** – Set **Record source group** to match the `Group` on selected Data Vault Sources (for example only `nightly` feeds).
* **Production guard** – Enable **Fail if DDL is needed** so the action fails if the target schema is not already aligned with the model. When any DDL is generated, the action logs a **source-to-target lineage explanation** (which mappings force the structural change). See link:source-to-target-lineage.adoc[Source-to-target lineage].

== DDL and target database

Each model references a single target database in its embedded configuration. DDL generation collects one statement per table, executes against that connection, and (when a filename is set) writes a single file with one target-database header. This matches the one-vault-database-per-model design used throughout the plugin.

:toc: macro

toc::[]

**Data Hopper EDW** is a set of Apache Hop plugins for an **Enterprise Data Warehouse**: catalog, source models, **model-driven Data Vault 2.0**, **Business Vault**, and **dimensional** loading. Version **0.12.0-SNAPSHOT** (latest release **0.11.0**) requires **Apache Hop 2.20.0-SNAPSHOT** and **Java 21**.

**Model once. Generate loads and consumption layers.** The visual models (`.hsm`, `.hdv`, `.hbv`, `.hdm`) are the contract between architects, modelers, and operations.

**Build an EDW:** link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]. **Architecture** (catalog, resource definition group, four controls): link:architecture.adoc[Architecture]. **Tour the sample:** link:getting-started-retail.adoc[Getting started — retail]. **AdventureWorks demo** (SQL Server source → Postgres DV/BV/DM): link:getting-started-adventureworks.adoc[Getting started — AdventureWorks] (issue https://github.com/ProjectDataHopper/hopper-edw/issues/180[#180]).

For a slide-style executive summary, see link:presentations/hop-data-vault-overview.md[presentations/hop-data-vault-overview.md]. Interactive HTML presentation: link:presentations/hop-data-vault-features.html[hop-data-vault-features.html]. For DV concepts and canvas usage, see link:datavault-plugin.adoc[Data Vault plugin].

**Large teams / hundreds of tables:** how to split models, assign personas (modeler, admin, ops, BV/DM, analysts), use git and the data catalog, and orchestrate loads — see link:enterprise-modeling-and-team-collaboration.adoc[Organizing large Data Vault programs].

== Architecture (logical)

Full pictures (catalog writers/readers, resource definition group spine, build vs run, harvest vs schema gate vs quality): link:architecture.adoc[Architecture].

image::images/diagrams/d1-logical-layers.svg[D1 — Logical layers,align="center"]

A **resource definition group** lists the `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm` files. **Update resource definition group** loads them (DV then BV then DM) and can publish target layouts back to the catalog. See link:resource-definition-group.adoc[Resource definition group].

== Major capabilities

=== Data Catalog and sources

Record definitions of type **`DV_SOURCE`** describe logical feeds: record-source indicator, optional **group** for partial loads, and physical layout (database table, file types, or **composite** multi-table query). Definitions live under namespace `hop/{project}/sources` in the project's FILE catalog storage directory (retail: `work/edw-catalog/`) and open in the **Data Catalog** perspective.

Hubs, links, and satellites reference source **names**, not raw connection details — one stable vocabulary from catalog through models to generated pipelines. A link:resource-definition-group.adoc[resource definition group] lists the warehouse models that harvest, validate, and load together. Pictures: link:architecture.adoc[Architecture].

=== Source modeler (`.hsm`)

Visual **source-system** modeler: import tables with PK/FK, draw relationships, **generate a raw Data Vault** (hubs, links, satellites, reference tables, hierarchy aliases) from selected tables, queries, JSON extractions, and pipelines after review, compose **source queries** (joins + projections), **source JSON** extractions (flatten a parent JSON field; chain steps for nested arrays), **pipeline sources** (declare a `.hpl` + output transform + field contract; publish as catalog **`PIPELINE`**), and **source masking** cards (a virtual table that runs Hop Mask fields; publish as catalog **`MASKING`**). **Validate** tables/queries/JSON/masking/pipelines/relationships at design time. Publish queries as **`COMPOSITE`**, JSON as **`JSON`**, masking cards as **`MASKING`**, pipelines as **`PIPELINE`**; Data Vault loads generate SQL/Merge Join, parent + JsonInput, parent + Mask fields, or MetaInject pipelines (with record-source injection and hub sort/distinct where needed). Catalog **Go to origin** opens the `.hsm` card for published pipeline/JSON/composite feeds. Retail sample: `retail-example/models/source-tables-crm.hsm` (shipment JSON + ASN pipeline) → `retail-360.hdv`. See link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[Source modeler].

image::images/source-modeler-retail-example-with-query-dialog-generated-sql.png[Source modeler — retail CRM tables with All customer info query SQL,align="center"]

image::images/source-modeler-example.png[Source modeler — tables, query, and JSON source cards,align="center"]

image::images/source-modeler-json-source.png[Source JSON dialog — extract fields from a parent JSON column,align="center"]

image::images/source-modeler-pipeline-source-graph.png[Source modeler — pipeline source card and relationships,align="center"]

image::images/source-modeler-pipeline-source-dialog.png[Source pipeline dialog — file, transform, and declared fields,align="center"]

image::images/source-modeler-generate-data-vault-model-dialog.png[Generate Data Vault from source model — review proposed hubs, links, and satellites,align="center"]

=== Project and metadata search (Hop 2.19)

Hop **Search Everywhere** / project search includes Data Hopper EDW models and metadata:

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Scope |Examples of matches

|`.hsm`
|Source tables, relationships, multi-table **query** names, WHERE text, published feed names

|`.hdv`
|Hub / link / satellite names, physical names, configuration, canvas notes

|`.hbv` / `.hdm`
|BV and dimensional table names, paths, configuration, notes

|`.hlv`
|Lineage backend name, logical table, dataset/job names, model file

|Resource definition group
|Group name, catalog connection, listed `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm` paths

|Data catalog, metrics profile, quality rule set
|Connection paths, rule field names, metrics folder
|===

Open a model hit to open the file (or focus an open tab) and jump to the matching table or source query when the hit carries a component name. Open tabs search **unsaved** in-memory content. Full usage: link:search.adoc[Search].

image::images/search-dialog-finding-results-in-models.png[Search Everywhere — model hit under Project files,align="center"]

image::images/search-panel-model-results.png[Search panel — Data Vault model match with matched text and file details,align="center"]

=== Raw Data Vault (`.hdv`)

Visual modeler for hubs, links, and satellites with embedded configuration (target database, hashing, sentinels, column names, pipeline options). Toolbar actions: **Edit model**, **Import sources**, **Check model**, **Generate DDL**, **Debug**, optional **AI Help**. A configuration **Read-only existing vault** checkbox documents an already-built vault so Business Vault and dimensional models can sit on top without Hop loading or altering those tables.

**Data Vault Update** workflow action validates (optionally), generates DDL, stages update pipelines, and runs them in parallel with a shared load timestamp.

=== Model validation and schema gate

**Check model** in the GUI and model checks in update actions share one engine: structural rules plus optional **detailed data type checking** against live source schemas.

Catalog **resource definition validation** adds feed-level checks with remediation proposals, acknowledgements, and **downstream impact** (Source→DV→BV→DM). From a **Resource definition group** you can **Tag catalog version**, **List catalog versions**, and **Validate sources** (options dialog for baseline + axes). Length remediation expands models and multi-layer DDL (DV/BV/DM) **from the catalog length** without rewriting the catalog. Retail sample package: `workflows/schema-remediation/accept-address_line1/` (see link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation]).

The **Validate resource definitions** workflow action is the **CI/CD schema gate**:

* Compare modes: live source vs catalog, working tree vs tagged baseline, or version vs version
* Failure severity (`FAIL_ON_BLOCKING`, `FAIL_ON_WARNINGS`, `WARN_ONLY`)
* Markdown/HTML reports (for example under `work/reports/`) with blast-radius tables

See link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation] and link:data-catalog.adoc#catalog-versions[Data Catalog — catalog versions].

image::images/validate-resource-definitions-action-dialog.png[Validate resource definitions action dialog,align="center"]

=== Business Vault (`.hbv`)

Linked to a `.hdv` model. Defines **SCD2** consumption tables (single- or multi-satellite merge), **PIT** helpers, **bridges** (query-friendly hub hash-key tables, usually from a DV link), and **SQL views/tables** (dbt-style `ref` / `source`, optional Jinja macros). **Import dbt models** on the canvas (and the **Import dbt project** workflow action) loads a dbt-core project as SQL business tables. **Business Vault Update** validates, optionally publishes target layouts to the catalog, generates SCD2 build pipelines (hash-key partitioned full rebuilds run as truncate-then-load wrapper workflows), and orchestrates parallel execution.

image::images/business-vault-dbt-import-models-dialog.png[Import dbt models dialog — project folder, model list, destination, and macro library,align="center"]

=== Dimensional modeler (`.hdm`)

Kimball star/snowflake modeling: dimensions, facts, junk dimensions, bridges, snapshot facts, and aggregates. **Dimensional Publish** drafts a `.hdm` from a `.hdv`; **Dimensional Update** loads the mart. Shares canvas interaction patterns with the DV modeler.

=== Execution maps (`.hem`)

Crawl a root workflow or model and persist a graph of workflows, models, generated pipelines, and source datasets. Open `.hem` files in Hop GUI for execution and lineage views. The retail example includes maps for its main update workflow and the six-month simulation.

image::images/execution-map-in-hop-gui-simulate-six-months.png[Execution map in Hop GUI — simulate-6-months,align="center"]

=== Hop Lineage View (`.hlv`)

Author a small view definition (seed table, depth, backend) and query **Marquez**, a folder of exported OpenLineage events, or the current models. The graph is not stored in the file. **Show lineage** on a DV/BV/DM table opens an unsaved upstream tab. Load-time badges come from the Hop OPS database — Marquez `latestRun` is the last _export_, not the last _load_. Retail sample: `retail-example/models/f_orders-upstream.hlv`. See link:hop-lineage-view.adoc[Hop Lineage View].

image::images/lineage-view-with-information-pane.png[Hop Lineage View — upstream graph and Markdown details pane,align="center"]

=== AI Help

Optional LLM advisory on Data Vault models, pipelines, and workflows — scenarios, context inclusions, review-before-apply proposals. Configure under Hop GUI → **Configuration → AI Assistant**.

The **Performance tuning** scenario can include load-run metrics and propose model configuration changes (parallel copies, preload lookup cache) after review:

image::images/ai-advisor-offering-performance-tuning-advice.png[AI advisor — performance tuning recommendations,align="center"]

=== Pipeline transforms

* **Get Record Definition Names** — stream catalog record definition metadata (or field layouts) as pipeline rows.
* **Catalog Record Definition Metadata Output** — discover or migrate field layouts into the data catalog (including stream field grouping).
* **Record Definition Input** — read actual data rows from a catalog record definition (same path as catalog Preview data).
* **Date Dimension Generator** — populate standard calendar dimension attributes.
* **Synthetic data** — seeded rows (sequences, choices, parent/child, unique pairs, optional nested XML). Retail source waves use `retail-example/pipelines/generate-retail-data.hpl`.

=== Operations

Docker-based runners (`scripts/run-hop.sh`, `run-postgres.sh`), parallel pipeline orchestration, **record source group** partial loads, catalog-backed load-run metrics, workflow load overview reports, and per-table duration bars on model graphs.

**Preferred batch shape:** **Update resource definition group** runs every DV/BV/DM model listed on a resource definition group (layer order DV → BV → DM), manages Begin/End-style vault update metrics in one action, and can write Markdown/HTML **load overview** reports. See link:update-resource-definition-group-action.adoc[Update resource definition group], link:operations.adoc[Operations], and link:performance-tuning.md[Performance tuning].

image::images/update-resource-definition-group-action-dialog.png[Update resource definition group action dialog,align="center"]

image::images/action-update-resource-group-load-metrics-dialog.png[Resource group load metrics — live wave progress and transform metrics,align="center"]

image::images/workflow-load-overview-summary-models.png[Workflow load overview — per-model summary,align="center"]

image::images/data-vault-retail-360-model-with-duration-metrics.png[Retail 360 model with load duration overview,align="center"]

== Sample projects

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Project |Use for

|link:../retail-example/README.md[retail-example]
|Learning path — CSV → CRM → DV → BV → DM, initial and monthly updates

|link:../integration-tests/PROJECT.md[integration-tests]
|CI/regression — Customer 360, multi-active, external read-only, golden datasets
|===

image::images/data-vault-model-retail-example.png[Retail 360 Data Vault model,align="center"]

**Recommended path:** link:architecture.adoc[Architecture] → link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW] to build → link:getting-started-retail.adoc[Getting started — retail] to tour the sample → link:getting-started-integration-tests.adoc[Getting started — integration tests] for advanced fixtures.

== 0.1.x focus

The transition from 0.0.x to 0.1.x emphasizes:

* Documentation completeness and accurate catalog-first workflows
* Validation UX (model checks + catalog issue handling, schema gates, catalog versions)
* First-time build order (link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]) plus the retail sample tour
* Hardening existing modelers and actions rather than large new subsystems

docs.content:
= Generate a Data Vault from a source model
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 2

toc::[]

When a link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[source model] (`.hsm`) already has tables, primary keys, and relationships, you can **generate hubs, satellites, links, and reference tables** into a new or existing Data Vault model (`.hdv`) instead of wiring every object by hand.

This is a **raw-vault starter**. Review the proposals, then refine names, business keys, and Business Vault work as usual.

== Where to start

* **Source modeler** toolbar / canvas: *Generate Data Vault…*  
  Uses the selected table, query, JSON, and pipeline cards, or every card if nothing is selected. You choose a **new** `.hdv` or an **existing** one.
* **Data Vault modeler** toolbar / canvas: *Generate from source model…*  
  Pick an `.hsm` and apply into the **open** vault (one undo). The coach panel **Generate DV** button opens the same path.
* **AI Help** on a Data Vault model includes a compact classification of sibling `.hsm` files in the same folder so the advisor can refine the same heuristic instead of starting from scratch.
* **AI Help** on the source modeler (`.hsm`) is chat-only and uses the same classification JSON so you can review Generate Data Vault before applying it on the canvas.

All of those paths open the same review dialog.

image::images/source-modeler-generate-data-vault-model.png[Source modeler toolbar Generate Data Vault action over the retail CRM tables,align="center"]

== Review dialog

Uncheck a row to skip that object. Edit **Vault name** before Apply. Options on the same screen (not a wizard):

* Create links for leftover foreign keys (for example `order_header.customer_id` → `lnk_order`)
* Create hub satellites from descriptive columns
* Exclude load-date / record-source columns
* Exclude foreign-key columns from satellites (uncheck to keep them for raw audit)
* Classify lookup / code tables as **reference tables** (`ref_*`)
* Create hierarchy links (and a hub alias) for self-referencing foreign keys
* Create one n-ary transactional link when a query, JSON, or pipeline feed has leftover keys to two or more hubs
* Include source queries, JSON extractions, and pipeline cards
* Publish unpublished tables to the catalog when the source model has a catalog connection

From the source modeler, choose **New Data Vault model**, **Existing Data Vault model**, or **Split into hub and link models**. From an open Data Vault model the same review can apply into **This Data Vault model** or split instead. Split does not write into the model that is already open.

image::images/source-modeler-generate-data-vault-model-dialog.png[Generate Data Vault from source model review dialog with proposed hubs, satellites, and links,align="center"]

== Split into hub and link models

Use this when one generated canvas would be too large to review or to merge. Apply still classifies once. The result is written as separate `.hdv` files:

[cols="1,2", options="header"]
|===
|File |Contents

|One file per hub
|That hub and the satellites whose parent is the hub

|One file per link
|That link, its link satellites, and a linked-table card for every participating hub

|One file per reference table
|That reference table only
|===

Link files do not copy hub metadata. Each hub card is a cross-model linked table (`referencedModelFilename`, usually `${PROJECT_HOME}/...`). A hierarchy link keeps the natural hub and the parent role alias (`hub_*_parent`) as two linked tables that point at the hub file. Linked tables are not loaded and do not get their own DDL.

On the review dialog:

* **Folder** — where the files are written. Defaults to the source model's folder, or `${PROJECT_HOME}/models` when that variable is set and the source file has not been saved.
* **Prefix** — optional text in front of each file name. `aw` is stored as `aw_`, so a hub becomes `aw_hub_customer.hdv`. Leave it empty to keep the vault object name.
* **Naming scheme** — when the project has a Data Vault model naming scheme (`edw-dv-model`), that scheme formats the file name. Hub, link, and satellite schemes are not applied again; the object names already use them. The dialog shows an example of the first hub and link file.
* **When a file already exists** — **Skip** (default) leaves the file untouched and does not merge new satellites into it. **Replace** overwrites the whole file.

Load **hub and reference files before link files**. Add the new files to the resource definition group before a group update; generation does not edit the group. Check each model you open. The confirmation lists how many files were written and does not open a tab per file.

== How sources are classified

The classifier uses **column membership**, not the stored child/parent labels, so inverted relationship edges still work. Query, JSON, and pipeline cards use the same grain rules as tables.

[cols="2,3", options="header"]
|===
|Source shape |Generated objects

|Several tables (or a query at the same grain) share the same primary key
|One hub (kernel table, preferring names like `customer_hub`) + one satellite per other table or composed feed

|Primary key is two or more foreign keys (+ optional extras)
|Link + optional link satellite; leftover key parts become dependent child keys

|Own primary key, plus leftover foreign keys
|Hub + optional satellite + binary link(s)

|Small lookup / code table (incoming FKs, few attributes, or a name like `country`)
|Reference table (`ref_*`). Parents of junction tables stay hubs.

|Self-referencing foreign key (for example `employee.manager_id`)
|Hub + hub alias (`hub_*_parent`) + hierarchy link

|Query / JSON / pipeline with its own identity and leftover FKs to two or more hubs
|Hub + satellite + one n-ary transactional link

|JSON or pipeline with its own key and a parent FK
|Hub + satellite + binary (or n-ary) link to the parent hub

|Isolated **table** with no table-to-table relationship
|Skipped — draw relationships first, or map it from a JSON/pipeline child

|No primary key (and no inferable identity on a feed)
|Skipped
|===

=== Retail CRM example

Selecting the landing tables in `retail-example/models/source-tables-crm.hsm` is expected to propose:

* `hub_customer` plus `sat_customer_demo`, `sat_customer_contact`, `sat_customer_address`, `sat_customer_prefs`
* `hub_product` / `sat_product`, `hub_warehouse` / `sat_warehouse`, `hub_sales_rep` / `sat_sales_rep`
* `hub_order` / `sat_order` / `lnk_order`
* `hub_order_rep` and leftover-FK links to `hub_sales_rep` when `order_rep` is in the model
* `lnk_order_line` / `sat_lnk_order_line` (dependent child key `line_number`)
* `lnk_warehouse_product` / `sat_lnk_warehouse_product`
* `order_shipment_tracking` (JSON) as `hub_order_shipment_tracking` plus a leftover-FK link to `hub_order`
* `asn-package-lines` (pipeline) as `hub_asn_package_lines` plus one n-ary link to the order, product, warehouse, and customer hubs

`order_shipment_event` is skipped (no table-to-table relationship). The JSON child of that event is classified.

== After apply

image::images/source-modeler-generated-data-vault-result.png[Generated Data Vault canvas with hub_customer satellites and the Created 20 tables confirmation,align="center"]

. **Check model** on the `.hdv`.
. Open each new table if you need to adjust keys or mappings.
. Run **Data Vault Update** as usual. Generation does not create pipelines by itself.

Existing vault tables are **reused** when a hub already has the same business-key source fields or catalog feed. Objects are never overwritten.

== Related documentation

* link:getting-started-edw.adoc#chapter-2[Getting started — generate the Data Vault]
* link:architecture.adoc[Architecture]
* link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[Source modeler overview]
* link:dv-hub.adoc[Hubs]
* link:dv-link.adoc[Links]
* link:dv-satellite.adoc[Satellites]
* link:dv-cross-model-references.adoc[Linked tables / hub aliases] (a single-file hierarchy uses a same-model hub alias; a split hierarchy stores that alias as a cross-model linked table)
* link:ai-advisory.md[AI Help]
* link:datavault-plugin.adoc[Data Vault plugin]

# Data Hopper EDW documentation index

Documentation for the **Data Hopper EDW** plugin (development **0.12.0-SNAPSHOT**, latest release **0.11.0**). Requires **Apache Hop 2.20.0-SNAPSHOT**. Highlights include **Free SQL / hop-hsm JDBC**, **source modeler** (`.hsm` with JSON and pipeline sources), **metadata harvesting**, optional **load cycle IDs**, **composite hub business keys**, **OpenLineage / Marquez export**, **Hop Lineage View** (`.hlv`), **source-to-target lineage**, catalog version tags, schema validation, multi-DB hardening, and Business Vault incremental loading. See [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md).

**New here?** Read [architecture.adoc](architecture.adoc) (catalog, models, resource definition group), then [getting-started-edw.adoc](getting-started-edw.adoc) to **build** an EDW. To **tour** a finished sample, use [getting-started-retail.adoc](getting-started-retail.adoc) or [getting-started-adventureworks.adoc](getting-started-adventureworks.adoc). Capability list: [feature-overview.adoc](feature-overview.adoc).

Architecture pictures are **committed SVGs** (`docs/images/diagrams/`) generated from PlantUML (`docs/diagrams/`). Do not put Mermaid or Markdown ` ``` ` fences in `.adoc` files.

`mvn package` writes an HTML copy of this guide to `target/generated-docs/` and into the plugin zip at `plugins/misc/hopper-edw/docs/` (open `index.html`).

| [performance-tuning.md](performance-tuning.md) | Sort memory and pipeline tuning |
| [ai-advisory.md](ai-advisory.md) | AI Help setup and usage |

## Sample Hop projects

| Folder | Document | Role |
|--------|----------|------|
| [../retail-example/](../retail-example/) | [../retail-example/README.md](../retail-example/README.md) | **Learn** — full-stack retail demo |
| [../adventureworks/](../adventureworks/) | [getting-started-adventureworks.adoc](getting-started-adventureworks.adoc) | **Demo / benchmark** — AdventureWorks SQL Server → Postgres (issue #180) |
| [../integration-tests/](../integration-tests/) | [../integration-tests/PROJECT.md](../integration-tests/PROJECT.md) | **Reference / CI** — regression suites |
| [../scripts/](../scripts/) | [../scripts/README.md](../scripts/README.md) | Shared Docker runners |

## Command-line tools

### `hop export`

Hop 2.20's unified diagram export. With this plugin installed it also loads EDW files:

```bash
hop export -f integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/customer-360.hdv --format svg -o /tmp/customer-360.svg
hop export -f models/retail-f-orders.hdm --format puml -o /tmp/retail-f-orders.puml
hop export -f models/retail-f-orders.hdm --format mermaid -o /tmp/retail-f-orders.mmd
hop export -f models/retail-f-orders.hdm --format drawio -o /tmp/retail-f-orders.drawio
hop export -f models/retail-f-orders.hdm --format pdf -o /tmp/retail-f-orders.pdf
hop export --list-exporters
```

Supported EDW extensions: `.hsm`, `.hdv`, `.hbv`, `.hdm`, `.hem`. Formats: **SVG**, **PDF**, **PlantUML** (`.puml`), **Draw.io** (`.drawio`), **Mermaid** (`.mmd`; execution maps emit a flowchart). Lineage views (`.hlv`) export SVG from an **open** Lineage View tab (the graph is a live session). Multi-model Draw.io rollups stay on `hop architecture-export`. Extra option keys (GUI `DiagramExportOptions.extraOptions`, when the Hop dialog/CLI supplies them): `syntaxStyle` (`CLASS`/`ENTITY`), `diagramType` (`ER`/`CLASS`), `layout` (`ELK`/`SWIMLANE`), `includeDataTypes`, `includeGrain`, `markdownFence`, `includeColumnDetails`.

### `hop svg`

Compatibility CLI for the same SVG painters (pipelines, workflows, `.hsm` / `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm` / `.hem`). Prefer `hop export` when you are on Hop 2.20.

**Docker (no local Hop install):** from `integration-tests/`:

```bash
cd integration-tests
./run-svg.sh -f tests/multi-satellite-bv/customer-360.hdv \
             -o ../docs/images/customer-360.svg --no-notes
```

**Local Hop** with the plugin installed:

```bash
hop svg -f integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/customer-360.hdv \
        -o docs/images/customer-360-generated.svg --no-notes
hop svg -s integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv -t /tmp/svg-out -r
hop svg -f integration-tests/tests/basic/load1.hpl -o /tmp/load1.svg
```

Options: `--no-notes`, `--magnification`, `--show-hash-keys` (`.hdv` only), `--project-home`.

### `hop edw-naming-check`

Validate `.hsm` / `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm` names against project Naming Schemes (Hop's `hop naming-check` covers pipelines, workflows, and metadata). See link:naming-schemes.adoc[EDW naming schemes].

```bash
hop edw-naming-check --project my-project
hop edw-naming-check --path /path/to/project --format json --require-scheme
```

### `hop project-doc`

Generate a self-contained HTML documentation set (search, zoomable SVG, dark/light) for the current project:

```bash
hop project-doc -e retail-example-docker-pg \
  -t ${PROJECT_HOME}/work/documentation
```

See [project-documentation.adoc](project-documentation.adoc).

## Internal design notes

See [plans/](plans/) — not part of the end-user documentation path.

Screenshots: [images/](images/)

docs.content:
= Operations
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

Day-to-day operation of Data Hopper EDW loads: environments, Docker runners, batch orchestration, and partial model updates.

How you *got* the models and the resource definition group is design-time — see link:architecture.adoc#d4-build-vs-run[Architecture — build vs run] and link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]. This page is the operate lane.

For **multi-team programs** (who owns core vs subject models, catalog contracts, git vs runtime, analyst discovery), see link:enterprise-modeling-and-team-collaboration.adoc[Organizing large Data Vault programs].

== Docker runners

From the repository root:

[source,bash]
----
# PostgreSQL on port 54320
./scripts/run-postgres.sh up

# Optional local Marquez (OpenLineage API :5001, UI :3001)
./scripts/run-marquez.sh up

# Run a workflow in a Hop container
./scripts/run-hop.sh retail-example workflows/run-retail-initial.hwf
./scripts/run-hop.sh integration-tests tests/run-tests.hwf
----

After Marquez is up, export model-derived lineage with `retail-example/workflows/send-lineage-to-marquez.hwf` and open a link:hop-lineage-view.adoc[Hop Lineage View] (`.hlv`). Optional smoke: `./scripts/smoke-lineage-view.sh` (not part of `mvn test` or the multi-database suite). `${MARQUEZ_API}` is the export POST URL; `${MARQUEZ_BASE_URL}` is the Marquez host root used by the lineage backend.

See link:../scripts/README.md[scripts/README.md] and link:../integration-tests/PROJECT.md[integration-tests/PROJECT.md] for multi-database CI runs.

== Batch orchestration pattern

Typical production workflow chain:

1. **Harvest source metadata** — discover live source schemas, persist drift history (OPS); does not load the EDW (see link:metadata-harvesting.adoc[Metadata harvesting])
2. **Validate resource definitions** — schema gate / policy on contracts (optional axes: live, version, target DDL)
3. **Measure / evaluate source quality** — content rules (optional)
4. **Update resource definition group** (or dedicated DV / BV / DM update actions) — load the warehouse
5. Optional **Measure target quality** with alert-only disposition

Configure on each action:

* Pipeline run configuration (connection, logging, variables)
* **Parallel pipeline copies** — throughput vs resource use
* DDL options — execute on database, export to file, or fail if DDL needed (CI gate)
* Optional **catalog publish** after DV/BV updates

Retail example: `retail-example/workflows/run-retail-initial.hwf` and `run-retail-update.hwf`.

== Partial loads (record source groups)

Tag `DV_SOURCE` definitions with a **group** (for example `hourly`, `daily`). On **Data Vault Update**, set **Record source group** to load only matching sources. Empty group means all sources participate.

See link:datavault-source.adoc[Data Vault Source] and link:datavault-update-action.adoc[Data Vault Update action].

== Metrics and regression

The integration-tests project collects Data Vault / Business Vault update metrics JSON and runs golden-dataset unit tests. Use it as a reference for CI gates (model check abort, fail-if-DDL-needed).

=== Workflow load overview

**Preferred:** use the **Update resource definition group** workflow action. It loads every DV/BV/DM model listed on a resource definition group (order: all DV, then BV, then DM; list order within each layer), and can **manage vault update metrics** internally (assigns `DV_WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_ID` at start and publishes a load overview at the end). No separate Begin/End actions or hand-wired per-model hops are required. While it runs, the canvas badge and **View load metrics** dialog show which model/table is current, stalls, and this-run plus OPS history (see link:performance-tuning.md[Performance tuning]).

image::images/update-resource-definition-group-action-dialog.png[Update resource definition group action dialog — group selection and layer includes,align="center"]

image::images/action-update-resource-group-load-metrics-dialog.png[Resource group load metrics — This run tab during a retail-sources update,align="center"]

Full option reference: link:update-resource-definition-group-action.adoc[Update resource definition group action].

Retail example (`run-retail-update.hwf` / `run-retail-update-models.hwf`):

[source,text]
----
Harvest source metadata (optional Phase 1 wiring)
  → Schema gate (Validate resource definitions)
  → Measure / Evaluate source quality
  → Update resource definition group (retail-sources)
  → Record the load in retail_load_log
----

Metadata harvest details: link:metadata-harvesting.adoc[Metadata harvesting].

**Advanced:** you can still bracket custom multi-action graphs with:

1. **Begin Vault Update** — assigns `DV_WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_ID` (and `DV_WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STARTED_AT`) before model updates run.
2. Per-model **Data Vault / Business Vault / Dimensional Update** actions (or a nested workflow).
3. **End Vault Update** — correlates all `load_run` rows with that execution id, publishes `workflow_load_overview` / `workflow_load_overview_model` to the OPS database, and optionally writes Markdown/HTML reports.

Schema gate details and HTML report samples: link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation].

Configure the group action (or End Vault Update) with the same execution metrics profile as the model updates (`retail-execution-metrics`). Retail report files default to `${PROJECT_HOME}/work/reports`.

Catalog record definitions for ops tables are published under the FILE catalog storage root (retail: `work/edw-catalog/hop/<project>/operations/`) — for example `workflow_load_overview`, `workflow_load_overview_model`.

The HTML report summarizes the wave (model count, pipeline count, total duration, rows inserted) and lists each DV/BV/DM model with per-model duration and row counts:

image::images/workflow-load-overview-summary-models.png[Workflow load overview report — summary and per-model table for run-retail-initial,align="center"]

Drill into a model to see pipeline-level read, insert, error, and duration metrics:

image::images/workflow-load-overview-model-metrics.png[Workflow load overview — per-pipeline metrics for dimensional models,align="center"]

=== Load duration overview on model graphs

When an execution metrics profile is configured and prior runs are stored in the OPS database, DV/BV/DM model canvases can show a **Load durations** pane alongside the graph. On the desktop each model table gets a horizontal bar per recent run (Airflow-style), with hover tooltips for run time and status. On Hop Web the same pane is a table (one row per table, one column per run). Toggle the pane from the modeler toolbar; use **View data** to open catalog-backed load metrics.

image::images/data-vault-retail-360-model-with-duration-metrics.png[Retail 360 Data Vault model with load duration bars on the right,align="center"]

See link:plans/load-run-metrics-plan.md[load-run metrics plan] for the metadata contract and catalog schema.

=== Load-run metrics tables (OPS)

Tables such as `load_run` and `load_pipeline_metric` live on the **OPS** connection (retail schema `dv_ops`), not in the Vault EDW.

A data engineer who needs the DDL should open metadata **Execution metrics profile**, set the target database and operations schema, and click **Generate SQL**. That opens Hop's SQL editor with dialect-specific `CREATE` statements (Postgres / MySQL / SQL Server / Snowflake). Review, copy for a DBA, or execute. Auto-create on first publish is optional; **Generate SQL** is the supported way to know which SQL to run. Retail's `sql/create-load-metrics-tables.sql` is only a Postgres bootstrap for the sample.

Help: link:help/execution-metrics-profile-dialog.adoc[Execution metrics profile].

== Performance

Sort memory, parallel pipeline/table copies, and large-model notes: link:performance-tuning.md[performance-tuning.md].

== Finding objects while operating

Day-to-day operators and modelers can use Hop **Search Everywhere** to jump to hubs, satellites, source queries, resource definition groups, or metrics profiles by name without walking the project tree. See link:search.adoc[Project and metadata search].

The **EDW Journey** perspective lists the same group's sources, controls, models, operate workflows, and reports in load order — see link:edw-journey.adoc[EDW Journey].

== Related documents

* link:update-resource-definition-group-action.adoc[Update resource definition group action]
* link:search.adoc[Project and metadata search]
* link:execution-maps.adoc[Execution maps]
* link:architecture.adoc[Architecture]
* link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]
* link:resource-definition-group.adoc[Resource definition group]
* link:getting-started-retail.adoc[Getting started — retail example]

:toc: macro

This guide is the **operating model** for Data Hopper EDW when many people share one vault: hundreds of tables, concurrent modelers, version control, a shared data catalog, and distinct roles from raw vault through reporting.
docs.content:
= Organizing large Data Vault programs
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

This guide is the **operating model** for Data Hopper EDW when many people share one vault: hundreds of tables, concurrent modelers, version control, a shared data catalog, and distinct roles from raw vault through reporting.

It does **not** replace the technical reference pages. It explains *how to organize work* and points at the feature docs for *how the product works*.

[cols="1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Need |Go here

|Cross-model linked tables and hub aliases (XML, canvas, load order)
|link:dv-cross-model-references.adoc[Linked tables and hub aliases]

|Catalog layout, namespaces, version tags
|link:data-catalog.adoc[Data Catalog]

|Schema gate, remediation, DTAP promotion
|link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation]

|Lineage discovery and drift
|link:source-to-target-lineage.adoc[Source-to-target lineage]

|Day-2 runners, partial loads, metrics
|link:operations.adoc[Operations]

|Architecture (catalog, RDG, four controls)
|link:architecture.adoc[Architecture]

|Build an EDW from scratch
|link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]

|Resource definition group
|link:resource-definition-group.adoc[Resource definition group]

|Tour the finished retail sample
|link:getting-started-retail.adoc[Getting started — retail]
|===

== Why split models

A single giant `.hdv` works for tutorials. It fails for programs:

* **Concurrent ownership** — two people cannot safely edit the same large XML canvas every day.
* **Reviewable change** — PRs should touch one subject area, not 400 tables of blast radius.
* **Independent load** — core hubs can run first; subject links/sats can lag or scale separately.
* **Clear authority** — business keys and hash definitions for a hub live in *one* owning model.
* **Cognitive load** — canvases stay readable; execution maps stay useful.

Data Hopper EDW supports this with **cross-model linked tables** (subject models point at core hubs without copying metadata), optional **hub aliases** for role-playing inside a model, multi-model **Business Vault** and **dimensional** references, and a **catalog** that publishes contracts for everyone else.

== Personas and responsibilities

Roles often overlap in small teams; at scale, keep **accountable owners** even if one person wears several hats.

[cols="1,2,2,2", options="header"]
|===
|Persona |Primary artifacts |Catalog |Typical Hop surfaces

|**DV platform / admin**
|Shared-core `.hdv`, **Data Vault configuration** metadata (hashing, naming, target database), resource definition groups, CI gates
|Owns source-contract process and catalog **version tags**; sets conventions for namespaces
|Model check standards, Validate resource definitions action, core Data Vault Update

|**DV modeler (subject)**
|Subject-area `.hdv` files, local links/sats, references to core
|Reads `DV_SOURCE` feeds; proposes source changes via steward (does not casually rewrite shared contracts)
|Data Vault canvas, Check model, subject Data Vault Update

|**Source steward / integration**
|Source system knowledge; may own ingest pipelines outside the vault
|Creates and maintains working-tree **`DV_SOURCE`** definitions; participates in validation and tagging
|Data Catalog perspective, Validate sources

|**Daily operations**
|Workflows, run configurations, load-control, environment variables
|Consumes published model targets and ops tables; rarely edits source contracts
|Begin/End Vault Update, metrics profiles, partial loads by record source group

|**Business Vault modeler**
|`.hbv` models (SCD2, PIT, bridges, SQL business tables)
|Publishes BV target definitions on BV Update
|BV canvas (DV aliases / multi-model refs), Business Vault Update

|**Dimensional modeler**
|`.hdm` models (facts, dims, conformed aliases)
|Publishes DM target definitions on DM Update
|Dimensional canvas, Dimensional Update / Publish

|**Data quality owner**
|Rule sets, bindings on sources and targets
|Quality rules on catalog records; ops quality tables when used
|Measure Data Quality, Evaluate quality gate

|**Analyst / reporter**
|(read-only consumers)
|Catalog tree, lineage siblings, optional external lineage (Marquez)
|Data Catalog browse, reverse lineage browser; usually **not** the modeler canvas
|===

=== Handoffs that matter

* **Source contract** (field names, lengths, types) is agreed in the catalog, not reinvented per model.
* **Raw grain** (hubs, links, sats) is owned by DV modelers; BV/DM people consume published structures and lineage.
* **Load order** is an ops + platform concern: core before subjects, DV before BV before DM.
* **Schema change** is DEV approval → tag → git promote → gate in TEST/ACC/PROD (see the DTAP recipe in link:resource-definition-validation.adoc#dtap-promotion-recipe[Resource definition validation]).

== Reference architecture: multi-file projects

=== Suggested folder layout

Adapt names to your org; keep the **idea** of separation:

[source]
----
my-vault-project/
├── models/
│   ├── core/                 # shared hubs (and optional shared links)
│   │   └── shared-core.hdv
│   ├── sales/                # subject: local links/sats + references to core
│   │   └── sales.hdv
│   ├── inventory/
│   │   └── inventory.hdv
│   ├── business/             # BV models (may ref multiple .hdv)
│   │   └── customer-360.hbv
│   └── marts/                # dimensional models
│       └── orders.hdm
├── workflows/
│   ├── load-core-dv.hwf
│   ├── load-sales-dv.hwf
│   ├── load-bv.hwf
│   └── load-marts.hwf
├── metadata/                 # Hop connections, run configs, resource groups (no secrets)
├── work/                     # gitignored runtime: catalog, metrics, reports, maps
│   └── edw-catalog/
└── project-config.json
----

Retail-example collapses many of these into fewer files for teaching. Integration-tests demonstrate **shared-core + subject** DV files (`shared-dv-core.hdv`, `cross-model-dv-subject.hdv`).

=== Shared core vs subject areas

[cols="1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Layer |Contents

|**Shared core** `.hdv`
|Enterprise hubs (customer, product, party, calendar keys, …), optional shared links, standard hash/config. **Authoritative** business keys and hub hash names live here.

|**Subject area** `.hdv`
|Links and satellites for that domain; **linked tables** to core hubs (and links if needed). Local hubs only when the concept is truly local.

|**Business Vault** `.hbv`
|SCD2 / PIT / bridge / SQL business objects. References DV tables via canvas aliases (possibly multi-model). May itself be split by domain.

|**Dimensional** `.hdm`
|Marts; conformed dimensions and role-playing dimension aliases. Often owned by a different team than raw DV.
|===

=== Load order

Always:

1. **Core Data Vault Update** — materialize shared hubs (and shared entities).
2. **Subject Data Vault Update(s)** — local links/sats; references do **not** reload core tables.
3. **Business Vault Update** — depends on raw vault tables existing.
4. **Dimensional Update** — depends on BV and/or raw vault as designed.

Partial loads: tag `DV_SOURCE` definitions with a **group** and pass **Record source group** on Data Vault Update (hourly vs daily feeds). See link:operations.adoc[Operations] and link:datavault-update-action.adoc[Data Vault Update action].

=== Two different “alias” ideas

Do not confuse them:

* **Cross-model linked table** — another `.hdv` owns the table; this file only points at it (collaboration / split files).
* **Same-model hub alias** — extra *role* of a hub already in this file (e.g. secondary sales rep). Prefer **natural hub + alias** so the physical hub stays connected on the canvas. See link:dv-cross-model-references.adoc[Linked tables and hub aliases].

== Version control playbook

=== What belongs in git

Commit:

* Model files: `.hdv`, `.hbv`, `.hdm`, `.hem` *definitions you author*
* Workflows and pipelines you maintain (including schema-remediation packages you choose to keep)
* Hop **metadata** that is not secret (resource definition groups, metrics profiles, catalog *connection* pointing at a path)
* Optional **seeded** catalog fixtures for CI (as integration-tests does) — not every developer’s full runtime dump

Keep **out** of git (or gitignore aggressively):

* Runtime FILE catalog working tree (`work/edw-catalog/` style)
* Catalog version snapshots generated per machine (unless you deliberately seed a baseline tag)
* Metrics JSON, load reports, generated bulk staging, execution-map *outputs* under `work/`

Connections and passwords: store **connection metadata templates** or variable-driven profiles; never commit production secrets.

=== Concurrent work without merge pain

XML model files merge poorly. Practical rules:

* **One subject file, one primary owner** (or one PR stream) at a time.
* Prefer **short-lived branches** per subject change; avoid multi-day edits to `shared-core.hdv` by everyone.
* **Shared-core changes** are rare and platform-reviewed: new enterprise hub, BK change, hash algorithm, standard column renames. Subjects then refresh references and re-check models.
* Do not copy hub BK lists into subjects “for convenience” — use a **reference** so core remains authority.
* When two subjects need the same new hub, add it to **core** first, then both subjects reference it.

=== Pull request checklist (model change)

* [ ] **Check model** clean on every touched `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm`
* [ ] Cross-model references resolve (no chains, no broken paths)
* [ ] Hash algorithm / hash key type / target database still align with core (warnings matter)
* [ ] Schema gate / impact reviewed if sources or lengths changed
* [ ] Load order documented or workflow hops updated (core before subject)
* [ ] No accidental switch of managed tables to EXTERNAL_READ / custom without ops agreement
* [ ] Catalog publish behavior understood (who regenerates targets in each environment)

== Data catalog as the team contract

The catalog is how **integration, modeling, ops, and analysts** share one vocabulary.

[cols="1,2,1", options="header"]
|===
|Namespace idea |Role |Who edits

|`hop/{project}/sources`
|`DV_SOURCE` feeds — logical contracts for loads
|Source stewards (+ platform review)

|`hop/{project}/models/...`
|Published DV table layouts after Data Vault Update
|System (publish); humans read

|`hop/{project}/business-vault/...`, `dimensional/...`
|Published BV/DM targets
|System (publish); humans read

|`hop/{project}/lineage/...`
|Derived source-to-target lineage siblings
|System; analysts use reverse browser

|`hop/{project}/operations/...`
|Load metrics, quality history stubs
|Ops / platform
|===

=== Working tree vs version tags

* **Working tree** — live contracts developers edit (often under a gitignored `work/` path on each machine or environment).
* **Catalog version tag** — immutable snapshot (for example `v2.4.0`) for “what we promoted.”
* **CI / daily gate** — Validate resource definitions against live sources and/or a promoted tag before vault loads.

Full detail: link:data-catalog.adoc#catalog-versions[Data Catalog — Catalog versions] and link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation].

=== Who may change what

* Changing a **source field length** is a **contract** change: steward updates catalog → validate impact → expand models/DDL from catalog (catalog is not silently rewritten by length remediation) → tag when agreed.
* Changing a **satellite attribute mapping** is a **subject model** change: DV modeler PR; lineage and impact explain downstream BV/DM.
* **Republishing** targets after a successful load is normal ops; it should preserve quality bindings (publish logic is designed for that).

== Day-2 operations at scale

Platform and ops typically own:

* Environment-specific run configurations and variables (`${DB_HOST}`, promoted tag, parallel copies)
* Orchestration graphs: core workflow → subject workflows → BV → DM (can be one master workflow with sub-workflows)
* **Fail if DDL is needed** on non-DEV environments so structure drift never silently applies
* **Begin / End Vault Update** for wave-level metrics and reports
* Record source **groups** for partial refresh windows
* Optional **execution maps** (`.hem`) per major workflow for “what ran”

See link:operations.adoc[Operations], link:execution-maps.adoc[Execution maps], and link:performance-tuning.md[Performance tuning].

Integration-tests is the **CI reference** (multi-database, golden datasets, schema gates). Retail-example is the **teaching** full stack, not a multi-team ownership template.

== How non-modelers learn the model

Not everyone should open a 200-table canvas.

[cols="1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Audience need |Prefer

|What columns exist on a vault table?
|Published catalog record for that table (after model publish)

|Where did this field come from?
|Lineage tab / reverse lineage browser / lineage siblings in catalog — link:source-to-target-lineage.adoc[Source-to-target lineage]

|What jobs touch this table?
|Execution map for the batch; optional OpenLineage/Marquez — link:openlineage-export.adoc[OpenLineage export]

|Is today’s source still compatible?
|Schema validation report from the gate (HTML/Markdown under `work/reports` or CI artifacts)

|Pretty architecture picture for a wiki?
|`hop svg` export of a subject `.hdv` / `.hbv` (see docs README); or link:architecture-export.adoc[Architecture export] to Draw.io for multi-file / workflow-driven views
|===

Reporting users usually connect BI tools to **BV or dimensional** schemas, not raw hubs/links. DV modelers still need raw models for history and audit; do not force analysts through raw vault unless that is an explicit architecture choice.

== Anti-patterns

* **One mega-model** everyone merges into daily.
* **Duplicating hub metadata** in every subject instead of a reference (diverging hash keys and BKs).
* **Loading subjects before core** so link loads invent hubs inconsistently.
* **Two hub aliases + orphan physical hub** when a natural hub + one alias would keep the canvas honest.
* **Committing local catalog dumps** as the only “truth” without version tags or DTAP discipline.
* **Editing production connections into shared git** models.
* **Silent structure changes in PROD** (DDL auto-apply without fail-if-DDL / review).
* **BV/DM teams editing raw DV mappings** without DV ownership — use lineage and requests instead.

== Worked sketch: people, files, systems

image::images/diagrams/enterprise-people-files-systems.svg[People, git models, catalog, and databases in a large Data Vault program,align="center"]

PlantUML source: link:diagrams/enterprise-people-files-systems.puml[enterprise-people-files-systems.puml].

== Where to go next

* **Mechanism — split DV files:** link:dv-cross-model-references.adoc[Linked tables and hub aliases]
* **Mechanism — catalog and tags:** link:data-catalog.adoc[Data Catalog]
* **Process — schema change and DTAP:** link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation]
* **Discovery — lineage:** link:source-to-target-lineage.adoc[Source-to-target lineage]
* **Run — ops:** link:operations.adoc[Operations]

docs.content:
# Memory and performance tuning

Practical notes for tuning Data Vault update loads. Settings live in two places:

- **Model** (`.hdv` → Target loading tab): batch size, Table Output copies, Sort Rows in-memory buffer
- **Workflow** (Data Vault Update action): parallel pipeline copies, JVM heap on the run configuration

There is a **third** kind of parallelism for the **schema gate** (not loads): concurrent live-source discovery and target-table DDL checks. See [Schema gate validation parallelism](#schema-gate-validation-parallelism) below.

---

## Two kinds of load parallelism

Generated update pipelines use parallelism at two independent levels. They stack: total resource use is roughly the product of both when loads run concurrently.

### 1. Parallel pipeline copies (orchestrator)

**Setting:** `parallelPipelineCopies` on the **Data Vault Update** workflow action (default `1`).

The action stages all generated `.hpl` files and runs them through a Get File Names → Pipeline Executor orchestrator. Each copy runs a different pipeline in parallel (round-robin over the staged files).

| Use case | Guidance |
|----------|----------|
| Many small hubs/links/sats | Increase copies (e.g. 2–4) to load several tables at once |
| One large satellite | Keep at `1` — a single heavy pipeline already saturates CPU and memory |
| Mixed model | Start low; raise copies only if individual pipelines are small and JVM headroom remains |

This does **not** split one satellite load across threads. It only runs **different** pipelines side by side.

### 2. Target table parallel copies (Table Output)

**Setting:** `targetTableParallelCopies` on the model **Target loading** tab (default `1`).

Applied to the generated **Table Output** transform as Hop transform copies. Rows are distributed round-robin across copies — there is **no hash-key affinity**, so merge/sort work upstream is still single-threaded per copy until rows reach Table Output.

| Observed effect | Notes |
|-----------------|-------|
| Faster Postgres inserts | Multiple concurrent `COPY`/batch writers (e.g. 4 copies ≈ 4 parallel DB connections) |
| Modest overall speedup | Merge Rows and Sort Rows still run on one copy each; DB write is only part of total time |
| More DB connections | Ensure Postgres `max_connections` and pool limits accommodate copies × concurrent pipelines |

Example from the large synthetic model (`integration-tests/files/large/syn-large.hdv`): `targetTableParallelCopies=4`.

**Scale-out preference:** prefer more concurrent **table pipelines** (`parallelPipelineCopies` / model orchestrator) over deeper single-pipeline partitioning. Hash-key ModPartitioner swimlanes were evaluated and **abandoned** — see [plans/hash-key-partitioning-plan.md](plans/hash-key-partitioning-plan.md).

---

## Schema gate validation parallelism

**Setting:** `validationParallelism` / **Parallel checks** on:

- Design-time **Validate sources** options dialog (resource definition group)
- Workflow action **Validate resource definitions (schema gate)**

Default **`8`** (clamped 1–64). Use **`1`** for serial debugging.

Live source validation opens a JDBC connection per catalog source to rediscover fields. Over a VPN, that latency dominates wall-clock time when hundreds or thousands of sources run **one after another**. Bounded parallel fan-out overlaps those waits. The same knob applies to **Check target databases** (per-satellite DDL readiness).

| Use case | Guidance |
|----------|----------|
| ~1000 database sources over VPN | Start at 8; try 12–16 if the source DB and gateway accept more sessions |
| Fragile source / low `max_connections` | Lower to 2–4 or 1 |
| Offline catalog-version only compare | Parallelism still helps lightly (catalog I/O); leave default |

This is **not** the same as `parallelPipelineCopies` on update actions. Validation does not load data.

See [resource-definition-validation.adoc](resource-definition-validation.adoc).

---

## Sort Rows in-memory buffer

**Setting:** `sortRowsSize` on the model **Target loading** tab (label: *Sort rows in memory*, default `1000000`).

Link and satellite update pipelines sort by hash key before **Merge Rows**. This value is the number of rows Sort Rows holds in memory before spilling to disk (Hop `SortRowsMeta.sortSize`).

### Trade-off

| More in-memory rows | Fewer in-memory rows |
|---------------------|----------------------|
| Less temp-disk I/O | More external sort I/O |
| Higher CPU use (sort/merge in RAM) | Lower CPU, more disk wait |
| Higher JVM heap per pipeline | Lower memory footprint |

### Observed results (25M-row `sat_syn_order` initial load)

On an 8-core host with **16 GB JVM heap** allocated:

- Increased in-memory sort buffer → **~6 GB heap used**, CPU spread across all 8 cores
- External sort I/O dropped sharply
- **Initial load time cut roughly in half** vs default spill-heavy sort

The large test model uses `sortRowsSize=30000000` alongside `targetTableParallelCopies=4`.

### Tuning guidance

1. **Size for the largest sort in the run** — usually the biggest satellite. Aim to hold most or all of that stream in memory if heap allows.
2. **Leave headroom** — reserve memory for merge buffers, target Table Input, JDBC drivers, and Postgres client buffers. If heap is 16 GB, ~6 GB for sort on one large pipeline is a reasonable ceiling; going higher only helps if the row set still spills.
3. **Per-pipeline, not global** — each running pipeline has its own Sort Rows. `parallelPipelineCopies=3` with three heavy satellites can need **3×** the sort memory.
4. **Row width matters** — wide attribute sets use more bytes per row than the row count alone suggests.
5. **Diminishing returns** — once the sort stays in memory, the bottleneck often moves to target read (Table Input + Group By), Merge Rows, or database write. Tune `targetTableParallelCopies` and batch size next.

---

## Target table batch size

**Setting:** `targetTableBatchSize` on the model **Target loading** tab (default `1000`).

Commit size for Table Output. For **Native bulk loader** mode on MySQL/SingleStore, this value is also passed as the bulk loader batch size. Larger batches reduce commit overhead; very large batches increase memory per output copy and time between commits. For bulk initial loads, values in the thousands are typical; increase gradually if the database tolerates it.

---

## Native bulk loading

**Setting:** `targetLoadMode` on the model **Target loading** tab (default **Table Output**).

When set to **Native bulk loader** and the matching Hop database plugin is installed, generated hub/link/satellite insert pipelines end in a bulk loader transform instead of Table Output:

| Target database | Hop transform | Mechanism |
|-----------------|---------------|-----------|
| MySQL, SingleStore | MySQL bulk loader | `LOAD DATA` via named pipe |
| PostgreSQL | PostgreSQL bulk loader | `COPY FROM STDIN` (streaming) |
| Oracle | Oracle bulk loader | `sqlldr` direct-path stream |
| Snowflake | Snowflake bulk loader | Internal stage + `COPY INTO` |
| MonetDB | MonetDB bulk loader | Column-store bulk insert |
| Vertica | Vertica bulk loader | Direct `COPY` stream |
| Doris | Doris bulk loader | Stream Load HTTP API |

Notes:

- Only the **insert leg** uses bulk loading. Satellite load-end-date **Update** transforms are unchanged.
- Native bulk loaders run as a **single transform copy** (`targetTableParallelCopies` is ignored for this mode). Use **Staging file** mode when you need parallel shard files.
- Delimiter, enclosure, and encoding on the Target loading tab feed the bulk loader field format (defaults: comma, double quote, UTF-8).
- Install the matching `hop-databases-*` and bulk-loader transform plugins in the Hop runtime.

---

## Staging file + bulk command

**Setting:** `targetLoadMode` = **Staging file + bulk command**.

Generated insert pipelines end in **Text File Output** with `targetTableParallelCopies` parallel copies. Each copy writes `${bulkLoadStagingFolder}/${pipelineName}-${Internal.Transform.CopyNr}.csv`. A master workflow then runs each staged pipeline and bulk-loads every shard file.

| Target database | Workflow action | Notes |
|-----------------|-----------------|-------|
| MySQL, SingleStore | MySQL bulk load | `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE` from staged CSV |
| Microsoft SQL Server | MSSQL bulk load | `BULK INSERT` from staged CSV (UTF-8, header skipped) |
| PostgreSQL | Pipeline (CSV input → PGBulkLoader) | Client-side `COPY FROM STDIN` from staged CSV |

Operational notes:

- Set **Bulk load staging folder** to a path writable by Hop. PostgreSQL loads from the Hop client via PGBulkLoader; MySQL/SingleStore use `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE`.
- **Bulk load requires local file** (default on) documents that Hop and the DB client must access the CSV on the filesystem.
- Cleanup of pipeline staging (`.hpl`) and bulk CSV folders runs in a `finally` block after the master workflow finishes.

---

## Bulk modes and parallel copies

**Native bulk loader** is a single writer: `targetTableParallelCopies` > 1 is ignored (model check warns). **Staging-file** mode uses parallel Text File Output copies for shard fan-out when copies > 1, not Hop ModPartitioner swimlanes.

---

## Suggested starting points

| Scenario | `parallelPipelineCopies` | `targetTableParallelCopies` | `sortRowsSize` |
|----------|--------------------------|-----------------------------|----------------|
| Dev / small feeds | 1 | 1 | default (`1000000`) |
| Production, many small tables | 2–4 | 1–2 | default |
| Large satellite initial load (10M+ rows) | 1 | 2–4 | Raise until sort stays in memory (monitor heap) |
| syn-large style (25M+ rows, 16 GB heap) | 1 | 4 | ~25M–30M rows if width is moderate |

Always align JVM `-Xmx` with these choices. Watch Hop logging and OS metrics (CPU, disk, heap) when changing more than one knob at a time.

---

## Monitoring a running update (Hop GUI)

While a Data Vault Update workflow is running, you can drill into live pipeline execution without waiting for the workflow to finish.

### Live stall badge on the workflow action

When a **Data Vault / Business Vault / Dimensional Update** action is executing, Hop paints a small status icon at the **bottom-right** of the action:

| Icon | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| Clock | Update running normally |
| Warning | No transform progress for about a minute (possible slow query, sort, or backpressure) |
| Failure | Errors detected in an active child pipeline |

Hover the icon for a short tooltip such as *Updating table d_customer of model retail-360*. Click it to open the **Live model update** dialog with per-pipeline transform metrics (rows in/out, buffer sizes, stall seconds) and a **Copy diagnostics** button for issue reports.

The **Update resource definition group** action uses the same corner. While the wave is running, the tooltip includes the current model and progress (`model 2/5`). Click (or context menu **View load metrics**) opens **Resource group load metrics**: **This run** lists every model in the wave with elapsed time and live transform metrics; **History** lists recent OPS workflow load overviews. When the action is idle, a metrics glyph stays on the icon so you can still open history without a live run.

![Resource group load metrics — This run tab during a retail-sources update](images/action-update-resource-group-load-metrics-dialog.png)

The action log also prints the **resolved staging folder** at orchestrator start (default `${java.io.tmpdir}/dv2/<model-name>/`, not necessarily `/tmp`) and repeats stall warnings about once per minute while a pipeline is quiet.

Live badges are sampled in the Hop GUI JVM. A remote workflow engine will not paint live stalls; History still works when the execution metrics profile published to OPS.

### Open execution from the workflow action

1. In the workflow execution view, click the running **Data Vault Update** action.
2. Choose **Open execution** from the context menu.

![Open execution on a running Data Vault Update action](images/open-execution-of-data-vault-update-action.png)

This opens the **DV Update Orchestrator** pipeline (`Get pipeline files` → **Execute update pipelines**). You can see which staged update pipelines are being picked up and how many executor copies are active (`parallelPipelineCopies`).

### Open execution from the orchestrator

From that orchestrator pipeline, click the running **Execute update pipelines** transform and choose **Open execution** again. That opens the **currently running** generated update pipeline (e.g. a single hub, link, or satellite load) so you can inspect transform metrics, row rates, and where time is spent (Sort Rows, Merge Rows, Table Output, and so on).

Use this when tuning `sortRowsSize` or `targetTableParallelCopies` — it shows whether sort is still spilling, whether multiple Table Output copies are busy, and which transform is the bottleneck.

### AI-assisted tuning

On DV/DM/BV models, open **AI Help**, choose the **Performance tuning** scenario, and enable **Include load-run metrics and insights**. The advisor correlates recent OPS metrics with model settings and can propose `SET_CONFIGURATION_PROPERTY` changes (for example raising `targetTableParallelCopies`) for review before apply. See [ai-advisory.md](ai-advisory.md#example-performance-tuning-on-a-dimensional-model).

### Execution information location

For richer history and metrics beyond the live GUI view, configure an **Execution Information Location** on the **Pipeline run configuration** selected in the Data Vault Update action (`Pipeline run configuration` field). Hop will persist execution data (status, timing, logging) to that location for orchestrator runs and the pipelines they launch. Point it at a folder or metadata store you use for operational analysis.

---

## Related docs

- [datavault-configuration.adoc](datavault-configuration.adoc) — full configuration reference
