docs.content:
= Data Vault Satellite
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

A Satellite stores the descriptive, time-varying attributes that belong to a Hub or a Link. Classic examples are customer name and address details, product descriptions and categories, order status history, etc.

In Data Vault 2.0, satellites are insert-only. When any of the tracked attributes changes for a given parent (hub or link), a new row is inserted with the new values and the current load date. Old rows are kept, giving you a complete history.

== How satellite updates work

When data is loaded for a satellite, the generated pipeline:

* Reads the parent business keys from *this satellite's* record source (so it can compute the parent hash key), plus the satellite attributes and the record source indicator.
* Calculates the parent hash key using the same logical business keys defined on the parent hub.
* Does **not** require the satellite feed to be listed as a hub record source. Hub and satellite loads are independent (Data Vault 2.0): only the parent identity columns must be present on the satellite feed (by default with the same names as the hub business keys).
* Compares the incoming data against the existing rows in the satellite table.
* Detects real changes by comparing the actual attribute values (not just the presence of the parent key).
* Inserts only the rows that are new for that parent key or that contain different attribute values.
* Adds the batch load date to every inserted row.

Because the comparison looks at the attribute values themselves, you do not get duplicate "no-change" rows in the satellite. This keeps history clean and query performance good.

== Options in the Satellite dialog

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Name
|The name of this satellite definition. Used as the default physical table name if you do not specify one.

|Physical table name
|The actual table name in the target Data Vault database. Leave blank to use the Name.

|Description
|Business description of the satellite and the kind of information it holds.

|Default record source
|The Data Vault Source that feeds this satellite. Required.

|Store record source indicator
|When checked (default), the satellite table includes the model record-source column and load pipelines write the feed's source indicator into it. Uncheck for **VaultSpeed-style** mono-source satellites that omit the source-indicator column from the physical table. The catalog feed binding is still required. Hubs and links always store record source.

|Parent hub
|Select the Hub this satellite describes (for normal hub satellites). Choose either a parent hub or a parent link, not both.

|Parent link
|Select the Link this satellite describes (for satellites that hold relationship-level attributes). Choose either a parent link or a parent hub, not both.

|Parent key source fields (tab)
|For **hub satellites** only: optional ordered list of columns on *this satellite's* record source that supply the parent hub **hash inputs**. Length and order match the hub's multipartite vault keys *or*, for composite hub business keys, the ordered source *parts* (not the composed vault BK column name). Leave empty to default from the hub (vault key names, or hub-mapped parts for the satellite record source when known). This is not a re-definition of hub keys — only where the values sit on this one feed. The satellite table does **not** store hub business-key text. Link satellites configure parent keys on the link's source mappings instead. Use **Load from hub mapping** to fill defaults.

|Attributes
|The list of descriptive columns whose changes you want to track.

Each attribute has:
* Column name (in both source and target).
* Optional description.
* Data type, length, and precision (used for DDL and loading).
* "Include in CDC" – normally left checked. Uncheck it for columns that should not trigger a new satellite row when they change (for example audit columns or fields added later that you do not want to version).

The **Load from source** button on the Attributes tab is very useful. It populates the list from the referenced source, automatically excluding primary key fields and any driving key. You can then delete columns you do not want to historize or adjust lengths and the "Include in CDC" flag.

If you leave the attributes list empty, the plugin will include all non-key, non-driving-key fields from the source. The model check will warn you about this so you can decide whether it is intentional.

|Multi-active satellite
|Check this box when more than one active record can exist for the same parent key at the same moment in time. A common example is multiple current phone numbers or email addresses for a customer.

|Driving key
|Required when Multi-active is checked. This is the additional column that, together with the parent hash key and load date, makes each row unique (for example the phone number type or the email address itself).

|Driving key source field
|Source column that supplies the driving key value. Renamed to the driving key column in the update pipeline and stored in the target satellite table.

|Integration mode (Options tab)
|Controls how Hop loads this satellite. **Hop managed** (default) generates DDL and update pipelines. **External read-only** skips generation — use when dbt or another tool loads the table; Business Vault still reads history from metadata. **Custom pipelines** runs your own `.hpl` paths. See link:dv-integration-modes.adoc[Data Vault integration modes].
|===

== Checks that involve satellites

The **Check model** button will report problems such as:

* The satellite is not attached to any hub or link.
* No attributes are defined (and therefore all non-key fields from the source will be used).
* One or more attributes have no name.
* The referenced parent hub or link does not exist in the model.
* **Source-to-target type mismatches** for explicit attributes, auto-attributes (when the attribute list is empty), and the driving key when multi-active mode is enabled.

Type validation compares each mapped source column to the satellite target column definition. Errors are raised for incompatible types or when the source is wider than the target. Warnings cover stored-metadata drift from the live source schema.

On **SQL Server**, vault string columns are created as `VARCHAR` with a UTF-8 collation so Unicode attributes store correctly without `NVARCHAR`. **Model lengths stay character-oriented** (e.g. attribute length 50). Generated vault DDL multiplies those lengths by three (`VARCHAR(150)`) because SQL Server measures UTF-8 `VARCHAR(n)` in **bytes**. Model check uses the same capacity rule (`effectiveStringCapacity`), so a source that reports 50 characters (typical `NVARCHAR(50)`) or a physical width that still fits in 150 bytes does not fail against model length 50. Catalog/CRM staging CREATE does **not** apply the vault ×3 expansion (character lengths stay as modeled). Detailed type checking still warns when source `NVARCHAR` maps to target `VARCHAR` because sort order can differ. ORDER BY risks on string keys are mitigated automatically by applying the same bridge `COLLATE` (preferring the **source** collation) on target and hub source SQL `ORDER BY` when live collations/types differ.

Satellite update pipelines Sort Rows the **source** stream after the parent hash is calculated in Hop (the merge key is not present in source SQL). The **target** leg is ordered only by SQL `ORDER BY` (no second Sort Rows).

These checks help you avoid generating pipelines that would fail or produce unexpected results.

== Target table layout for satellites

The layout that drives DDL and loading usually contains:

1. The parent hash key column (the hash key name is taken from the parent hub definition).
2. The satellite attribute columns, in the order you listed them (or all qualifying source columns if the list is empty). Length and precision information from the source definition is used when available so you get realistic column types.
3. The record source column (**only when Store record source indicator is enabled**).
4. The load date column.

The same attribute list that is used for change detection is also used for the target table and the final load, so what you see in the dialog is what ends up in the database.

When **Store record source indicator** is off, the feed does not need a static or column-based source indicator for this satellite alone. If the same catalog source also feeds a hub or link, that consumer still requires an indicator.

== Tips for satellites

* Use **Load from source** and then review the list. Remove columns that are not interesting for history (for example large free-text fields or technical IDs that never change).
* The "Include in CDC" flag is powerful. Use it to ignore columns that would otherwise cause unnecessary new rows (last-updated timestamps from the source, for example).
* For multi-active satellites, be clear about what the driving key represents. It becomes part of the uniqueness rule for the satellite.
* Attach satellites to links when the descriptive information truly belongs to the relationship rather than to one of the participating hubs.
* When the parent hub is fed by multiple record sources, it is common and recommended to create a separate satellite definition for each source (even if they track the same attributes). This keeps the incoming data, record source values, and change history cleanly separated per origin system while still describing the same parent hub.

If this satellite feed can introduce a parent business key that is not yet in the hub, use **Also load parent hub...** on the satellite dialog or an orphan policy other than `PASS`. See link:datavault-configuration.adoc#_orphan_handling_tab[Orphan handling].

== Satellites on multi-source hubs

If your hub definition lists several record sources, you will normally also create multiple satellites (one per source) that all point to the same parent hub. Each satellite only needs to reference the Data Vault Source that is relevant to it. This pattern gives you clean per-source history while keeping the hub itself as a single unified business key table.

You can also attach a satellite to a feed that is **not** used to load the hub (for example a multi-table source query that joins hub keys with descriptive attributes). The hub still loads from its own sources; the satellite only needs the parent business key columns on its feed so the same parent hash key can be computed.

== Parent business keys on the satellite feed

* The hub defines vault business keys and, for composite keys, ordered source parts. The parent hash uses the same delimiter / suffix / casing rules as hub loads (from the model configuration).
* **Multipartite hub keys:** by default the satellite feed exposes columns with those vault names (for example `customer_id`). If names differ, list source columns on the **Parent key source fields** tab in hub key order (for example `cust_no` for hub key `customer_id`).
* **Composite hub keys** (single vault column on the hub): list **N source part columns** in hub part order (for example `num_seq_bkcc_bk`, `num_seq_bk`). Do **not** require a composed `burger_bk` column on the satellite feed. Leave the list empty to default from the hub mapping when the sat record source is also a hub source (or when the hub definition carries default part names).
* Do **not** put satellite-only source column names on the hub Keys tab — that tab is only for sources that **load the hub**.
* Independent satellite feeds (multi-table composite queries, other models that only reference the hub) are expected; the sat feed need not be a hub record source.
* See link:dv-hub.adoc#composite-hub-business-keys[Composite hub business keys] for storage vs hash rules.

docs.summary:
= Metadata harvesting
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

**Metadata harvesting** is a first-class **operational** step that discovers **live source schemas**, compares them to the catalog (or a catalog version tag), and **persists** snapshots and drift history — without loading the EDW and without
docs.content:
= Metadata harvesting
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

**Metadata harvesting** is a first-class **operational** step that discovers **live source schemas**, compares them to the catalog (or a catalog version tag), and **persists** snapshots and drift history — without loading the EDW and without rewriting the working catalog.

Harvest is **not** a greenfield first step. It needs a link:resource-definition-group.adoc[resource definition group] whose models already reference catalog sources. To *start* a warehouse, publish from a source model first — link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]. **Generate .hsm from harvest…** is a day-2 discovery path after you have already loaded (or at least modeled) those sources.

This is separate from:

* link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation] (schema **gate** / policy)
* link:data-quality.adoc[Data quality measure] (row **content** rules)
* link:data-catalog.adoc#catalog-versions[Catalog versions] (design-time **frozen contracts**)
* DV/BV/DM **update** actions (load)

[Issue #112](https://github.com/ProjectDataHopper/hopper-edw/issues/112) motivates treating “what do the sources look like now?” as its own wave in an EDW update.

== Why a separate step?



|===
| Concern | Without harvest | With harvest
| When is live metadata read? | Inside validate / model check / load | Explicit **Harvest source metadata** action
| History over time? | Ephemeral reports only | OPS tables (`schema_harvest_*`)
| Efficiency at scale | One discovery per record definition | **Connection-batched** discovery (one JDBC session per source database)
| Detect drift without models? | Tied to validation axes | Harvest alone is enough to record and review drift
| Catalog rewritten? | Only via explicit refresh/remediation | **Never** by harvest
|===

== Recommended EDW update chain

[source]
----
Harvest source metadata          ← observation (this page)
  → Validate resource definitions  (schema gate / policy)
  → Measure / Evaluate source quality
  → Update resource definition group
  → (optional) Measure target quality ALERT_ONLY
----

Harvest **observes**. The schema gate **decides** whether drift should fail the workflow. Quality measures **content**. Update **loads**.

[[harvest-action-dialog]]
== Workflow action: Harvest source metadata

Category **General**. Plugin id `HARVEST_SOURCE_METADATA`.

=== Selection and baseline

|===
| Option | Description
| Resource definition group | Required. All catalog sources referenced by the group's DV/BV/DM models are harvested.
| Data catalog connection | Optional override; empty uses group/model defaults.
| Expected baseline | `WORKING_CATALOG` (default) or `CATALOG_VERSION`.
| Baseline catalog version | Tag when baseline is a version.
| Record source group filter | Optional `DV_SOURCE` group tag (e.g. `hourly`).
| Source database filter | Optional Hop connection name; only DATABASE feeds on that connection.
|===

=== History (OPS)

|===
| Option | Description
| Persist harvest history | Default on. Writes durable rows.
| History database | Default: configured name, else `SCHEMA_HARVEST_DATABASE`, else `OPS` if present.
| History schema | Empty = connection default database.
| Auto-create history tables | Creates `schema_harvest_*` when missing.
| Publish catalog definitions | Upserts operations record definitions under `hop/{project}/operations/`.
| Fail on persist error | Default on.
| Fail on discovery errors | Default **off**. Schema **drift never fails** this action.
|===

=== Reports

Optional Markdown report path (Hop VFS folder or `.md` file). The action also sets:

* Variable **`DV_SCHEMA_HARVEST_RUN_ID`** for downstream steps
* Extension data key `schemaHarvestReportText`

== What is stored

|===
| Table | Content
| `schema_harvest_run` | Run id, timestamps, group, baseline, status, counts, workflow execution id
| `schema_harvest_subject` | Per record definition: connection/schema/table, discovery status, in_sync, message
| `schema_harvest_field` | EXPECTED and DISCOVERED field snapshots (name, Hop type, length, precision, PK, native type)
| `schema_harvest_fk` | EXPECTED and DISCOVERED foreign-key constraints (child/parent columns, constraint name)
| `schema_harvest_change` | Diff events (field ADDED/REMOVED/CHANGED, PRIMARY_KEY_CHANGED, FOREIGN_KEY_*, severity)
|===

Harvest compares the catalog **effective** layout (after link:data-type-mappings.adoc[data type mappings]) to rediscovered source projections. PIPELINE, JSON, and COMPOSITE feeds reload attached mapping profiles on rediscovery, so a mapped default String length is not reported as `FIELD_TYPE_CHANGED` against a physical String with no length.

=== Primary keys and foreign keys

* **PK drift** — catalog field `primaryKeyPosition` vs live key composition (`PRIMARY_KEY_CHANGED`, typically **BLOCKING**).
* **FK discovery** — JDBC imported keys are always stored on the harvest (`schema_harvest_fk`) and can seed catalog contracts and `.hsm` models (see below).
* **FK vs catalog contract** — optional FK attributes on catalog source fields (`fkConstraintName`, `fkPosition`, `fkReferenced*`). When the catalog has **no** FK metadata yet, live-only FKs are recorded as **INFO** inventory (not a gate failure). When a catalog FK contract exists, removed/changed FKs are **BLOCKING** and extra FKs are **WARNING**.

Runs are **immutable**: reusing a `harvest_run_id` skips insert.

== Applying harvest to the catalog and source models

Harvest **never** rewrites catalog contracts by itself. After you review a good harvest run, you can promote FK (and optionally field) inventory deliberately:

=== Apply harvest to catalog (GUI)

On metadata type **Resource definition group**, bottom bar **Apply harvest to catalog…**:

1. Loads the latest harvest for the group (or the run id in `DV_SCHEMA_HARVEST_RUN_ID` when set).
2. Offers **Foreign keys only** (default choice) or **Field layouts and foreign keys**.
3. Writes DISCOVERED FKs onto matching catalog `DV_SOURCE` child columns (`fkConstraintName`, `fkPosition`, `fkReferencedSchema/Table/Column`), clearing any previous FK stamp first.

After apply, the next harvest/gate treats those FKs as a real contract (removed/changed → **BLOCKING**, extra → **WARNING**) instead of INFO inventory only.

=== Generate `.hsm` from harvest (GUI)

Same editor bar: **Generate .hsm from harvest…**

* Prompts for a `.hsm` path (variables allowed; default under `${PROJECT_HOME}/models/…-from-harvest.hsm`).
* Builds or **merges** a link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[source model]: DISCOVERED tables/columns, relationships from DISCOVERED FKs, and optional **stub parent** tables when a parent was not harvested as a subject.
* Existing relationships are not duplicated on re-run; existing tables get column layouts refreshed.

Use this when you want source-modeler canvas/relationships aligned with the same inventory the harvest already observed.

== Efficiency

For `DATABASE` sources that share a Hop connection, harvest opens **one** JDBC session and discovers every table in that partition serially on that session. Parallelism is across **source systems** (connections), not every table on the same VPN path.

CSV / Parquet / Iceberg / COMPOSITE feeds still use the shared discovery services (composite rediscovers from the `.hsm` projection).

== Catalog is never rewritten by harvest alone

The **Harvest source metadata** action does **not** update working-tree catalog contracts or catalog version tags. To accept live layout as the new contract:

* **Field layouts** — **Refresh from source** (catalog GUI) or remediation from link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[resource definition validation]
* **Foreign keys (and optional fields) from a harvest run** — **Apply harvest to catalog…** on the resource definition group (above)
* **Source model relationships** — **Generate .hsm from harvest…**

== Relationship to the schema gate


|===
|  Harvest | Validate resource definitions
| Live discovery | Primary | `LIVE_SOURCE` rediscovers; **`HARVEST_RUN` reuses OPS harvest** 
| Target DDL / lineage impact | No | Yes (optional axes)
| Persist history | Yes (OPS) | Report files only
| Fail on drift | No (by default) | Yes (severity policy)
|===

=== Compare mode `HARVEST_RUN`

On **Validate resource definitions**:

* **Compare mode** = `HARVEST_RUN`
* **Harvest run id** = `${DV_SCHEMA_HARVEST_RUN_ID}` (set by the harvest action), or empty → **latest** harvest for the group
* **Harvest history database / schema** = same OPS location as harvest (retail: `OPS` / `dv_ops`)

The gate rebuilds a normal validation report from `schema_harvest_change` / subject rows (no second JDBC discovery of sources). Severity policy is unchanged:

|===
| Harvest change | Typical gate severity
| Field removed / primary key changed | **BLOCKING**
| Field added / type or length changed | **WARNING**
| Source unavailable / discovery error | **BLOCKING**
|===

Optional **Check target databases** still runs live against the EDW (independent of harvest).

Retail `run-retail-update-models.hwf` uses **Harvest → Validate (HARVEST_RUN) → quality → update**.

== Exploring harvest history (GUI)

=== Resource definition group

Open metadata type **Resource definition group**. The bottom button bar includes harvest actions next to version management and validation:

image::images/resource-definition-group-editor.png[Resource definition group editor for retail-sources with Generate .hsm from harvest, Apply harvest to catalog, Harvest history, Browse lineage, catalog version, and Validate sources,align="center"]

* **Generate .hsm from harvest…** / **Apply harvest to catalog…** — promote harvest inventory (see above)
* **Harvest history…** — browse OPS runs and subject drift
* **Browse lineage…** — reverse lineage across models in the group
* **List / Tag catalog version**, **Validate sources** — design-time contracts and schema gate

=== Harvest history browser

**Harvest history…** opens a master/detail dialog over OPS `schema_harvest_*` tables:

image::images/schema-harvest-history-dialog.png[Schema harvest history for retail-sources: runs table (status, subjects, changes, baseline, run id) and subjects for the selected run,align="center"]

* Master table: recent harvest runs for that group (status, subject counts, change counts, baseline, run id)
* Detail table: subjects for the selected run (in sync, discovery status, source type, database, table)
* Filters: **Only subjects with changes**, **Database** connection name, **Source type** (`DATABASE`, `CSV`, …)
* **Open changes…** / double-click subject → change events + expected/discovered field snapshots
* **Open in catalog** → jump to the record definition in the Data Catalog perspective

=== Subject changes drill-down

Double-click a subject (or **Open changes…**) to inspect persisted drift and field snapshots for that harvest run:

image::images/schema-harvest-changes-dialog.png[Schema harvest changes dialog: WARNING CHANGED on customer_id expected length 9 to actual length 10, with Fields expected/discovered tab,align="center"]

* **Changes** tab — severity, kind (`CHANGED`, `ADDED`, `REMOVED`, PK/FK kinds), field, detail
* **Fields (expected / discovered)** tab — side-by-side snapshots stored in `schema_harvest_field`

=== Catalog record (DV_SOURCE)

On the record detail **Quality** tab, **Schema harvest…** opens a timeline of harvest results for that subject key. Double-click a row for the same changes/fields drill-down.

OPS connection resolution matches harvest/gate: `SCHEMA_HARVEST_DATABASE`, published `schema_harvest_run` catalog definition, or connection **OPS**.

== Model check reuse (Phase 4)

After harvest (and optionally after the schema gate), **Data Vault Update** and **Update resource definition group** can reuse DISCOVERED layouts for detailed type checking:

* Option **Prefer last harvest for type checks** (default on)
* **Harvest run id** default `${DV_SCHEMA_HARVEST_RUN_ID}`
* **Harvest history database** (OPS) when not auto-resolved

Behavior:

1. Load DISCOVERED fields for each database subject from the harvest.
2. Pre-seed the model-check live-fields cache (same keys as JDBC resolution: connection/schema/table).
3. Cache hits skip live JDBC for those tables; missing keys still discover live.

This avoids a third full source-schema discovery after harvest + gate in the retail chain.

== Phase roadmap

* **Phase 1:** harvest engine, OPS history, workflow action, reports
* **Phase 2:** schema gate `HARVEST_RUN` + retail chain
* **Phase 3:** harvest history browser (group + catalog subject)
* **Phase 4:** model-check reuse of harvest for detailed type checking
* **Follow-on:** PK/FK drift inventory, apply harvest → catalog FKs, generate/merge `.hsm` from harvest (available)

== Related documentation

* link:architecture.adoc#d5-four-controls[Architecture — four controls]
* link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW] (harvest is day-2, not chapter 1)
* link:resource-definition-group.adoc[Resource definition group]
* link:data-catalog.adoc[Data catalog]
* link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[Source modeler]
* link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation]
* link:update-resource-definition-group-action.adoc[Update resource definition group]
* link:operations.adoc[Operations]
* link:data-quality.adoc[Data quality]
* link:database-table-metadata.adoc[Database Table Metadata transform]
* Plan: link:plans/metadata-harvesting-plan.md[Metadata harvesting plan (issue #112)]

= Architecture and model export (Draw.io)
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

Export **derived** diagrams for architects and analysts. Models and workflows remain the source of truth; exports are projections for Draw.io / ArchiMate-style communication (issue #104).

For a **single** open model (`.hsm` / `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm` / `.hem`), prefer Hop 2.20 **File → Export diagram** or `hop export -f model.hdm --format drawio` (also SVG, PDF, PlantUML, Mermaid). This page is the **multi-model** Draw.io workflow (`hop architecture-export`): SOLUTION architecture, DATA inventory, and aggregated DV/BV/DM diagrams.

== Four products

[cols="1,2,2", options="header"]
|===
|Product |Purpose |Layout

|**SOLUTION architecture**
|What the project *implements and runs* at **process** level: workflows, controls/capabilities, and **model file** references (e.g. `models/retail-360.hdv`). No table/dataset grain (that would clutter Draw.io beyond a useful overview).
|Layered **swimlanes** with multi-row wrapping (architecture layout — not ELK / Draw.io auto-layout).

|**DATA inventory**
|Which tables and sources are involved across models (lineage). **No relationship arrows**. Default file name: `data-inventory.drawio`. Catalog feeds (including composite sources published from `.hsm` queries) appear as source inventory when referenced by vault models.
|Swimlanes by layer; multi-row packing.

|**MODEL diagrams (aggregated by layer)**
|**Enterprise multi-file** data-model projection: all `.hdv` files → one DV diagram; all `.hbv` → one BV diagram; all `.hdm` → one dimensional diagram. Shared hubs/dims are **deduped by name**. Structural relationships included. Source models (`.hsm`) remain the ER canvas for physical sources; they are not yet a separate aggregated Draw.io layer (use the `.hsm` file and DATA inventory for source-side views).
|**ELK** layout (same stack as the Hop GUI canvas).

|**MODELS diagrams (one file per model)**
|**Documentation set** for each model listed on a **resource definition group** (or an explicit path list): one Draw.io per `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm` under type subfolders. No SOLUTION crawl required.
|**ELK** layout per model file.
|===

The point of **MODEL** export is the **aggregate across model files** (subject areas, shared core, multiple dimensional stars). Use **MODELS** when you want a folder of diagrams named after each model for docs or review.

== Screenshots (retail example)

Solution architecture — workflows, controls/capabilities, and model file references (no table dump):

image::images/architecture-export-retail-example-solution-drawio.png[Retail SOLUTION architecture Draw.io export,align="center"]

Data inventory — tables and sources involved, no relationship edges (default file `data-inventory.drawio`):

image::images/architecture-export-retail-example-inventory-drawio.png[Retail DATA inventory Draw.io export,align="center"]

Aggregated Data Vault model — all `.hdv` tables unioned with ELK layout:

image::images/architecture-export-retail-example-data-vault-drawio.png[Retail aggregated data-vault.drawio ELK export,align="center"]

Aggregated dimensional model — all `.hdm` tables unioned with ELK layout:

image::images/architecture-export-retail-example-dimensional-model-drawio.png[Retail aggregated dimensional.drawio ELK export,align="center"]

== Example artifact set (retail)

[source,text]
----
work/architecture/retail-solution.drawio       # process architecture only
work/architecture/data-inventory.drawio        # short default inventory name
work/architecture/models/data-vault.drawio     # all .hdv tables unioned + ELK
work/architecture/models/business-vault.drawio
work/architecture/models/dimensional.drawio

# MODELS view (per file) — typically from a resource definition group:
work/architecture/models/data-vault/retail-360.drawio
work/architecture/models/business-vault/retail-360.drawio
work/architecture/models/dimensional/retail-f-orders.drawio
work/architecture/models/dimensional/retail-conformed-dims.drawio
----

== Formats (current)

* **Draw.io** (`.drawio` / mxfile XML) — open in https://app.diagrams.net/[diagrams.net] or the Draw.io desktop app.

ArchiMate Open Exchange XML is planned next (same intermediate graphs).

== Workflow action

**Export architecture** (`EXPORT_ARCHITECTURE`):

* **Root** — workflow path, `.hem`, or for DATA/MODEL/MODELS a comma-separated list of `.hdv`/`.hbv`/`.hdm` paths (optional when a resource definition group supplies models)
* **Resource definition group** — optional. When set, supplies model files for DATA, MODEL, MODELS, and SOLUTION “also export” options (overrides root path list and execution-map discovery)
* **View type** — `SOLUTION`, `DATA` (inventory), `MODEL` (layer aggregates), `MODELS` (one file per model under type subfolders), or `END_TO_END`
* **Output Draw.io file** — primary SOLUTION destination
* **Also export DATA inventory** — second file from models (group preferred, else crawl discovery)
* **Also export aggregated model diagrams (ELK)** — writes `data-vault.drawio` / `business-vault.drawio` / `dimensional.drawio` under the models folder
* **Models output folder** — for `MODEL` aggregates and `MODELS` per-file diagrams (default `${PROJECT_HOME}/work/architecture/models`)

=== MODELS-only documentation export

To document every model on a resource definition group **without** solution architecture:

1. Set **View type** to `MODELS`
2. Select the **Resource definition group**
3. Set **Models output folder** (optional)
4. Leave **Root** empty

Output layout:

[source,text]
----
{models folder}/
  data-vault/{basename}.drawio
  business-vault/{basename}.drawio
  dimensional/{basename}.drawio
----

Basename is the model file name without extension (`models/subdir/retail-360.hdv` → `retail-360.drawio`).

== CLI

With Data Hopper EDW installed. Enable a Hop **project** or **lifecycle environment** the same way as `hop-run` (projects plugin mixins). Use **one** of `-j` / `--project` **or** `-e` / `--environment` (not both).

Relative paths resolve under `${PROJECT_HOME}`. Paths inside diagrams are project-relative (e.g. `models/retail-360.hdv`).

[source,bash]
----
# Solution + inventory + aggregated layer model diagrams:
hop architecture-export \
  -e retail-example-docker-pg \
  -f workflows/run-retail-update.hwf \
  -o work/architecture/retail-solution.drawio \
  --view SOLUTION \
  --also-data \
  --data-output work/architecture/data-inventory.drawio \
  --also-models \
  --models-output work/architecture/models

# MODEL only — pass every model file; get three layer aggregates:
hop architecture-export \
  -e retail-example-docker-pg \
  -f models/retail-360.hdv,models/retail-360.hbv,models/retail-f-orders.hdm,models/retail-conformed-dims.hdm \
  --view MODEL \
  --models-output work/architecture/models

# MODELS only — one Draw.io per model from a resource definition group:
hop architecture-export \
  -e retail-example-docker-pg \
  -g retail-sources \
  --view MODELS \
  --models-output work/architecture/models
----

DATA inventory only:

[source,bash]
----
hop architecture-export \
  -e retail-example-docker-pg \
  -f models/retail-360.hdv,models/retail-360.hbv \
  -o work/architecture/retail-data-inventory.drawio \
  --view DATA
----

Or with a group:

[source,bash]
----
hop architecture-export \
  -e retail-example-docker-pg \
  -g retail-sources \
  -o work/architecture/retail-data-inventory.drawio \
  --view DATA
----

== How it is built

[source,text]
----
workflow / .hem     →  Execution map crawl  →  ArchitectureGraph (SOLUTION)
model lineage       →  ArchitectureGraph (DATA inventory, no ER edges)
all .hdv / .hbv / .hdm
  →  ElkGraphLayout.from*Models (union + dedupe)
  →  layoutToBoxes (ELK, no model file mutation)
  →  ArchitectureGraph (MODEL freeform)  →  data-vault | business-vault | dimensional .drawio
each .hdv / .hbv / .hdm
  →  ElkGraphLayout (single file)
  →  ArchitectureGraph (MODELS freeform)
  →  {type}/{basename}.drawio
----

* ELK coordinates are computed in memory and **do not** rewrite table positions in model files on disk.
* Does **not** replace OpenLineage/Marquez or `hop svg` (canvas fidelity per file).
* Multi-team model organization: link:enterprise-modeling-and-team-collaboration.adoc[Organizing large Data Vault programs].

== Related

* link:execution-maps.adoc[Execution maps]
* link:source-to-target-lineage.adoc[Source-to-target lineage]
* link:openlineage-export.adoc[OpenLineage export]
* link:feature-overview.adoc[Feature overview]

# Hop Web support for modelers

Status: **available (experimental)** — issue [#119](https://github.com/ProjectDataHopper/hopper-edw/issues/119).

Under **Hop Web** (RAP), the six model file graphs (the original five plus Hop Lineage View) render through the same SVG canvas stack as pipelines and workflows, with plugin-specific painters and client interaction polish.

## File types

| Extension | Graph |
|-----------|--------|
| `.hsm` | Source modeler |
| `.hdv` | Data Vault modeler |
| `.hbv` | Business Vault modeler |
| `.hdm` | Dimensional modeler |
| `.hem` | Execution map viewer |
| `.hlv` | Hop Lineage View (live session graph; experimental, same bar as `.hem`) |

## What works

| Area | Behaviour |
|------|-----------|
| Open / create / save | Same file types and explorer tabs as desktop |
| Paint | Server `SvgGc` → SVG snapshot → client overlay above the RAP canvas |
| Pan | Middle button or Ctrl+drag: dimmed SVG + **wireframe** of cards/notes; full paint on mouse-up |
| Zoom | Toolbar combo / buttons; **mouse wheel** via Hop Web zoom handler (SVG host does not capture wheel events) |
| Drag tables/cards | Client **card-sized** blue outline ghosts while dragging; server applies final positions on mouse-up (RAP has no move-while-held) |
| Drag notes | Full note-size outline from top-left (not a cursor square); same final apply on mouse-up |
| Note resize | Edge/corner cursors and 8 handles; live outline while resizing |
| Multi-select | Lasso; drag previews for all selected cards/notes |
| Relationships | Rubber-band hop line on the SVG effects layer (from card center when sizes are published) |
| Minimap | Bottom-right navigation viewport with miniature cards (including **source model** content) |
| Tab switch | SVG + zoom rebind so the active tab paints without an extra click |
| BV/DV reference links | Follow name-click navigation; shared SVG client stays on the **target** tab (no snap-back to the previous model) |
| Execution map breadcrumb | Drill / breadcrumb **zoom-fit uses the focused subgraph** size (not the full-document maximum) |
| Lineage view details | Right-hand Markdown sash uses a plain `Text` widget on RAP (no `StyledText`); **View as HTML** still opens formatted details |
| Lineage view empty/error | Painted in the SVG snapshot (not only the status `Label`) |
| Dark mode | SVG render uses `SvgGc` dark theme + `NotePadStyle` |
| Edit | Double-click / name-click dialogs, **left-click context dialogs** on tables/cards, toolbars (standard SWT/RAP dialogs) |
| Hover | Name underline via Hop Web hover remote object |

## Hop core requirement

Plugin code calls:

- `CanvasSvgFacade.registerCanvas` / `publishSnapshot` / `ensureInteractionHandler`
- `IWebCanvasGraph` (hover + area owners)

These APIs land in Apache Hop via [issue #7873](https://github.com/apache/hop/issues/7873) / [PR #7874](https://github.com/apache/hop/pull/7874). Use **Apache Hop 2.20.0-SNAPSHOT**, which includes that SPI, the related Hop Web client fixes (SVG effects-layer previews, zoom wheel hit-testing, active-canvas-only rebind), explorer HTML/PDF with a document base ([issue #8297](https://github.com/apache/hop/issues/8297)), and the AI Assistant workbench.

### Hop Web client behaviour (core)

The shared client scripts (`canvas-svg.js`, `canvas-zoom.js`, explorer tab hooks) also provide:

- Drag/resize/pan previews on an **effects layer above** the SVG (pipeline `canvas.js` paint sits under the SVG and is not visible for model graphs)
- **Single SVG + zoom remote** per UI session: only the **active** canvas rebinds the client after paint (avoids a background paint stealing the overlay after link navigation)
- Zoom wheel attached to the RAP canvas by widget id; SVG host uses `pointer-events: none` so the wheel reaches the canvas

## Desktop vs web

| Concern | Desktop | Hop Web |
|---------|---------|---------|
| Paint | `SwtGc` on SWT `Canvas` | Server `SvgGc` → SVG snapshot → client overlay |
| Drag while button held | Server mouse-move | Client outline; server applies final position on mouse-up |
| Left-click vs drag | 3px threshold on move-while-held | Mouse-down arms a client drag ghost; mouse-up with no movement is a click (table context dialog) |
| Load duration overview | Optional right pane (duration bars) | Same pane; table with one row per table and one column per run |
| Coach palette DnD | DropTarget on canvas | Disabled (use toolbar / dialogs) |
| Markdown details / notes | SWT `StyledText` style ranges | Plain `Text` (RAP has no `StyledText`); lineage **View as HTML** still opens formatted details |

## Architecture (plugin)

```
HopGuiModelGraphBase
  ├── setupWebCanvas()          register + zoom + empty nodes/notes/hops
  ├── paint → *CanvasSvgRenderer → SvgGc painters
  ├── applyWebCanvasRender()    area owners, setNodes/setNotes, publishSnapshot
  └── armWeb*DragModes()        mode=drag|resize|hop for client ghosts

ModelGraphWebCanvasData         RAP-safe setData for nodes/notes/hops/mode
*ModelCanvasSvgRenderer         Source / DV / BV / DM / EM / HLV wrappers
SourceModelSvgPainter           headless .hsm SVG export
LineageViewCanvasSvgRenderer    live .hlv session graph (not a persisted snapshot)
```

Painters already target `IGc`. Interactive web path uses the `*ModelCanvasSvgRenderer` wrappers, collects `AreaOwner` hit regions, and publishes via `CanvasSvgFacade.publishSnapshot`.

## Run locally

1. Install Hop with the canvas SPI and current web client scripts (`core` / `engine` / `ui` / `rap` as needed).
2. Build this plugin: `mvn clean package -DskipTests`
3. Unzip `target/hopper-edw-*-SNAPSHOT.zip` into the Hop Web home (not only `plugins/misc/hopper-edw/`) so Jinjava jars land in `lib/core`.
4. Start Hop Web (for example `docker/run-hop-web-local.sh --quick` from a Hop checkout that mounts the plugin).
5. Create or open a model under the explorer.

## Known limitations

- Continuous “live” card motion while the button is held is client-outline only; the authoritative model updates on mouse-up (RAP).
- Coach drag-from-palette remains desktop-first. Load-duration overview is a table on Hop Web.
- Lineage view cards are **not** user-draggable (ELK owns layout). Click is select / context only.
- Marquez, export-folder, and OPS queries run in the **Hop Web server JVM**. `${MARQUEZ_BASE_URL}=http://localhost:5001` is localhost inside that process (or container), not the browser. Use a URL or folder the server can reach, or the **Local models** backend / **Show lineage**.
- Requires the Hop SPI and client fixes above; older Hop Web builds will not compile or run this plugin version correctly.

## Related

- Feature matrix: [feature-overview.adoc](feature-overview.adoc)
- Changelog: [../CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md)
- Hop SPI: [apache/hop#7873](https://github.com/apache/hop/issues/7873), [PR #7874](https://github.com/apache/hop/pull/7874)

docs.content:
= Target type mappings (Hop type to DDL)
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

== Why

link:data-type-mappings.adoc[Data type mappings] control how source metadata arrives as Hop types (String, Integer, Timestamp, length, precision). They do **not** control the **native SQL type** Hop emits for CREATE/ALTER.

Hop dialect defaults are reasonable (Postgres `VARCHAR(n)`, `TIMESTAMP`, `SMALLINT` for short integers) but estates often want project policy: `CHAR(1)` flags, `NVARCHAR({length})`, `timestamp(6) with time zone`.

A **Target type mapping** is a reusable metadata element with ordered rules. Matching rules run **before** Hop `getFieldDefinition`. Unmatched columns keep today’s database-specific types.

On **Snowflake**, the plugin then rewrites Hop’s dialect defaults that are wrong for Data Vault: `TYPE_BINARY` → `BINARY(n)` instead of `VARIANT`, timestamps → `TIMESTAMP_NTZ`, dates → `DATE`. A target type mapping still wins when a rule matches.

Issue https://github.com/ProjectDataHopper/hopper-edw/issues/127[#127].

== Concepts

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Concept |Role

|**Target type mapping** (metadata)
|Named project profile: optional **target database** plus ordered **rules**.

|**Match**
|Hop type, inclusive min/max length and precision, length absent, optional field-name pattern.

|**Target SQL type**
|Native type template. Hop variables (`'${VARCHAR_TYPE}'`) then `'{length}'` / `'{precision}'`.

|**First match wins**
|Put `CHAR(1)` before `NVARCHAR({length})`.

|**Auto-match**
|When no mapping is selected and **exactly one** saved mapping names the actual target connection, that mapping is used.
|===

This is **not** a Data type mapping. Data type mappings improve source → Hop. Target type mappings improve Hop → DDL.

== Project metadata editor

In Hop **Metadata** perspective, under **EDW**, create a **Target type mapping** (key `target-type-mapping`).

* **Name** / **Description**
* **Target database** — Hop connection this profile is intended for (auto-match + preview)
* **Rules** — ordered match → SQL type grid
* **Preview** — sample Hop type / length / precision / field name → resolved SQL (or dialect default)

image::images/target-type-mapping-editor-rules-tab.png[Target type mapping editor — Rules tab with match criteria and target SQL type,align="center"]

image::images/target-type-mapping-editor-preview-tab.png[Target type mapping editor — Preview tab resolving String length 1 to CHAR(1),align="center"]

Retail ships **vault-target-mapping** (`retail-example/metadata/target-type-mapping/`, target database `Vault`):

* String, min-length=1, max-length=1 → `CHAR({length})`

`run-retail-update-models.hwf` selects that mapping on **Update resource definition group**. Other useful rules (not in the sample):

* String, max-length=2000 → `NVARCHAR({length})` (or `VARCHAR({length})` on Postgres)
* Integer, max-length=2 → `BYTE`
* Integer, max-length=3 → `SMALLINT`
* Timestamp → `timestamp(6) with time zone`

== Where you select it

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Surface |Behaviour

|**Record Definition DDL**
|Optional **Target type mapping** on the Target tab. Empty → auto-match on the resolved target connection.

|**Update resource definition group**
|Operations tab. The name is copied to each child DV / BV / DM update.

|**Data Vault / Business Vault / Dimensional Update**
|DDL tab. Same optional override.

|Modeler SQL, schema gate, remediation
|No extra field. Unique auto-match on the model target connection, or the `DATAVAULT_TARGET_TYPE_MAPPING` variable set by an update action.
|===

An explicit name that does not exist **fails DDL** (no silent fallback). Two mappings for the same target database skip auto-match; select one explicitly.

A mapping on the integration-test `Vault` connection changes generated DDL; do not add one there unless you update the relevant goldens. The retail sample mapping only remaps one-character Strings to `CHAR({length})`.

== Placeholders and variables

. `IVariables` resolves the template (`'${VARCHAR_TYPE}'`).
. `'{length}'` and `'{precision}'` (case-insensitive) are replaced from the Hop field.

If the template still contains `'{length}'` and the field has no length, the rule does not match.

== SQL Server UTF-8

Vault/EDW SQL Server DDL still expands unmatched ANSI `VARCHAR`/`CHAR` (length ×3 + UTF-8 `COLLATE`). A column that **matched a rule** is emitted verbatim (`NVARCHAR({length})` is not expanded).

== Recommended workflow

. Create one **Target type mapping** per warehouse dialect / connection.
. Set **Target database** to the vault connection so modeler SQL and Update agree without selecting the mapping on every action.
. List specific rules first.
. Optionally select the mapping on **Update resource definition group** or **Record Definition DDL** when several mappings exist.

docs.content:
= Data Vault Source
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3
:openvar: ${
:closevar: }

toc::[]

A **Data Vault Source** is a **Data Catalog record definition** of type `DV_SOURCE`. It describes a logical feed that supplies rows to hubs, links, and satellites. Model tables reference the source **name**, not a raw database connection.

Each definition combines:

* **DV semantics** — record source indicator, optional **group** for partial workflow loads
* **Physical layout** — **database** table, **CSV** / **Parquet** / **Iceberg**, **composite** multi-table query, **JSON** extraction, or **pipeline** feed from a link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[source model (`.hsm`)]

Sources live under namespace `hop/\{project\}/sources` in the FILE catalog storage directory (retail example: `work/edw-catalog/`) and open in the **Data Catalog** perspective. See link:data-catalog.adoc[Data Catalog] for folder layout and refresh behavior.

Field layout is stored on structured homes (`dvSource.fields` and, for table-backed sources, physical table fields). Do not invent a parallel layout blob in catalog JSON.

== Composite sources

A **COMPOSITE** `DV_SOURCE` is published from a source-model **source query**. It stores:

* Projected field list (aliases used when mapping hub/sat attributes)
* Path to the `.hsm` file and the query name (generation prefers live SQL from the model)
* Optional cached SQL when the model file is unavailable

Data Vault Update builds either a single-connection `Table Input` or a Merge Join pipeline depending on the query's generation mode. See link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[Source modeler overview].

== JSON sources

A **JSON** `DV_SOURCE` is published from a source-model **Source JSON** object. It stores:

* Projected field list (pass-through keys + JsonPath extractions)
* Path to the `.hsm` file and the Source JSON name
* Parent reference (table / query / nested JSON source) and the JSON field to parse

At load time, Data Vault Update injects the generated parent + JsonInput graph, then:

* Adds a **Constant** (or rename) for the vault record-source column when the feed uses a static `sourceIndicator`
* For **hubs**, sorts and distincts identity fields so MergeRowsPlus CDC matches database/file sources on incremental loads

Retail sample: `feed_order_shipment_tracking` over `order_shipment_event.payload` → `hub_order_shipment` / link / sat.

== Create and edit a source

. Open the Hop project.
. Open the **Data Catalog** perspective.
. Under `hop/\{project\}/sources`, create or open a `DV_SOURCE` record.
. Set connection, table, and fields (database-backed sources).
. Configure record source indicator and optional group.

The model toolbar **Import sources** action can also create catalog entries from live database metadata.

== JSON structure (file catalog)

Each source is a JSON file. Important fields:

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Field |Description

|`namespace`
|Must match folder path (for example `hop/retail-example/sources`)

|`name`
|Unique within namespace; used in hub **Record sources** and satellite **Default record source**

|`type`
|`DV_SOURCE`

|`physicalTable`
|Database connection name, schema, table (`databaseMetaName`, `schemaName`, `tableName`)

|`dvSource.sourceIndicator`
|Optional fixed record source value for every row (for example `CRM`, `ERP`)

|`dvSource.sourceIndicatorField`
|Optional source column for per-row record source (used when indicator is empty)

|`dvSource.group`
|Optional tag for **Record source group** on Data Vault Update

|`dvSource.fields`
|**Authoritative** column layout (types, lengths, primary-key / FK flags, CSV options). Location refs (`physicalTable` / `physicalFile`) do not store the contract.

|===

Example path: `retail-example/work/edw-catalog/hop/retail-example/sources/E2E-customer-hub.json`.

== Record source indicator at runtime

The plugin applies this precedence:

1. If **source indicator** is non-empty (after variable resolution), that static value is used for all rows.
2. Otherwise, if **source indicator field** is set, the pipeline reads that column and aliases it to the model's record source column name.
3. If neither is set, no indicator is added from this source.

The target column name comes from `.hdv` model configuration unless a hub or link overrides it.

== Database field layout

Database-backed sources store per-column metadata used by **Load from source**, hashing, and type checking. See link:datavault-source-database.adoc[Database source details] for the field editor and **Import** from live schema.

Keeping the field list accurate is essential for **Check model** and **detailed data type checking**.

== Groups and partial loads

Set **group** on a source when only some feeds should run in a batch (for example `nightly` vs `hourly`). On **Data Vault Update**, set **Record source group** to match; sources with a different or empty group are skipped for that run.

== Validation

* **Catalog validation** — feed-level checks, proposals, acknowledgements; see link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation]
* **Check model** — verifies every referenced source exists and fields are present; optional live schema type checks

When detailed type checking is active, database sources resolve types from the live table. Stored catalog metadata remains the baseline; drift from the live schema produces warnings.

== Practical advice

* Name sources after the business feed, not only the physical table.
* Agree on record source value conventions across the program.
* Use **group** for scheduled partial loads without maintaining separate models.
* Prefer a static source indicator when all rows share one feed identity.
* Refresh the catalog (F5) after editing JSON files on disk.

== Related documents

* link:data-catalog.adoc[Data Catalog]
* link:datavault-source-database.adoc[Database source details]
* link:record-definition-input.adoc[Get Record Definition Names transform]
* link:record-definition-output.adoc[Catalog Record Definition Metadata Output transform]
* link:record-definition-data-input.adoc[Record Definition Input transform] (reads data rows)
* link:dv-hub.adoc[Hub metadata]
== Pipeline sources

Catalog type **`PIPELINE`** points at a Hop pipeline (`.hpl`) and an output transform. Field layout is the **declared** contract (from the source modeler pipeline card or catalog fields). Data Vault Update injects the pipeline with **MetaInject** using those declared output fields.

Typical authoring path:

. Add a **Source pipeline** card on a `.hsm` model.
. Design convert/filter/aggregate transforms; set the **output transform**.
. **Get fields from transform** (or edit the declared field list), mark logical keys, **Publish to catalog**.
. Bind hubs/links/satellites to the published feed name.

See link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[Source modeler overview].

The catalog is a **contract bus** (picture:
docs.content:
= Data Catalog
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

Data Hopper EDW stores **record definitions** in the Hop **Data Catalog**. Modelers work in the **Data Catalog** perspective; generated pipelines and transforms resolve definitions by namespace and name.

The catalog is a **contract bus** (picture: link:architecture.adoc#d2-catalog-bus[Architecture — D2]):

* **In:** source feeds (`DV_SOURCE` / `COMPOSITE` / `JSON` / `PIPELINE`) published from a source model or imported in this perspective.
* **Out:** published DV / BV / DM table layouts, lineage siblings, and operations stubs — written when **Update resource definition group** (or a per-model Update) has catalog publish enabled.

Harvest does **not** rewrite working-tree contracts. Apply-harvest and Refresh from source are explicit. Build order: link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]. The list of models that publish and validate together is a link:resource-definition-group.adoc[resource definition group].

== Local file catalog

Sample projects use a file-based catalog configured in `metadata/data-catalog/local-catalog.json`:

[source,json]
----
{
  "name": "local-catalog",
  "enabled": true,
  "catalog": {
    "FILE": {
      "pluginId": "FILE",
      "storageDirectory": "${PROJECT_HOME}/work/edw-catalog"
    }
  }
}
----

Definitions are JSON files under the FILE catalog **storage directory** (retail example: `work/edw-catalog/`, gitignored). The path after the storage root must match the record's **`namespace`** field. Other projects may still use a tracked folder such as `catalog-data/` — the path is only a metadata property.

== Namespaces

The plugin derives the default sources namespace from the open Hop project:

* Pattern: `hop/{project-folder-name}/sources`
* Examples:
** `retail-example/` → `hop/retail-example/sources`
** `integration-tests/` → `hop/integration-tests/sources`

Additional namespaces appear when models publish catalog entries, for example:

* `hop/{project}/models/{model-name}/` — DV table definitions
* `hop/{project}/business-vault/{model-name}/` — BV target tables
* `hop/{project}/dimensional/{model-name}/` — dimensional table definitions
* `hop/{project}/lineage/{dv|bv|dm}/{model-name}/` — **source-to-target lineage** sibling records (derived; not an edit surface)

Catalog lineage namespaces, the Lineage tab, explainable DDL, the drift gate, and the reverse browser are documented in link:source-to-target-lineage.adoc[Source-to-target lineage].

The catalog **key** is `namespace/name` (for example `hop/retail-example/sources/E2E-customer-hub`).

== Folder layout example (retail-example)

[source]
----
work/edw-catalog/              # gitignored runtime FILE catalog
└── hop/
    └── retail-example/
        ├── sources/           # DV_SOURCE feeds (copied from fixtures/catalog-sources)
        ├── models/retail-360/ # Published DV table layouts
        ├── business-vault/    # Published BV tables
        ├── dimensional/       # Published dimensional tables
        └── operations/        # Ops / quality table stubs (published at runtime)
----

== Working in Hop GUI

. Open the Hop project (so `${PROJECT_HOME}` resolves).
. Open the **Data Catalog** perspective.
. Browse the tree by namespace.
. Double-click a record to open its editor.
. Press **F5** or use refresh if files changed on disk.

If a record appears in the tree but fails to open, the **`namespace`** in the JSON file likely does not match its directory path. Fix the namespace and refresh.

== Record definition types

|===
| Type | Role |

| `DV_SOURCE` | Data Vault source feed — see link:datavault-source.adoc[Data Vault Source] |
| Other catalog types | Published model targets, conformed dimensions, pipeline inputs |
|===

== Field layout

Catalog documents store column layout in **structured field lists** — never as a top-level Hop `rowMetaXml` blob.

|===
| Type | Authoritative layout |

| `DV_SOURCE` | `dvSource.fields[]` (name, Hop type, length, precision, PK, optional FK and CSV options) |
| Vault / BV / DM targets, ops tables | `physicalTable.fields[]` |
|===

`physicalTable` / `physicalFile` / `physicalIcebergTable` are **location** refs for sources; only target/ops records put columns on `physicalTable.fields`.

In-memory Hop `IRowMeta` is derived from the structured list for pipeline APIs and is **not** persisted. Legacy files that still contain `rowMetaXml` are migrated into the structured list on load and rewritten without the blob.

Hub **Import keys**, satellite **Load from source**, catalog DDL, and the catalog field grid all resolve layout through `DvSourceFieldSupport.sourceFieldsFromDefinition`.

See also link:ai-file-schemas/metadata/catalog-record-definition.md[Catalog record definition schema notes].

== Validation

Use **Validate** on catalog record groups to run feed-level **schema** checks. Issues can include remediation proposals and acknowledgements — see link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation].

For **content** rules (not empty, allowed values, ranges, nulls), bind quality rules on the record definition and use the **Measure data quality** / **Evaluate quality gate** workflow actions — see link:data-quality.adoc[Data quality].

Model-level **Check model** validates `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm` structure separately; these layers complement each other.

[[catalog-versions]]
== Catalog versions

File-based catalogs can freeze **source record definitions** under a semantic tag (for example `v2.4.0` or `2026-Q3-Release`). Tags are a design-time baseline for schema comparison and CI gates; they are independent of DTAP database state.

=== Storage layout

Versions live under the catalog storage directory in a **non-hidden** folder named `catalog-versions` (not `.catalog-versions`):

[source]
----
{storageDirectory}/                 # e.g. work/edw-catalog/
├── hop/.../sources/*.json          # working tree (editable)
└── catalog-versions/
    ├── versions.json               # tag → snapshot index
    └── snapshots/<snapshot-id>/
        ├── manifest.json
        └── records/hop/.../*.json  # immutable copies
----

The working-tree catalog **list** API ignores `catalog-versions/` so snapshots never appear as live records. The Data Catalog perspective shows live records under **Working catalog (N)** and snapshots under **Catalog sources versions**. Get Record Definition Names reads only the working catalog. Retail stores the live catalog under gitignored `work/edw-catalog/`; a **seed** for demo tag `v1.0.0` lives in `fixtures/schema-gate-baseline/` and is copied by `workflows/bootstrap-retail-work.hwf` when `catalog-versions/versions.json` is not already there.

=== Tagging from Hop GUI

A catalog sources version freezes the **source contracts used by a resource definition group’s models**, not every file in the catalog.

**From a Resource definition group**

. Open metadata type **Resource definition group**.
. Select the group that references your DV/BV/DM models (for example `retail-sources`).
. Set the **Default catalog connection** (FILE catalog, for example `local-catalog`).
. Use **Tag catalog version** to snapshot all source definitions currently referenced by the group's models.
. Use **List catalog versions** to review existing tags, timestamps, and record counts.
. Use **Validate sources** for an interactive schema check: a design-time options dialog asks for the baseline (working catalog or version tag) and which axes to check (live sources, version drift, target models, target databases). Length remediation expands models and DV/BV/DM DDL from the catalog without rewriting catalog records.
. Use **Harvest history…** to browse persisted schema harvest runs and drift for sources used by the group.
. Use **Apply harvest to catalog…** / **Generate .hsm from harvest…** to promote harvest FK (and optional field) inventory into catalog contracts or a source model (see link:metadata-harvesting.adoc[Metadata harvesting]).

**From the Data Catalog perspective**

. Select any element under a FILE catalog connection (for example `local-catalog`).
. Click the toolbar **Tag version** action (enabled only when a catalog is selected).
. Choose the **resource definition group** that defines source scope, then enter the tag and optional description.
. Expand **Catalog sources versions** under that connection to browse tags and open frozen record definitions **read-only** (snapshots are never edited from the UI).

image::images/resource-definition-group-editor.png[Resource definition group editor for retail-sources with harvest actions, lineage, catalog version buttons, and Validate sources,align="center"]

Duplicate tags are rejected. Snapshot contents are immutable: editing working-tree JSON after tagging does not change the frozen version.

=== Scope (MVP)

* Snapshots cover **source record definitions** discovered from the resource definition group (hubs, satellites, links, BV SCD2 feeds, and DM `RECORD_DEFINITION` sources).
* Model files (`.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm`) remain versioned in Git; they are not copied into the snapshot.
* Only the **FILE** catalog implementation is supported.

Use tagged versions as the expected contract for the **Validate resource definitions** workflow action (compare tagged catalog vs live source or vs working tree, with optional Markdown/HTML reports and downstream impact). Full UI, compare modes, and DTAP recipe: link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation].

== Related documents

* link:resource-definition-group.adoc[Resource definition group]
* link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]
* link:datavault-source.adoc[Data Vault Source]
* link:metadata-harvesting.adoc[Metadata harvesting]
* link:record-definition-input.adoc[Get Record Definition Names transform]
* link:record-definition-output.adoc[Catalog Record Definition Metadata Output transform]
* link:record-definition-data-input.adoc[Record Definition Input transform] (reads data rows)

docs.content:
= Update resource definition group action
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

== Description

This is the **normal** load action once you have a link:resource-definition-group.adoc[resource definition group] — including a group that lists only one `.hdv`. Build order: link:getting-started-edw.adoc#chapter-4[Getting started — first load]. Per-model Data Vault / Business Vault / Dimensional Update actions remain available; **Begin/End Vault Update** is the advanced way to bracket a custom multi-action graph.

The **Update resource definition group** workflow action loads every Data Vault (`.hdv`), Business Vault (`.hbv`), and dimensional (`.hdm`) model listed on a **Resource definition group**, in a fixed layer order:

1. All **Data Vault** models (list order on the group)
2. All **Business Vault** models
3. All **dimensional** models

Each model runs through the same update path as the dedicated **Data Vault Update** / **Business Vault Update** / **Dimensional Update** actions (model check options, DDL policy, parallel pipeline copies, optional catalog publish).

If a listed `.hdv` uses a **read-only existing vault** configuration, that Data Vault job is **skipped** (logged) so Business Vault and dimensional updates still run. A standalone Data Vault Update action pointed at the same file still errors.

Optionally the action **manages vault update metrics** for the whole wave: it assigns `DV_WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_ID` at the start (Begin-style) and publishes a workflow load overview at the end (End-style). You do not need separate Begin/End Vault Update actions or hand-wired per-model hops for a standard multi-layer load.

Retail example workflows `run-retail-update.hwf` and `run-retail-update-models.hwf` use this action with group **`retail-sources`**.

== Dialog

image::images/update-resource-definition-group-action-dialog.png[Update resource definition group action dialog — Selection tab with group and layer includes,align="center"]

The dialog is organized into tabs.

=== Selection

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Resource definition group
|Metadata name of the group that lists `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm` paths (for example `retail-sources`). Required.

|Include Data Vault models
|Run Data Vault Update for each `.hdv` on the group (first).

|Include Business Vault models
|Run Business Vault Update for each `.hbv` (after DV).

|Include dimensional models
|Run Dimensional Update for each `.hdm` (after BV).
|===

=== Run

Load date, pipeline / workflow run configurations, parallel pipeline copies, and optional **Record source group** filter for Data Vault models (same semantics as Data Vault Update).

=== Operations

**Update target database structure**, **Fail if DDL is needed**, **Do not update target database** (dry run), and DV **Ensure special records**.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Update target database structure / Fail if DDL is needed
|Same DDL policy as the dedicated update actions, applied per model.

|Target type mapping
|Optional link:target-type-mappings.adoc[Target type mapping] applied before Hop dialect types. Copied to each child DV / BV / DM update. Empty uses unique auto-match on the model target connection.

|Do not update target database
|**Dry run.** Runs the parallel model checks (and optional DDL when structure update or fail-if-DDL is on) but **skips data load pipelines** on every child DV/BV/DM update — same semantics as Data Vault Update. With structure update and fail-if-DDL both off, only validation runs and reports (no per-model update step).
|===

=== Validation

Model checks for every selected DV/BV/DM model run **before** the update wave. Repeated **environment** findings (for example target database encoding / Unicode capability on a shared connection) are **collapsed once** in the log and report, with a model count, instead of one identical line per model.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Log model check failures / Abort on model check failures
|Log aggregated findings; abort stops the action when **errors** exist (warnings never abort by themselves).

|Detailed data type checking
|Live source schema checks for Data Vault models (higher latency over VPN).

|Prefer last harvest for type checks
|When detailed checking is on, reuse DISCOVERED layouts from **Harvest source metadata** (`${DV_SCHEMA_HARVEST_RUN_ID}` or latest for the group) instead of re-querying each source table. Default on; falls back to live discovery when no harvest is available.

|Harvest run id / history database
|Optional overrides for harvest reuse (defaults: `${DV_SCHEMA_HARVEST_RUN_ID}`, auto-resolved OPS).

|Model check parallelism
|Max concurrent model validations (default `8`, range 1–64, variables allowed). Independent of **Parallel pipeline copies** used for data loads.

|Ignore warnings
|Omit warnings from the workflow log (including shared encoding warnings). Errors still abort when abort-on-check is on. Warnings remain in the validation report file when written.

|Write validation report
|Write Markdown and/or HTML under the validation report folder (default `${PROJECT_HOME}/work/reports`). Shared findings appear once; model-specific issues are listed per model.
|===

=== Data catalog

**Publish target tables to catalog** after each model update, with optional catalog connection override (empty = use the group's default catalog connection).

=== Metrics

When **Manage vault update metrics (Begin/End)** is enabled:

* Assigns `DV_WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_ID` (and related variables) before models run — prefer **Use workflow log channel id as execution id**
* Propagates those variables onto this action and each programmatic child DV/BV/DM update so `load_run.workflow_execution_id` is correlated (required for overview reports)
* Uses the shared **Execution metrics profile** (retail: `retail-execution-metrics`)
* Can publish overview rows to the OPS database, ensure catalog definitions for overview tables, and log a summary to the workflow

=== Reports

Optional Markdown / HTML **workflow load overview** under a report folder (retail default: `${PROJECT_HOME}/work/reports`). Same report style as **End Vault Update**.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Write Markdown / Write HTML
|Emit load-overview reports after the wave (and on failure when metrics are available).

|Report output folder
|Directory for report files (variables allowed). Default `${PROJECT_HOME}/work/reports`.

|Report file base name
|Optional base name without extension (variables allowed). Retail passes `REPORT_BASE_NAME` (`retail-dv-initial-report` / `retail-dv-update-report`). Empty → auto name from workflow + execution id + timestamp.

|Include pipeline detail / insights
|Same detail levels as **End Vault Update**.
|===

If reports are missing after a successful load, check the workflow log for **no metrics found** for the execution id: child updates must inherit `DV_WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_ID` (handled by this action when metrics management is on).

== Live badge and load metrics

On the workflow canvas the action shows a bottom-right badge while it runs (clock / stall warning / failure) and a metrics glyph when idle. Click the badge or use **View load metrics** on the action context menu to open **Resource group load metrics**:

* **This run** — every model in the wave, current table, elapsed time, and live transform metrics (rows, buffers, stall seconds)
* **History** — recent OPS `workflow_load_overview` rows (double-click for per-model / per-pipeline detail)

image::images/action-update-resource-group-load-metrics-dialog.png[Resource group load metrics — This run tab during a retail-sources update (model 5 of 8, fact f_orders loading),align="center"]

See link:performance-tuning.md[Performance tuning] and link:help/resource-group-update-metrics-dialog.adoc[Resource group load metrics help].

== Open referenced models

From the workflow canvas context menu, **Open referenced object** lists every non-empty model path on the configured group (DV, then BV, then DM). Labels show a **project-relative** path for readability (for example `Data Vault: models/retail-360.hdv`) without a `${PROJECT_HOME}/` prefix. Opening still uses the stored path so Hop can resolve project variables.

== Typical chain

[source,text]
----
Harvest source metadata
  → Schema gate (Validate resource definitions)
  → Measure / Evaluate source quality
  → Update resource definition group (retail-sources)
  → Record the load in retail_load_log
----

See link:metadata-harvesting.adoc[Metadata harvesting] for the observation step, link:operations.adoc[Operations] for Docker runners and load overview screenshots, and link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation] for the schema gate.

= OpenLineage export
:toc: macro
