docs.content:
= Business Vault configuration
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

**Business Vault configuration** is project metadata that many `.hbv` files can share. Create it in the Metadata perspective under **EDW** and select it on **Edit model**. Older `.hbv` files may still embed a `<configuration>` block; **Extract to project configuration…** promotes that copy.

== General settings

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Setting |Description

|Target database
|Database connection (`DatabaseMeta`) where Business Vault tables are created and loaded. Required for DDL, Debug, and Business Vault Update. **May be a different connection** from the linked Data Vault model target — satellite history is read from the DV connection; BV tables are written (and incremental watermarks resolved) on this connection.

|Generated pipeline folder
|Optional folder where generated build pipelines are saved when debugging or updating. Variables supported.

|SCD2 pipeline name prefix
|Prefix for generated SCD2 build pipeline names (default `bv-scd2-`).

|PIT pipeline name prefix
|Prefix for generated PIT build pipelines (default `bv-pit-`).

|Business table pipeline name prefix
|Prefix for future business table pipelines (default `bv-biz-`).
|===

== SCD2 defaults

These values apply when an SCD2 table does not override them.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Setting |Description

|Functional timestamp field
|Default satellite column for the functional timeline. Leave empty to use the load-date fallback.

|Load date fallback field
|Used when no functional timestamp is set on the model or table (default follows Data Vault `loadDateField`, often `x_load_ts`).

|Valid from field
|Output column name for interval start (default `valid_from`; sample project uses `x_from_ts`).

|Valid to field
|Output column name for interval end (default `valid_to`; sample project uses `x_to_ts`).

|Open start sentinel
|Substituted when `valid_from` is null (default `1900-01-01 00:00:00`).

|Open end sentinel
|Substituted when `valid_to` is null (default `9999-12-31 23:59:59`).

|Generate primary keys in DDL
|When enabled, generated **CREATE TABLE** statements include a `PRIMARY KEY` on Business Vault identity columns (for example SCD2 grain + `valid_from`, or PIT hash key + snapshot date). Off by default. CREATE only (no ALTER retrofit).

|Generate foreign keys in DDL
|When enabled, generated **CREATE TABLE** statements may include `FOREIGN KEY` constraints to parent Data Vault tables **only when** the BV target database is the same connection as the linked DV model. Skipped for cross-database BV/DV setups and on engines without FK support (for example SingleStore). Off by default.
|===

== Target loading

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Setting |Description

|Target table batch size
|Commit size for generated `TableOutput` transforms (default 1000).

|Target table parallel copies
|Parallel copies hint for table output (default 1).
|===

== Data Vault model path

Configured on the Business Vault model itself (not inside the configuration block):

* **Data Vault model file** — path to the linked `.hdv` file
* Use `${PROJECT_HOME}` when the model lives inside a Hop project
* **Reload DV model** refreshes the linked model from disk after external edits

The linked `.hdv` must have its own **target database** configured — Business Vault reads satellite (and hub) history from that connection. Using separate Hop connection names for DV and BV is supported and recommended when raw vault and business vault live in different databases.

docs.title: Catalog Record Definition Metadata Output
docs.summary:
= Catalog Record Definition Metadata Output
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

The **Catalog Record Definition Metadata Output** transform (plugin id `RecordDefinitionOutput`) writes **record definition metadata** to a Hop **data catalog** connection. It is an output transform (category **Output**)
docs.content:
= Catalog Record Definition Metadata Output
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

The **Catalog Record Definition Metadata Output** transform (plugin id `RecordDefinitionOutput`) writes **record definition metadata** to a Hop **data catalog** connection. It is an output transform (category **Output**) and appears in the transform palette with the data catalog icon.

Use it when you want to **publish or migrate** catalog entries from a pipeline instead of only editing them in the Data Catalog perspective. Two field sources are supported:

* **Physical discovery** — inspect a database table, CSV/Parquet file, or Iceberg table and store the discovered layout.
* **Stream field definitions** — accept one input row per column (name, type, length, precision, primary key position, format options) and assemble complete definitions with a **field grouping** key. This path is intended for catalog migration and bulk load of existing metadata.

The inverse transform is link:record-definition-input.adoc[Get Record Definition Names], which reads catalog entries as metadata pipeline rows. To read **actual data** from a catalog source, use link:record-definition-data-input.adoc[Record Definition Input].

== Prerequisites

* A configured **data catalog connection** (DataCatalogMeta). The transform's **Catalog connection** dropdown lists every catalog connection in the project.
* For **physical discovery**: a reachable physical source (database connection, file path/folder, or Iceberg settings) that the Hop runtime can inspect.
* For **stream fields**: an upstream transform that emits **one row per field**, preferably sorted so consecutive rows for the same record definition share a stable grouping value.

You can inspect written entries afterward from the **Data Catalog** perspective in Hop GUI.

== Operating modes

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Mode |When to use

|Fixed configuration discovery
|No input stream (or no “select from input”). Namespace, name, and physical location are fixed dialog values. The transform discovers fields once and optionally writes one catalog entry.

|Per-row discovery
|**Select definition and source from previous transform input?** is enabled, and stream field mode is off. Each input row supplies definition keys and/or physical location fields; the transform discovers and writes once per input row.

|Stream field definitions (migration)
|**Use field definitions from input stream?** is enabled on the **Fields** tab. Physical discovery is skipped. Field rows are collected into groups; each group becomes one catalog write.
|===

== Dialog overview

The transform dialog has seven tabs: **General**, **Definition**, **Fields**, **Physical table**, **Source**, **DV Source**, and **Output**.

=== General

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Transform name
|The name of this transform in the pipeline graph.

|Catalog connection
|Required. Target data catalog connection for the upsert.

|Record definition type
|Semantic type of the entry to write (for example `DV_SOURCE`). Data Vault source loads use `DV_SOURCE`.

|Select definition and source from previous transform input?
|When enabled, namespace, name, description, and physical location can be read from input fields instead of fixed values. Stream field mode also requires an input stream (the dialog enables select-from-input when field stream mode is on).

|Write definition to catalog?
|When enabled (default), successful field resolution is written via the catalog registry (upsert). When disabled, the transform still resolves fields and emits status columns without persisting.

|Fail when no fields are available?
|When enabled (default), an empty field list fails the transform. When disabled, empty groups or failed discoveries produce status output without writing.
|===

=== Definition

Identifies the catalog entry (namespace + name) and optional description.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Namespace field / Name field / Description field
|Enabled when reading from input. Names of incoming columns that hold catalog namespace, record name, and description.

|Namespace value / Name value / Description value
|Enabled when not reading from input. Fixed values for a single definition. Namespace and name are required for a successful write.
|===

Typical namespaces follow project conventions (for example `hop/integration-tests/sources` or `hop/<project>/sources`). Names must be unique within a namespace.

=== Fields

Configures **stream field definition** mode — the migration path.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Use field definitions from input stream?
|When enabled, the transform does **not** discover fields from the physical source. Each input row contributes one column to the current definition. Select-from-input is forced on.

|Field grouping field
|Optional. Name of an input column used as the **consecutive group break key**. While this value stays the same, field rows are accumulated. When it changes, the previous group is written to the catalog and a new group starts. Leave empty to treat the **entire input stream** as a single definition (flush only at end of input).

|Field name field
|Required in stream mode. Incoming column that holds the catalog field name.

|Field type field
|Required in stream mode. Incoming column that holds the Hop type name (`String`, `Integer`, `Number`, `Date`, `Timestamp`, `Boolean`, `BigNumber`, and so on — the same labels as the catalog Fields tab).

|Field length field
|Optional. Incoming column for field length (stored as text on the source field).

|Field precision field
|Optional. Incoming column for field precision.

|Primary key position field
|Optional. Incoming column for 1-based position in the source primary key. Empty or zero means the field is not part of the key.

|Format field
|Optional. CSV/text format mask (for example date formats). Stored under field input options.

|Decimal symbol field
|Optional. Decimal separator for numeric CSV parsing.

|Grouping symbol field
|Optional. Thousands grouping symbol for numeric CSV parsing.
|===

==== Field grouping semantics

Stream mode behaves like a single-pass **Group By**:

* Rows must be **ordered** so that all fields for one record definition are consecutive. A later reappearance of an earlier grouping value starts a **new** group (it is not merged with the first).
* The **first row** of each group is the base for definition-level attributes (namespace, name, description, physical source fields, delivery type field). Keep those columns stable within a group.
* On end of input, the last open group is flushed automatically.
* One **status output row** is emitted per completed group (not one row per field).

.Example stream (grouping field = `record_name`)
[cols="1,1,1,1", options="header"]
|===
|record_name |field_name |field_type |field_length

|customer |customer_id |Integer |9
|customer |name |String |100
|order |order_id |Integer |9
|order |amount |Number |12
|===

This produces **two** catalog writes: `customer` with two fields, then `order` with two fields (namespace/name still come from Definition mapping on the first row of each group).

==== Mapping to the catalog Fields tab

Stream mappings align with the Fields section of a catalog entry in the Data Catalog perspective:

[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Dialog mapping |Catalog column |Stored on

|Field name |Name |Source field name
|Field type |Type |Hop type + source data type label
|Field length |Length |Source field length
|Field precision |Precision |Source field precision
|Primary key position |PK position |1-based key order
|Format / Decimal / Grouping |Format / Decimal / Grouping |CSV field input options (only when at least one is non-empty)
|===

Empty field names or unknown Hop type labels fail the transform with a clear error so bad migration rows do not silently corrupt the catalog.

=== Physical table

Maps to the catalog entry **Physical table** properties (`PhysicalTableRef`: database connection, schema, table). Used when the source type is **Database** (discovery and stream field modes).

In stream field / migration mode, values are taken from the **first row of each field group** when the corresponding input field is mapped and non-empty. Fixed values act as fallbacks.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Database connection
|Fixed Hop database connection name for the physical table.

|Schema
|Fixed schema (or empty for the connection default).

|Table
|Fixed physical table or view name.

|Database connection field
|Input column holding the connection name (preferred over the fixed value when non-empty).

|Schema field
|Input column holding the schema name.

|Table field
|Input column holding the table name.
|===

=== Source

Selects the Data Vault / discovery **source type** and non-table locations (file or Iceberg). Database connection coordinates live on the **Physical table** tab.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Source type
|`DATABASE`, `CSV`, `PARQUET`, or `ICEBERG` (composite sources are published from a `.hsm` source model, not this transform). For `DATABASE`, configure connection/schema/table on the **Physical table** tab.

|File path, folder, include/exclude masks, include subfolders
|CSV and Parquet location settings (fixed and/or field-based).

|Iceberg URI, warehouse, namespace, table, snapshot, branch, S3 credentials
|Iceberg location settings (fixed and/or field-based).
|===

In **discovery** mode, Source (and Physical table for databases) are used to **inspect** the physical object and derive the field list. In **stream field** mode the location is stored on the definition but discovery is skipped.

=== DV Source

Data Vault source metadata written with `DV_SOURCE` definitions.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Source indicator
|Fixed record-source indicator value (for example a system code such as `CRM`).

|Source indicator field
|Name of a **source data column** used as the record-source indicator (not an input mapping for this transform). Stored as source metadata.

|Group
|Organizational group tag on the Data Vault source. Distinct from the **Field grouping field** on the Fields tab.

|Delivery type
|Fixed delivery semantics: **Changes only** (`CHANGES_ONLY`) or **Full snapshot** (`FULL_SNAPSHOT`). Important for status tracking satellites and CDC-style loads: deletion detection is only valid for full snapshots.

|Delivery type field
|Optional input column that overrides the fixed delivery type per definition (first row of the group). Accepts codes (`CHANGES_ONLY`, `FULL_SNAPSHOT`) or the dialog description labels. Empty values fall back to the fixed **Delivery type**.
|===

=== Output

Names of status columns appended to each emitted row. Defaults:

[cols="2,3", options="header"]
|===
|Default name |Description

|`field_count`
|Number of fields written (or discovered) for the definition.

|`written_to_catalog`
|Boolean: `true` when the definition was upserted (write enabled and field count greater than zero).

|`catalog_namespace`
|Namespace that was written.

|`catalog_name`
|Record name that was written.
|===

In discovery modes the transform passes through the input row (when present) and appends these columns. In stream field mode it emits **one row per completed group**, based on the first row of that group, with the same status columns appended.

== Example: migrate field metadata into the catalog

A typical migration pipeline discovers columns with link:database-table-metadata.adoc[Database Table Metadata] (or loads a spreadsheet where each row is one column of a source table):

1. **CSV file input** (or table input) — rows with `namespace`, `name`, `record_key`, `field_name`, `field_type`, `field_length`, `field_precision`, `pk_position`, optional format columns, physical table coordinates, and `delivery_type`.
2. **Sort rows** — sort by `record_key` (and a stable field order if you care about column order).
3. **Record Definition Output**:
   * Catalog connection set to your target catalog.
   * **Use field definitions from input stream?** enabled.
   * **Field grouping field** = `record_key` (or `name` if that uniquely identifies each definition and is constant on every field row).
   * Map **Field name / type / length / precision / PK / format** columns.
   * Definition: namespace and name from input fields.
   * Physical table: database connection / schema / table from input fields (first row of each group).
   * Source: source type **Database** (or file/Iceberg as appropriate).
   * DV Source: delivery type fixed (**Full snapshot** / **Changes only**) or from a `delivery_type` field (`FULL_SNAPSHOT` / `CHANGES_ONLY` codes are accepted).
   * **Write definition to catalog?** enabled.

After the pipeline runs, open the Data Catalog perspective and confirm each definition’s Fields tab matches the migration file.

== Example: discover and publish from a physical table

1. **Get variables** or fixed values for namespace and name.
2. **Record Definition Output** with stream field mode **off**:
   * Source type **Database**, connection/schema/table set (fixed or from input).
   * Delivery type and source indicator on the DV Source tab.
   * Write to catalog enabled.

Each run discovers current columns and upserts the catalog entry. Use this for onboarding tables that already exist in the database.

== Tips

* Prefer **stream field mode** when the authoritative field list already exists outside Hop (data dictionaries, Excel, another catalog). Prefer **discovery** when the physical system is the source of truth.
* Always **sort** (or already group) input by the field grouping key before Record Definition Output in migration pipelines.
* Do not confuse **Field grouping field** (row-break key for collecting columns) with **Group** on the DV Source tab (business/org tag on the source).
* Keep catalog connection names stable across environments; override database connection names in the stream or via variables if needed.
* Variables are supported on catalog connection name and on fixed string values; field name combos select columns from the previous transform.
* After writing, use link:record-definition-input.adoc[Get Record Definition Names] (optionally with denormalized field metadata) to verify or drive DDL from the same catalog.
* Composite multi-table sources are not created by this transform; publish those from a link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[source model (`.hsm`)].

== Related documentation

* link:data-catalog.adoc[Data Catalog] — local catalog setup, namespaces, versions
* link:record-definition-input.adoc[Get Record Definition Names] — read catalog definition metadata as rows
* link:datavault-source.adoc[Data Vault sources] — `DV_SOURCE` record definitions
* link:datavault-source-database.adoc[Database-backed sources] — database source fields

docs.content:
= Data Vault linked tables and hub aliases :toc: macro :toclevels: 3 toc::[] Data Vault models use **linked tables** (`tableType=LINKED_TABLE`) for two related cases: 1. **Cross-model links** — read-only canvas cards that point at hubs, links, satellites, or reference tables defined in another `.hdv` file (subject-area models around a shared core). 2. **Same-model hub aliases** — role-playing names for the **same physical hub** so a link can participate that hub more than once with distinct source mappings and link columns (for example primary and secondary sales rep, or from/to location). Both patterns mirror dimensional `DIMENSION_ALIAS` / `referencedModelFilename`. IMPORTANT: A **linked table** is not a **Reference table**. Reference tables (`tableType=REFERENCE`) are physical code/catalog tables in the vault (natural keys, load, DDL). Linked tables are canvas pointers (no DDL or load of their own). == When to use * **Enterprise core + subject areas** — shared hubs live in `shared-core.hdv`; subject models link to them and define local links and satellites. For team ownership, git, catalog, and personas, see link:enterprise-modeling-and-team-collaboration.adoc[Organizing large Data Vault programs]. * **Avoid metadata duplication** — hash keys, business keys, and source mappings stay authoritative on the physical hub. * **Independent load workflows** — each `.hdv` file runs its own Data Vault Update action; linked tables/aliases do not generate DDL or loads. * **Same hub twice on one link (role-playing)** — prefer the **natural hub + one alias per extra role** (not an orphan physical hub). See link:dv-link.adoc[Data Vault Link] and the role-playing section below. == Linked table metadata A linked table is stored as `tableType=LINKED_TABLE` (legacy files may still say `TABLE_REFERENCE`; the plugin dual-reads both and re-saves as `LINKED_TABLE`): [source,xml] ---- hub_customer${PROJECT_HOME}/models/shared-core.hdvHUBhub_customerhub_customerLINKED_TABLE
hub_sales_repHUBsecondary_rep_hkhub_sales_rephub_secondary_repLINKED_TABLE
---- * `referencedModelFilename` — optional; empty means **same model**. * `name` — unique canvas name (may differ from `referencedTableName` for aliases). * `hashKeyFieldName` — role column used when the alias participates in a **link** (must differ from the physical hub hash column and from other roles). * Physical `tableName` is synced from the target hub; aliases never create a second hub table. Linked tables and aliases do not generate DDL or load pipelines. == Canvas workflow From the Data Vault canvas context menu: * **Add Linked Hub** / **Add Linked Link** / **Add Linked Satellite** — browse an external `.hdv` and pick a table. * **Add Hub alias** — pick a physical hub **in this model**, enter a unique alias name and a role hash key column (for example `secondary_rep_hk` or `to_party_hk`). * Drag relationships from local links or satellites to linked tables/aliases (same rules as local tables). Cards show `(linked)` for cross-model linked tables and `(alias)` for same-model role-playing aliases, plus the source model basename when external. == Navigate to the source table * **Click the table name** on a linked/alias card to open the owning model (or select the physical hub in the same model) and select the linked table. * Or use the table context menu action **Go to source table**. == Role-playing on links (issue #103) Data Vault 2.0 allows multiple foreign hash keys of the **same hub domain** on one link, distinguished by **role-named columns** (from/to location, employee/manager, primary/secondary rep). === Recommended canvas shape: natural hub + alias(es) Avoid leaving the physical hub as an orphan card that never participates in the link. Prefer: 1. Create and load the physical hub once (`hub_sales_rep`). 2. On the link, use the **physical hub for the primary / natural role** (column = the hub’s own hash key, e.g. `sales_rep_hk`, mapped from `primary_rep_id`). 3. Add **one hub alias per additional role** only (`hub_secondary_rep` → `secondary_rep_hk`, mapped from `secondary_rep_id`). 4. List participants as `hub_sales_rep`, `hub_secondary_rep` (and any other hubs), not the physical hub name twice. === Avoid * Two aliases of the same hub with **no** natural hub on the link (orphans the physical card and confuses ownership). * Reusing the same hash key column name for two roles. === Mapping and load * Link source mappings use the **canvas name** of the participant (alias name for extra roles). * DDL and load pipelines emit one column per role (`sales_rep_hk`, `secondary_rep_hk`, …). * Special records and optional FK constraints follow the same role columns. * Data Vault Update **skips** linked tables (no pipeline); only physical hubs/links/sats/reference tables load. == Validation and load order * Linked tables must resolve to a real non-linked table (local or external). * External models must not form circular linked-table chains. * Target database, hash algorithm, and hash key data type should match across models. * In a multi-file program, load **core** models before subject models that only hold linked tables to shared hubs. == Related * **Reference tables** (physical code tables) — distinct feature; not this document. * **Business Vault** — multi-model DV aliases and BV canvas pointers. See link:business-vault-sql-view.adoc[Business Vault SQL views and tables]. * **Enterprise split** — link:enterprise-modeling-and-team-collaboration.adoc[Organizing large Data Vault programs]. * **Links** — link:dv-link.adoc[Data Vault Link].

docs.content:
= Date Dimension Generator
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

The **Date Dimension Generator** transform produces a calendar date dimension as pipeline rows. It is an input transform (category **Input**) and appears in the transform palette with the calendar icon.

For each day between a configured **start date** and **end date** (inclusive), the transform emits one output row. Each output column is defined in a field table: you specify the field name, Hop data type, length, precision, a Java `DateTimeFormatter` pattern, and an optional locale. This makes it straightforward to populate a `dim_date` table (or role-playing date aliases) for Kimball star schemas modeled in link:dimensional-modeler-overview.adoc[the dimensional modeler].

The transform does not read upstream rows. Incoming hops, if present, are ignored.

== Prerequisites

* Apache Hop 2.19.0 or compatible (required by Data Hopper EDW).
* A target table (or downstream transforms) that accept the field layout you configure. The **Load defaults** button supplies a layout aligned with the standard `dim_date` attributes created by the dimensional modeler's date dimension template (`date_key`, `full_date`, `day_of_week`, and related calendar columns).

== Dialog overview

The transform dialog configures the date range, optional **reference date** and **fiscal offsets**, and the **Output fields** table. **Load defaults** fills the standard calendar field set and the default range `2000-01-01` through `2030-12-31`. **Add relative fields** and **Add fiscal fields** append optional packs without removing existing columns.

=== Date range and calendar options

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Transform name
|The name of this transform in the pipeline graph.

|Start date
|First calendar day to emit, in `yyyy-MM-dd` form. Variables are supported (for example `${DIM_DATE_START}`).

|End date
|Last calendar day to emit, inclusive, in `yyyy-MM-dd` form. Variables are supported.

|Reference date
|Optional “as of” date for relative attributes (`@rel_*`, `@ytd`, `@ytg`, `@rolling12`). Empty means the JVM local date at runtime. Variables are supported (for example `${LOAD_DATE}`).

|Day / week / month offset (fiscal)
|Integer offsets applied when evaluating fiscal tokens (`@fiscal_*`). For a July-start fiscal year, set **month offset** to `6` so July maps to fiscal month 1. Variables are supported.

|Load defaults
|Replaces the date range, clears offsets/reference, and replaces the field table with the built-in standard date dimension layout.

|Add relative fields
|Appends relative-to-reference columns (`day_rel`, `month_rel_label`, `is_ytd`, …) when missing.

|Add fiscal fields
|Appends fiscal calendar columns (`fiscal_year`, `fiscal_quarter`, …) when missing.

|Add load timestamp
|Appends a `Timestamp` field (`load_dt` in the transform dialog, or the dimensional model's load timestamp column on the Source tab) with mask `@now`. The value is the transform init time and is the same on every generated day. Rename the field when the target column uses another name (for example `x_load_ts`).
|===

The transform validates that the start date is not after the end date. An empty or unparseable date produces a configuration error at runtime.

=== Output fields

Each row in the **Output fields** table defines one column on the output stream.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Column |Description

|Field name
|Name of the output field added to the row stream.

|Type
|Hop data type (`Integer`, `String`, `Date`, `Boolean`, `Number`, `Timestamp`, and others from the type combo).

|Length
|Optional length for the Hop value metadata. Leave empty when not applicable.

|Precision
|Optional precision (mainly for `Number`). Leave empty when not applicable.

|Format mask
|Pattern used to derive the field value from the current calendar day. See <<format-masks,Format masks>> below.

|Locale
|Optional locale for localized names (for example `en_US`, `nl_NL`, `de_DE`). When empty, the JVM default locale is used. Locale affects patterns such as `MMMM` (month name) and `EEEE` (weekday name).
|===

Values are computed per day, then converted to the configured Hop type. For example, an `Integer` field with mask `d` stores the day-of-month as a number; a `String` field with mask `MMMM` and locale `nl_NL` stores the Dutch month name.

== Format masks

Format masks use Java `DateTimeFormatter` pattern letters unless noted as a special token below.

Common patterns for date dimensions:

[cols="2,1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Mask |Typical type |Produces

|`yyyyMMdd` |Integer |Surrogate date key (`20000101` for 2000-01-01). Optimized internally; does not round-trip through a string.

|`yyyy-MM-dd` |Date |Calendar date at start of day in the JVM default time zone.

|`@day_of_week` |Integer |ISO day of week: Monday = 1 through Sunday = 7.

|`d` |Integer |Day of month (1–31).

|`D` |Integer |Day of year (1–366).

|`w` |Integer |Week of week-based year.

|`M` |Integer |Month of year (1–12).

|`MMMM` |String |Full month name in the field's locale (`March`, `maart`, …).

|`Q` |Integer |Quarter of year (1–4).

|`yyyy` |Integer |Four-digit year.

|`@is_weekend` |Boolean |`true` on Saturday and Sunday, `false` otherwise.
|===

=== Special tokens

Some calendar attributes are easier to express as tokens than as formatter letters:

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Token |Behavior

|`@day_of_week`
|Integer ISO day of week (Monday = 1). Prefer this over the letter `u`, which in `DateTimeFormatter` means *year*, not day of week.

|`@is_weekend`
|Boolean weekend flag. Use with type `Boolean`.

|`yyyyMMdd` or `YYYYMMDD`
|Integer date key. Stored directly as `year * 10000 + month * 100 + day` for efficiency.

|`@fiscal_year` / `@fiscal_quarter` / `@fiscal_month` / `@fiscal_week` / `@fiscal_day_of_year`
|Fiscal calendar attributes computed on `row date + day/week/month offsets`. Civil `date_key` / `full_date` stay unshifted.

|`@rel_day` / `@rel_week` / `@rel_month` / `@rel_quarter` / `@rel_year`
|Integer distance from the reference date (`0` = same period as the reference).

|`@rel_label_day` / `@rel_label_week` / `@rel_label_month` / `@rel_label_quarter` / `@rel_label_year`
|Cognos-style labels such as `D`, `D-1`, `M+1`, `Y`.

|`@ytd` / `@ytg` / `@rolling12`
|Boolean flags: year-to-date (same year, on or before reference), year-to-go (same year after reference), and rolling 12 months ending at the reference (inclusive).

|`@now` or `@load_ts`
|Current timestamp captured once at transform init (not the calendar day). Use with type `Timestamp` (or `Date` / `String`) for warehouse load-audit columns. An empty mask on a `Timestamp` field is treated as `@now`.
|===

=== Hop conversion masks

Format masks drive *generation* only. They are **not** copied to Hop conversion masks on `Integer`, `String`, or `Boolean` fields. If they were, the Hop preview grid would prepend the mask to displayed values (for example `yyyyMMdd20000101` instead of `20000101`). Conversion masks are set only on `Date` and `Timestamp` fields so preview and downstream steps can render dates consistently.

== Default field layout

**Load defaults** configures the following fields (matching the dimensional modeler's standard `dim_date` attributes):

[cols="2,1,1,1,2,1", options="header"]
|===
|Field name |Type |Length |Precision |Format mask |Locale

|`date_key` |Integer |8 |0 |`yyyyMMdd` |

|`full_date` |Date | | |`yyyy-MM-dd` |

|`day_of_week` |Integer |1 |0 |`@day_of_week` |

|`day_of_month` |Integer |2 |0 |`d` |

|`day_of_year` |Integer |3 |0 |`D` |

|`week_of_year` |Integer |2 |0 |`w` |

|`month` |Integer |2 |0 |`M` |

|`month_name` |String |20 |0 |`MMMM` |`en_US`

|`quarter` |Integer |1 |0 |`Q` |

|`year` |Integer |4 |0 |`yyyy` |

|`is_weekend` |Boolean | | |`@is_weekend` |
|===

You can add, remove, or rename fields. Multiple string fields with different locales on the same pipeline are supported (for example `month_name_en` with `en_US` and `month_name_nl` with `nl_NL`, both using mask `MMMM`).

== Example: load `dim_date`

A typical pipeline to populate a warehouse date dimension:

1. **Date Dimension Generator** — set start/end dates for the calendar span you need; use **Load defaults** or customize the field table.
2. **Table output** (or **Insert / update**) — map output fields to the physical `d_date` (or `dim_date`) table on your warehouse connection.

For a 31-day range, the transform emits 31 rows with no upstream input. Connect only the generator's output hop to the loader.

=== Variables for rolling calendars

Use pipeline or workflow variables on the date range so the same pipeline can be reused:

* Start date: `${DIM_DATE_START}`
* End date: `${DIM_DATE_END}`

Set the variables before the pipeline runs, for example in a parent workflow or using the **Set variables** action.

=== Role-playing date dimensions

In link:dimensional-modeler-overview.adoc[the dimensional modeler], multiple fact date roles (order date, ship date, delivery date) often reference the same conformed `dim_date` table. Generate the calendar once, load it once, and join facts to `dim_date` on `date_key` for each role. The modeler can create role-playing aliases that point at the same physical table.

== Multilingual month and weekday names

Set **Locale** per field when the format mask includes localized text:

* `MMMM` — full month name
* `MMM` — abbreviated month name
* `EEEE` — full weekday name
* `EEE` — abbreviated weekday name

Example: two fields both named with mask `MMMM`, one with `en_US` and one with `nl_NL`, on the same row for `2024-03-15` yield `March` and `maart`.

Locale values use the usual language and country form (`en_US`, `fr_FR`). Underscores are accepted and normalized internally.

== Tips

* Use **Preview** on the transform to verify masks and locales before loading to the database. After fixing configuration, reload defaults if you still have the old `day_of_week` mask `u` (that letter formats the *year* in Java, not the day of week).
* Keep `date_key` as `Integer` with mask `yyyyMMdd` for integer join keys; use `full_date` as `Date` for human-readable reporting and date arithmetic in SQL.
* Narrow the start/end range during development to keep previews fast; widen for production loads (for example 20–30 years).
* In the dimensional modeler, choose **Source type = Date generator** on a dimension (or use **Add date dimension** on the canvas) to embed this transform in the generated load pipeline — no separate `.hpl` required for the standard calendar. The modeler Source tab mirrors these options (including **Preview data**); see link:dimensional-modeler-overview.adoc#date-dimension[Dimensional modeler — date dimension]. Type 1 date-dimension loads require the model load timestamp column on the source stream; the generator adds it automatically (`@now`) when it is missing from the field table.
* For holidays or bespoke attributes, keep using a **Pipeline** source with a custom `.hpl` that starts from this transform (or SQL).
* Boolean fields accept `@is_weekend` / `@ytd` / `@ytg` / `@rolling12` or formatted values parsed as `Y`/`N`, `true`/`false`, or `1`/`0` when you use a string-producing mask with type `Boolean`.

== Related documentation

* link:dimensional-modeler-overview.adoc[Dimensional modeler overview] — `dim_date`, date generator source, and star schema modeling
* link:record-definition-input.adoc[Get Record Definition Names] — catalog definition metadata as rows
* link:datavault-plugin.adoc[Data Vault plugin overview] — shared Hop GUI and workflow infrastructure

docs.content:
= Record Definition DDL
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 2

toc::[]

== Description

The **Record Definition DDL** transform (plugin id `RecordDefinitionDdl`) creates or updates database tables from catalog **record definitions**, including primary-key clauses. It is the catalog/CRM staging counterpart to model-driven vault DDL.

Typical pipeline:

. link:record-definition-input.adoc[Get Record Definition Names] (optionally with field metadata)
. **Record Definition DDL** — generate and/or execute `CREATE TABLE`

== Dialog

=== Source

Catalog connection, optional filter by namespace/name (fixed values or input fields).

=== Target

Optional override connection / schema / table when the catalog physical table ref should not be used.

**Target type mapping** (optional): a project link:target-type-mappings.adoc[Target type mapping] applied before Hop dialect types. Empty uses unique auto-match on the resolved target connection. Variables are allowed.

=== DDL

Execute on the database, drop-if-exists, skip-if-exists, semicolon, fail if no fields, output field names (`ddl`, `ddl_status`).

Catalog/CRM staging does **not** apply the vault SQL Server UTF-8 length ×3 policy. A matching target type rule still wins over Hop defaults.

== Related

* link:record-definition-input.adoc[Get Record Definition Names]
* link:target-type-mappings.adoc[Target type mappings]
* link:data-catalog.adoc[Data catalog]

docs.summary:
= Dimensional modeler overview
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

The dimensional modeler adds Kimball star/snowflake modeling to Data Hopper EDW. Models are saved as `.hdm` files and drive native Hop warehouse transforms for dimension and fact loads.

== Why a separate modeler

Data Vault and Kimb
docs.content:
= Dimensional modeler overview
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

The dimensional modeler adds Kimball star/snowflake modeling to Data Hopper EDW. Models are saved as `.hdm` files and drive native Hop warehouse transforms for dimension and fact loads.

== Why a separate modeler

Data Vault and Kimball semantics differ enough that they use separate model files:

* `.hdv` — hubs, links, satellites, hashing, insert-only history
* `.hdm` — dimensions, facts, bridges, grains, measures, SCD policies

The plugins share infrastructure (graph shell, ELK layout, orchestrator, workflow action pattern) but keep domain metadata separate.

== Dimensional model (`.hdm`)

A dimensional model contains:

* **Configuration** — target database, default standard column names (`dim_key`, `date_from`, `date_to`, …), pipeline naming, optional **Generate primary keys** / **Generate foreign keys** for CREATE TABLE DDL
* **Per-dimension surrogate keys** — optional override of strategy (none, auto-increment, source field such as a DV hash key) and column name; fact foreign key columns remain per join
* **Tables** — dimensions, facts, junk dimensions, bridges, factless facts, snapshot facts, aggregates
* **Conformed dimension registry** — logical name → physical dimension table
* **Notes** — canvas documentation only
* **Logical contracts** — source type **None (logical)** lets you sketch stars and field lists before staging SQL exists. Canvas cards show a **Logical** badge. **Check model** warns; **Dimensional Update** skips those tables until a load source is set.
* **Field documentation** — **Edit field...** on attributes, natural keys, measures, and degenerates stores a description plus Markdown **notes** and **requirements** (the old Excel mapping comments). Project documentation renders that Markdown.
* **Bus matrix** — facts carry Business / process level 1–3 from a **Business process catalog**. Open the crosstab from the resource definition group, EDW Journey, or **Tools → View bus matrix…**. See link:bus-matrix.adoc[Kimball bus matrix].
* **Fact presentation** — bind a link:semantic-layer.adoc[semantic layer] (`.hsl`) to this model and **Create presentation...**, or right-click a fact → **Create presentation…**. Pick groups, axes, and measures, then generate a Hopper crosstab against the target warehouse. See link:help/fact-crosstab-editor.adoc[crosstab editor].

Optional DDL constraints (both off by default):

* **Generate primary keys** — dimension and junk surrogate keys, and bridge composite keys, as `PRIMARY KEY` on CREATE TABLE. Fact tables do not receive a primary key in this release.
* **Generate foreign keys** — fact/bridge roles and dimension outriggers emit `FOREIGN KEY` clauses when the target engine supports them (not SingleStore). Parent dimensions receive a primary key when FK generation is enabled so references are valid. CREATE only; no ALTER retrofit.


Open a `.hdm` file in Hop GUI for the visual editor (same interaction model as the Data Vault canvas).

The retail example `retail-f-order-lines.hdm` shows a transaction fact with conformed dimension aliases and multiple date roles on one canvas:

image::images/dimensional-model-f-order-lines.png[Dimensional model — f_order_lines fact with conformed dimensions and date roles,align="center"]

=== Table types

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Type |Kimball role

|Dimension (`DmDimension`)
|SCD1, SCD2, or SCD3/hybrid dimension loads

|Fact (`DmFact`)
|Transaction fact with dimension roles and measures

|Junk dimension (`DmJunkDimension`)
|Low-cardinality flag combinations via Combination Lookup

|Bridge (`DmBridge`)
|Many-to-many resolution between two or more dimensions

|Factless fact (`DmFactlessFact`)
|Coverage/attendance pattern — dimension FKs only

|Periodic snapshot (`DmPeriodicSnapshotFact`)
|Grain includes snapshot period

|Accumulating snapshot (`DmAccumulatingSnapshotFact`)
|Milestone grain with row updates across a lifecycle

|Aggregate fact (`DmAggregateFact`)
|Pre-computed rollup from a base fact
|===

=== Staging sources

Each dimension or fact has a **Source** tab that defines how staging rows are obtained for generated load pipelines. Supported source types:

* **Database / SQL** — SQL executed by a generated `TableInput` (the traditional path)
* **Pipeline** — a Hop `.hpl` whose output is injected via MetaInject
* **Record definition** — a data catalog record definition
* **Date generator** — built-in calendar generation (dimensions; see below)

Model validation requires a complete source configuration for the selected type before running **Dimensional Update**.

[[date-dimension]]
==== Date dimension (`dim_date`)

For the standard calendar dimension:

* Canvas action **Add date dimension** creates `dim_date` / `d_date` with source type **Date generator**, default calendar fields, and TYPE1 attributes.
* On the **Source** tab, **Date generator** embeds the link:date-dimension-generator.adoc[Date Dimension Generator] in the generated Dimensional Update pipeline: start/end dates, optional reference date, fiscal day/week/month offsets, and a field table. No external `.hpl` is required for the standard calendar.
* Use **Load defaults**, **Add relative fields**, **Add fiscal fields**, and **Add load timestamp** to manage the output field pack; **Preview data** generates sample rows with the same logic as the transform.
* Type 1 loads need the model load timestamp column (for example `x_load_ts`) on the source stream. The date generator adds that field automatically as a `Timestamp` with mask `@now` when it is not already in the field table.
* Advanced customizations (holidays, bespoke SQL) can still use **Pipeline** or **SQL** sources.

The generator's **Load defaults** field pack matches the modeler template (`date_key`, `full_date`, `day_of_week`, and related columns). Optional relative and fiscal field packs support dynamic reporting filters (`month_rel = 0`, YTD) and fiscal calendars.

image::images/dimensional-model-date-dimension.png[Dimensional model — date dimension Source tab with Date generator,align="center"]

== Workflow integration

Production loads and DV-to-dimensional publish use workflow actions documented in link:dimensional-update-action.adoc[Dimensional Update and Publish actions].

== GUI workflows

=== Canvas context menu

Left-click the dimensional canvas background to:

* **Import database tables** — scaffold draft tables from an existing database schema
* **Add date dimension** — standard calendar `dim_date` with **Date generator** source (see <<date-dimension>>)
* Add dimension, fact, junk dimension, bridge, factless fact, or note

=== Data Vault canvas

From a `.hdv` model, use **Publish draft dimensional model** to create a draft `.hdm` via the same publish adapter as the workflow action.

== Pipeline generation strategy

Generators are thin builders over native Hop warehouse transforms:

[cols="2,2,3", options="header"]
|===
|Kimball pattern |Hop transform |Notes

|SCD Type 1 (all attributes Type 1) |Insert/Update |Overwrite attributes on natural key match

|SCD Type 2 (all attributes Type 2) |MergeRows chain (satellite pattern) |Ported from `DvSatellite` load-end-date chain

|Hybrid / Type 3 (mixed attribute policies) |Dimension Lookup (`update=true`) |Per-attribute update types; optional source→target rename; `is_current` via Last Version

|Junk dimension |Combination Lookup |Key field combinations → surrogate key

|Fact FK resolution |Dimension Lookup (`update=false`) |One lookup per dimension role. **Copies** on the join (empty = 1; variable expressions allowed) is the lookup transform's copies. Date-key joins use the same value on the generated date-key transforms.

|Bridge / factless / snapshots |Mix of above + TableOutput/InsertUpdate |Catalog-specific builders
|===

== Database import heuristics

**Import database tables** infers table type from naming:

* `d_*`, `dim_*` → dimension
* `f_*`, `fact_*` → fact
* `bridge_*` → bridge
* `factless_*`, `f_factless_*` → factless fact

Column heuristics:

* Skip standard warehouse columns (`dim_key`, `version`, `date_from`, …)
* `*_id` / `*_code` → natural key candidate on dimensions
* Integer `*_key` columns → dimension roles on facts/bridges/factless facts
* Numeric columns → measures on facts

Imported tables are **draft** metadata — review grains, roles, and source SQL before production loads.

== Test fixtures

[cols="2,3", options="header"]
|===
|Fixture |Purpose

|`integration-tests/tests/basic/basic-star.hdm`
|Minimal customer/product/sales star (SCD1 dims + transaction fact)

|`integration-tests/tests/basic/extended-catalog.hdm`
|Full Phase C catalog: SCD3, junk, bridge, factless, snapshots, aggregate

|`integration-tests/tests/basic/vault1.hdv` + publish
|DV → draft dimensional publish golden path
|===

Unit tests: `DmBasicStarPipelineTest`, `DmCatalogPipelineTest`, `DvToDimensionalPublishTest`, `DmDatabaseTableImportTest`, `DmGoldenFixtureTest`.

* link:getting-started-edw.adoc#after-first-load[Getting started — after the first load]
* link:getting-started-retail.adoc[Getting started — retail example]
* link:datavault-plugin.adoc[Data Vault plugin overview]

docs.content:
= Data Vault Link
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

A Link represents a relationship or association between Hubs. Examples include "Customer placed Order", "Product supplied by Supplier", "Employee assigned to Department", or any many-to-many connection you need to track.

The link table itself stores the hash keys of the participating hubs or hub aliases (role-named columns when the same physical hub appears more than once, and optional *dependent child keys* for transactional grain), its own surrogate link hash key, the record source, and the load date.

Links can also have their own satellites when the relationship carries descriptive attributes that change over time.

== Transactional links (dependent child keys)

A **standard link** stores a *distinct list of relationships*. The link hash is built from the participating hub hashes only. If the same customer buys the same product at the same store twice, the second load produces the same link hash and is not inserted again.

A **transactional link** (also called a non-historized link in Data Vault 2.0 literature) keeps *one row per event or transaction*, even when the hub combination repeats. You do this by defining one or more **dependent child keys** on the link — for example a measurement timestamp, transaction id, or order line number.

Those values are:

* Stored as columns on the link table
* Included in the link hash calculation together with the hub hashes (in the order you list them, after the hubs)

So each distinct dependent-child combination gets its own link hash key. Satellites attached to the link then parent on that event-level key.

*Dependent child keys* are not the same as *driving keys*:

* **Hub aliases (role-playing)** — same physical hub more than once on the link: natural hub for one role, alias for each extra role (from vs to, primary vs secondary). See link:dv-cross-model-references.adoc[Linked tables and hub aliases].
* **Dependent child keys** — making repeated occurrences of the *same* hubs unique (measurement every hour, sale line, sensor reading).

You can map any source column(s) as dependent child keys; the plugin does not hard-code timestamps versus ids.

Configure them on the link dialog **Dependent child keys** tab (target column name, source field, data type / length for DDL, optional description):

image::images/data-vault-link-table-with-dependent-child-keys.png[Link editor — Dependent child keys tab on lnk_order_line (line_number), with the retail model canvas behind the dialog,align="center"]

=== Retail worked example: order lines

In the link:getting-started-retail.adoc[retail example], **order lines** are modeled as a transactional link:

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Object |Role

|`hub_order`, `hub_product`
|Participating hubs

|`lnk_order_line`
|Link hash = order HK + product HK + **`line_number`** (dependent child key)

|`sat_lnk_order_line`
|Measures only (`quantity`, `unit_price`, `discount_pct`) — standard satellite parented by the event-level link key

|`E2E-order-line` / `order_line_*.csv`
|Source grain: one row per order line
|===

Why not a standard link? The same product can appear twice on one order (for example two promotions with different unit prices). Without `line_number` in the link hash, both lines collapse to one `lnk_order_line_hk`.

Teaching contrast in the same model:

* `lnk_order` — standard link (customer placed this order once)
* `lnk_order_line` — transactional link (this *line* of the order)
* `lnk_warehouse_product` — standard link + satellite (product stocked in warehouse; stock is relationship *state*)

== How link updates work

When a link is loaded, the generated pipeline:

* Reads the raw business key values (and any driving keys and dependent child keys) from the source attached to the link.
* Calculates the hub hash keys for each participating hub, using either the hub's own business key names or the explicit mappings you provided.
* Calculates the link's own hash key from the hub hashes and any dependent child key values (in list order).
* Compares the resulting link rows against what already exists in the target link table.
* Inserts only truly new link rows (new relationships, or new transactional events when dependent child keys are used).
* Adds the batch load date and record source value.

The comparison is done on the link hash key, so only new combinations of hubs (and dependent child keys when configured) are loaded.

If this feed can see a hub business key that is not yet in the parent hub, either add the feed as a hub record source (**Also load parent hubs...**) or set an orphan policy other than `PASS` on the model or this link. See link:datavault-configuration.adoc#_orphan_handling_tab[Orphan handling].

== Suggest hub source mappings

On the link dialog **Hub sources** tab:

. Add or select a Data Vault catalog source (for example a published **pipeline** feed such as `asn-package-lines`).
. Ensure **participating hubs** are listed on the Options tab (or leave empty to let suggest propose hubs fully covered by the feed).
. Click **Suggest mappings…**.
. Review proposed hub business key → source field maps (`exact` / `alias` / `missing`).
. Confirm to apply (only **empty** hub maps are filled; existing mappings are preserved).
. Use **Edit hub source mappings…** to adjust anything that did not match.

Matching uses the catalog field list for the selected source and the hub business-key names already on the model. This is especially helpful for multi-hub links fed by a flat pipeline or composite feed where most maps are identity renames.

Retail example: `lnk_package_line` on `retail-360.hdv` maps `asn-package-lines` into `hub_order`, `hub_product`, `hub_warehouse`, `hub_customer`, and `hub_package_line` via the same field names on the ASN package-line feed. `hub_package_line` is `asn_id` + `product_id` + `line_number`, because one ASN can repeat a product on another line.

== Options in the Link dialog

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Name
|Name of the link definition. Used as the default physical table name.

|Physical table name
|Actual table name in the target database.

|Description
|Business description of the relationship this link represents.

|Default record source
|The Data Vault Source that supplies the relationship rows. This source must contain the business key values (or foreign keys) needed to identify the participating hubs.

|Participating hubs
|The list of hubs (or **hub aliases**) that take part in this relationship. You need at least two. The order in the list is the order in which the hub hash columns will appear in the link table and is also the order used when calculating the link hash key.

Add hubs or hub aliases by selecting them from the available definitions in the model. To put the **same physical hub twice** on one link (primary/secondary rep, from/to location), keep the **physical hub as the natural first role** and add a **hub alias only for each extra role** — see link:dv-cross-model-references.adoc[Linked tables and hub aliases]. List e.g. `hub_sales_rep` then `hub_secondary_rep` (not the same hub name twice). The alias contributes a distinct role hash key column and its own source business-key mapping.

|Driving key names
|Legacy optional fields on the link dialog. **Do not use these for role-playing the same hub**; use hub aliases instead. Multi-active **satellite** driving keys (a different concept) are configured on the satellite.

|Dependent child keys
|Optional columns for transactional (non-historized) link grain. Each row has a target column name, optional source field name (defaults to the target name), data type / length for DDL, and optional description.

When set, these values are stored on the link and folded into the link hash after the participating hub hashes. Use them when the same hub combination must appear more than once (sensor readings, sales transactions, order lines, and similar event streams).

|Link hash key field name
|Name of the surrogate hash key column for the link itself. If you leave this empty, a name is derived from the link name (for example ORDER_CUSTOMER_LK).

|Hub source key fields
|This section lets you map the source columns that should be used to calculate each participating hub's hash key.

In many source systems the columns that identify a hub inside a relationship table have different names than the business keys in the hub's own source (for example customer_id in the customer hub source versus cust_fk or customer_id in an order source). When this happens, use the table in this section to tell the plugin exactly which source columns correspond to which hub's business keys.

For each participating hub you can enter source field mappings (in the same order as the hub's hash-input parts). **Multipartite** hubs: one source field per vault business key name. **Composite** hubs (single vault BK column): one row per *source part* with the same hub business key field name (order matters), or a multi-part mapping that expands to those parts. If you leave a mapping empty for a hub, the plugin falls back to the hub business key names (multipartite) or the hub's default source parts (composite). Links do **not** store hub business-key text — only hub hash keys (and optional dependent child keys).

This mapping capability is one of the most practical features when integrating real-world source systems that do not use identical column naming across tables.

|Has descriptive attributes (link satellite)
|Check this box as a reminder that you intend to attach a satellite to this link. The flag itself does not change how the link is loaded, but the model check will emit a note when it is set.

|Integration mode (Options tab)
|Same as hubs and satellites: **Hop managed**, **External read-only**, or **Custom pipelines**. See link:dv-integration-modes.adoc[Data Vault integration modes].
|===

Natural hub plus hub alias on one link (second role of the same physical hub):

image::images/data-vault-link-table-hub-alias.png[Link with natural hub participation and a hub alias for a second role of the same physical hub,align="center"]

== Checks related to links

Clicking **Check model** will flag issues such as:

* Fewer than two participating hubs are defined.
* No link hash key field name was supplied (a default will be used).
* Two participants resolve to the same hash key column name (use distinct role hash key fields on hub aliases).
* Dependent child keys are listed but a name (or resolvable source field) is missing, or the source field is not present on a link hub record source.
* A participating hub or hub alias does not resolve in the current model.
* The "Has descriptive attributes" flag is on (informational note).
* **Source-to-target type mismatches** for hub-key field mappings: each resolved source field (including every composite part) is validated against the source column and the corresponding hub business key definition.
* Composite hub business keys with the wrong number of mapped source parts on a link feed.

These checks run early and prevent many runtime surprises.

== Target table layout for links

The layout used for DDL and loading normally includes:

1. The link's own hash key column.
2. One column for each participating hub's hash key (in the order the hubs are listed in the link).
3. Dependent child key columns (if any), in the order defined on the link.
4. The record source column.
5. The load date column.

Driving key values may be stored when configured for role-playing. Dependent child keys are always materialised on the link when defined, because they are part of the link's identity and hash.

== Record source handling for links

The source query for a link includes the mapped business key fields, any driving keys, any dependent child key source fields, and the record source indicator (either a static value or a column from the source, depending on how you configured the Data Vault Source).

On the target side a NULL placeholder is used for the record source during the comparison step so that the actual record source value from the source leg can be passed through cleanly.

== Tips for links

* Define your hubs first. Links depend on them.
* When you have role-playing hubs (same hub used multiple times), always define driving keys so the relationships are unambiguous.
* When the same hubs can relate more than once (hourly sensor readings, repeated purchases, line items), add dependent child keys so each event gets its own link hash — do not rely on a link satellite alone to invent event identity under a single relationship hash.
* Use the Hub source key fields mapping whenever the column names in the relationship source differ from the hub business key names (or composite source parts). This is very common and saves a lot of source-side view or staging work.
* For composite hub BKs, map ordered source parts on the link feed; do not expect a composed vault BK column on the link table. See link:dv-hub.adoc#composite-hub-business-keys[Composite hub business keys].
* If the relationship itself has attributes that change (for example contract terms, status, effective dates), create a satellite on the link and check the "Has descriptive attributes" box as documentation. For pure event facts, you may still attach a satellite for measures; after dependent child keys are set, that satellite parents on the event-level link key.
* Keep the list of participating hubs in a consistent order across the model if you care about column ordering in the physical link tables.

docs.content:
= Data Vault integration modes
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

Every hub, link, and satellite in a `.hdv` model has an **integration mode** that controls how Hop treats the physical table in the warehouse.

To document an **entire** existing raw vault (Hop must not load or alter any table) use **Read-only existing vault** on the Data Vault configuration instead of setting External read-only on every card. See link:datavault-configuration.adoc[Data Vault configuration]. That flag refuses Data Vault Update, Generate DDL, and Debug, and model check keeps referential integrity only so Business Vault and dimensional models can sit on top. Per-table External read-only remains the mixed-ownership mode (Hop still runs Update and skips those tables).

Integration mode is set on the **Options** tab of the hub, link, or satellite dialog (combo: *Hop managed*, *External read-only*, *Custom pipelines*).

== Why integration modes exist

Real enterprises rarely have a single tool loading every raw vault table. Teams use dbt, hand-written SQL, legacy ETL, or bespoke Hop pipelines alongside model-driven loads.

Integration modes let all of those tables **participate in one Data Vault model** for:

* Visual lineage and documentation
* Model validation
* Business Vault and dimensional generation (metadata-driven)
* Data catalog publish
* Workflow orchestration (where applicable)

Downstream features read **metadata** (`getTargetTableLayout()`, table names, attributes) — not generated DV update pipelines.

== Modes

[cols="1,2,2", options="header"]
|===
|Mode |Hop behavior |Typical use

|Hop managed (default)
|Generates DDL, sentinel rows (hubs/links), and update pipelines. Data Vault Update runs generated `.hpl` files.
|Greenfield vault tables owned by Hop.

|External read-only
|Skips DDL, sentinels, and pipeline generation for this table. Data Vault Update logs and continues. Canvas label: `(ext)`.
|Tables loaded by dbt, SQL, or another ETL; Hop documents structure for BV.

|Custom pipelines
|Skips generated pipelines; Data Vault Update loads `.hpl` paths from `customUpdatePipelinePaths` and runs them in the orchestrator. Canvas label: `(custom)`.
|Hop-maintained loaders that do not match the generator pattern.
|===

== Data Vault Update behavior

For each table, `ActionDataVaultUpdate` branches on integration mode:

[cols="1,1,1,1", options="header"]
|===
|Phase |Hop managed |External read-only |Custom pipelines

|DDL generation
|Yes
|Skip
|Skip

|Sentinel rows (hub/link)
|Yes (if enabled)
|Skip
|Yes for hub/link if enabled

|Update pipelines
|`generateUpdatePipelines()`
|Skip (info log)
|Load `customUpdatePipelinePaths`

|Empty pipeline list
|Error
|OK
|Error if paths empty
|===

The parallel pipeline orchestrator runs both generated and custom pipelines the same way.

== Validation differences

[cols="1,1,1,1", options="header"]
|===
|Check |Hop managed |External read-only |Custom pipelines

|Record source required
|Yes
|Warning if missing
|Per custom pipeline

|Source field mapping
|Strict
|Relaxed
|N/A for generation

|Target table layout
|From sources
|Modeler must define columns
|From sources or overrides

|Physical table name
|Required
|Required
|Required
|===

External tables must still have accurate **attribute lists**, **hash keys**, and **table names** so Business Vault SQL and catalog publish are correct.

== Business Vault compatibility

`BvScd2PipelineSupport` reads satellite history with `TableInput` SQL built from DV metadata. It does **not** call DV update pipelines.

Therefore **external read-only** satellites work in Business Vault models as long as:

* The linked `.hdv` model has a **target database** configured
* Satellite tables exist in that database with the modeled layout
* Field mappings reference valid attribute names

See `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/customer-360-external.hdv` and `customer-360-external.hbv`.

== Custom pipeline paths

When mode is **Custom pipelines**, set `customUpdatePipelinePaths` on the table (list of `.hpl` files, variables allowed).

* Paths resolve relative to the Hop project / VFS like other file references
* Model check warns if paths are empty or files are missing
* Hubs with multiple record sources: one path list per table in v1; use multiple paths or separate tables if feeds need distinct pipelines

== Canvas indicators

The Data Vault model painter appends a suffix to table cards:

* `(ext)` — external read-only
* `(custom)` — custom pipelines

Hop-managed tables show no suffix.

In the Customer 360 external sample, every satellite shows `(ext)`:

image::images/data-vault-model-customer-360-external.png[Customer 360 Data Vault model with external read-only satellites,align="center"]

== Modeling guidelines

* Start new subject areas as **Hop managed** until loads stabilize
* Switch to **external read-only** when another tool owns DDL and loads but you want Hop BV / catalog / checks
* Use **custom pipelines** when you have proven Hop loaders that predate or extend the generator
* Keep one `.hdv` as the contract for both Hop and non-Hop consumers — avoid duplicate metadata in spreadsheets

docs.content:
= Data type mappings (pre-modeling sources)
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

== Why

Source systems rarely hand you EDW-grade types. Kafka, JSON, XML, CDC, and many files produce **String / Integer / Number without lengths** (or weak temporal typing). Downstream DDL then collapses to `TEXT` / `LONGTEXT` / CLOB, and load pipelines need ad-hoc **Select Values** transforms.

**Data type mappings** make pre-modeling **explicit**:

* Project-level **reusable policies** (metadata)
* Per-source **profile attach** + **field overrides** on the source model (`.hsm`)
* **Catalog** stores the **effective** layout (types, lengths, conversion masks, renames)
* **DV/BV/DM load pipelines** inject Select Values so runtime matches the contract

Fields remain “what the physical source produces.” Mappings remain “what the warehouse expects.”

See also: link:plans/data-type-mappings-plan.md[design plan], issue https://github.com/ProjectDataHopper/hopper-edw/issues/113[#113].

For **Hop type → native SQL type** on CREATE/ALTER, use link:target-type-mappings.adoc[Target type mappings] (issue https://github.com/ProjectDataHopper/hopper-edw/issues/127[#127]). Do not put dialect tokens such as `CHAR(1)` or `timestamptz` in a Data type mapping.

== Concepts

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Concept |Role

|**Data type mapping** (metadata)
|Named project profile with ordered **rules** (match + target type/length/conversion) and optional **scope** (source kinds, DB/path patterns).

|**Match criteria**
|Hop type, native/SQL type pattern, field name pattern, length absent / below / above.

|**Target**
|Hop type, length, precision, rename, conversion mask, decimal/grouping symbols, locale, time zone, lenient flags.

|**HSM binding**
|Each source table / query / JSON / pipeline card can attach one or more profiles (order matters) and field-level overrides.

|**Effective layout**
|Physical fields ⊕ profiles ⊕ overrides. Catalog publish and vault modelers use this only.

|**Model default profiles**
|On **Edit model**, set comma-separated default profile names applied to newly imported tables and new cards.
|===

=== Merge semantics

1. Within a profile: **first matching rule** establishes the base target for a field.
2. Across attached profiles (list order): **attribute-level merge** — later non-empty attributes override earlier ones.
3. Per-source **field overrides** always win last.

== Project metadata editor

In Hop **Metadata** perspective, under **EDW**, create a **Data type mapping** (key `data-type-mapping`).

The editor has **Name** / **Description**, then two tabs:

* **Scope** — multi-select source kinds (`DATABASE`, `CSV`, …) and optional connection / schema / path / namespace patterns (`TextVar`).
* **Rules** — ordered match → target grid (first match wins within the profile).

image::images/data-type-mapping-rules.png[Data type mapping metadata editor — Rules tab with match criteria and target conversion columns,align="center"]

Example **premodel-defaults** (also shipped under `retail-example/metadata/data-type-mapping/`):

* String + length absent → String length **2000**
* Field name `*_at` / `*_ts` + String → Timestamp + mask `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`

Rules without match criteria are rejected at validation. String → Date/Timestamp **without** a conversion mask is an **error**.

Use the **Help** button in the editor for the full column reference (scope patterns, masks, safety tips).

== Source model dialogs

Every source card dialog has a **Data type mapping** tab:

image::images/source-model-table-data-type-mapping.png[Source table dialog — Data type mapping tab with profiles, field overrides, and effective fields preview,align="center"]

. **Profiles** — comma-separated project mapping names (applied in order), with **Add** / **Select** / **Edit** buttons:
** **Add** — create a new Data type mapping profile and attach it.
** **Select** — multi-select existing project profiles (pre-selects currently attached names).
** **Edit** — edit the single attached profile, pick among attached profiles, or open the project picker when none are attached.
. **Field overrides** — fine-tune rename, type, length, mask, symbols, locale, time zone.
. **Effective fields** — read-only preview (**Refresh effective**).
. **Validate** — includes mapping safety checks (missing profiles, dangerous conversions, rename collisions).

Applies to:

* Source **table**
* Source **query**
* Source **JSON**
* Source **pipeline**

=== Edit model defaults

**Edit model** → **Default data type mappings**: comma-separated profile names. Used when:

* Importing schema tables
* Adding a new table / query / JSON / pipeline card that has no profiles yet

== Catalog publish

Publish (table / query / JSON / pipeline) writes the **effective** field list to the data catalog `DV_SOURCE`:

* Effective field **name** (after rename)
* Hop type, length, precision
* `inputOptions.conversion` (mask, locale, symbols, …)
* `sourceStreamName` when a rename maps a different physical/stream name

Modelers that “get attributes from source” therefore see pre-modeled types (e.g. `VARCHAR`-friendly length 2000 instead of unbounded text).

Harvest, catalog refresh, and **Validate resource definitions** rediscover **PIPELINE**, **JSON**, and **COMPOSITE** feeds through the same projection path as publish, including attached mapping profiles.

The catalog is a **second model**. Editing lengths or mappings on the `.hsm` card does not change vault loads or the schema gate until you **publish**. Source-model **Check model** / dialog **Validate** report a stale catalog feed; harvest findings for those source kinds say to republish rather than to widen hub/link keys to the last published length.

== Load pipelines

After the source read transform (database, file, JSON, composite, pipeline inject, …), generated DV loads call **apply catalog data type mappings**:

* Select Values transform name: `apply data type mappings`
* Applies length, conversion mask, and rename when present on catalog fields that are **on the incoming stream**
* Hub and link loads typically `SELECT` only relationship keys and alias the source indicator (`record_source AS x_record_source`). Satellite attributes on the same catalog feed (`stock_qty`, `order_status`, `quantity`, …) and source `load_date` are not mapped. The source-indicator mapping is applied to the **vault alias**. If the generated stream layout cannot be determined, mappings are skipped rather than applied to the full catalog.

No `.hsm` is required at generate/runtime once the catalog has been published.

== Validation summary

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Severity |Example

|ERROR
|String → Date/Timestamp without conversion mask; override references unknown field; duplicate target names; missing attached profile name

|WARNING
|String → Number without mask; length narrowing; PK type change; Boolean-ish conversions; temporal without locale/time zone

|OK
|Physical fields unchanged and no mapping configured (legacy behaviour)
|===

== Recommended workflow (large estates)

. Define org standards once as **Data type mapping** metadata (global + domain-specific profiles).
. Set **Default data type mappings** on each `.hsm` model.
. Import schema / add sources → profiles attach automatically.
. Fine-tune outliers on the **Data type mapping** tab.
. **Validate** and **Publish to catalog**.
. Build / refresh DV/BV/DM models from catalog; generate loads.

== Related

* link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[Source modeler overview]
* link:data-catalog.adoc[Data catalog]
* link:feature-overview.adoc[Feature overview]
