docs.content:
= Data Hopper EDW
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

**Data Hopper EDW** helps you design and load a Data Vault 2.0 data warehouse using Apache Hop — as one layer of a full EDW (catalog, source models, Business Vault, dimensional). Instead of writing many similar pipelines by hand, you create a visual model of your Hubs, Links, and Satellites. Hop then generates the pipelines needed to load data into those structures.

== What the plugin is for

Data Vault 2.0 is a modeling technique for building scalable, auditable enterprise data warehouses. It uses three main building blocks:

* **Hubs** – Core business concepts (Customer, Product, Order, etc.) identified by their natural business keys.
* **Links** – The relationships between Hubs.
* **Satellites** – The time-varying descriptive details that hang off Hubs and Links.

The plugin lets you capture this model once, together with the rules for hashing, naming, and loading. You can then:

* Visually design the model inside Hop GUI.
* Automatically generate and run the pipelines that keep the Data Vault up to date.
* Use a single workflow action to load an entire model in a controlled, repeatable way.

The generated load processes follow the standard Data Vault 2.0 "insert-only" approach:

* New business keys or relationships are added to Hubs and Links.
* For Satellites, a new row is added only when descriptive attributes actually change for a given parent key.
* Every row loaded in one run receives the same load date, making it easy to know what was processed together.

== Typical workflow

Recommended order (full walkthrough: link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]; pictures: link:architecture.adoc[Architecture]):

1. **Tools → Configure EDW setup...** (or the first-time prompt) — FILE catalog and shared source / DV / BV / DM configurations.
2. Model landing tables in a **source model** (`.hsm`): **Import schema**, draw relationships, then toolbar **Push to catalog**. Feeds become catalog `DV_SOURCE` / `COMPOSITE` / `JSON` / `PIPELINE` records under `hop/{project}/sources`.
3. **Generate Data Vault…** from the `.hsm` into a `.hdv` (review hubs, links, satellites). Prefer the shared **Data Vault configuration** on **Edit model**. **Check model**.
4. Create a **Resource definition group**, list the `.hdv` (BV/DM later), set the default catalog connection. See link:resource-definition-group.adoc[Resource definition group].
5. In a workflow, add **Update resource definition group**, enable **Update target database structure** and **Publish target tables to catalog**, and run. Single-model **Data Vault Update** remains available for one file.
6. Add a **Business Vault model** (`.hbv`) and dimensional models (`.hdm`) to the **same** group and update again.

You can still add hubs, links, and satellites by hand (or from the coach panel) instead of generating from the source model. **Generate DDL** and **Debug** on the `.hdv` toolbar preview CREATE/ALTER and a sample update pipeline without loading.

This approach gives you consistent, maintainable Data Vault loads that stay in sync with your model.

== Finding models and metadata (search)

With **Apache Hop 2.19**, project **Search Everywhere** includes this plugin’s model files and metadata:

* **Files:** `.hsm` (source), `.hdv` (raw vault), `.hbv` (business vault), `.hdm` (dimensional)
* **Content:** table and query names, physical names, notes, configuration strings, published feed names, resource-definition-group model paths, quality rule fields, and related settings
* **Open:** select a result to open the model (or metadata editor); model hits can jump to the matching table or source query on the canvas

Open editor tabs are searched from **in-memory** content so unsaved renames still match.

Full details: link:search.adoc[Project and metadata search].

image::images/search-dialog-finding-results-in-models.png[Search Everywhere finding a match inside a Data Vault model,align="center"]

image::images/search-panel-model-results.png[Search panel results for a model source field with canvas context,align="center"]

== Visual model editor

When you open a `.hdv` file you get a graphical editor comparable to the pipeline graph in Hop GUI.

image::images/data-vault-model-rendered.png[Data Vault model canvas with tables and annotation notes,align="center"]

=== Canvas interactions

The model editor follows the same touch-friendly interaction model as the rest of Hop GUI: **left-click context menus with icon actions**. There is no right-click menu and no double-click editing.

* **Drag** Hubs, Links, and Satellites to position them on the canvas (drag the table icon body, not the name).
* **Left-click the canvas background** to open the model context menu: Add Hub, Add Satellite, Add Link, Add note, Paste, Import sources, Edit model properties, and more.
* **Left-click a table icon** (the body of the card, not the name) to open the table context menu: Edit, Delete, Show update pipeline.
* **Left-click a table name** to open that table's properties dialog directly (the name is shown underlined on hover).
* **Left-click a note** to open the note context menu: Edit, Delete.
* **Drag relationships** from one table to another using the middle mouse button or Shift+left-click on a table icon, then drop on a valid target. Supported pairs are hub↔satellite, hub↔link, and link↔satellite. The model stores the relationship by updating the appropriate name references on the table objects.
* **Lasso-select** multiple objects; use the selection toolbar buttons or keyboard shortcuts to copy, cut, paste, or delete.
* **Annotation notes** document the model without affecting loads. Add a note from the canvas context menu, edit or delete from the note context menu, and drag the resize handles to change size. On Apache Hop **2.19+**, model notes reuse the same **CommonMark/GFM Markdown** canvas engine as pipeline and workflow notes (headings, emphasis, code, lists/task lists, tables, local images, horizontal rules). Pick a note type (General, Important, Warning, Information) for colors and accent icons. Links: `[Label](https://example.org)` opens a URL; relative paths to Hop-openable files (for example `.hpl` / `.hwf`) open in Hop Gui when resolvable from the model file; bare names such as `[Customer](hub_customer)` still navigate to a table in the model.

image::images/data-vault-model-note-dialog.png[Edit note dialog,align="center"]

Rendered like this:

image::images/data-vault-model-note-rendered.png[Data Vault model canvas with tables and annotation notes,align="center"]

=== Toolbar

The model editor toolbar provides the main operations:

image::images/hopgui-data-vault-model-toolbar.png[The data vault model toolbar in the Hop GUI,align="left"]


[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Button |Purpose

|Edit model
|Opens the model properties dialog (name, description, and all configuration tabs). See link:datavault-configuration.adoc#_edit_model_dialog[Data Vault Configuration].

|Import sources
|Imports database tables as new Data Vault Source metadata objects (connection, schema, and field layout).

|Check model
|Runs validation and shows results in a Hop check dialog (missing keys, broken references, duplicate names, source-to-target type compatibility, and more). Always uses detailed data type checking (live source schema where supported).

|AI Help
|Opens the Hop AI Assistant workbench bound to the open `.hdv` model for source analysis, type mapping, modeling advice, and troubleshooting. The assistant can propose model changes that you preview, validate, and selectively apply. See link:ai-advisory.md[AI advisory for Data Vault modeling] for details.

|Generate DDL
|Collects CREATE/ALTER statements for every table in the model against the configured target database and opens them in the SQL editor.

|Debug
|Generates update pipeline(s) for the selected table(s) and opens them in Hop for inspection or manual execution.

|Copy / Cut / Paste / Delete
|Clipboard operations for selected tables and notes (same pattern as pipeline graphs).

|Undo / Redo
|Snapshot-based undo/redo for model edits. The number of undo points kept in memory is configurable under Hop GUI → Configuration → Data Vault 2.0 (default 200).

|Zoom
|Zoom in, out, 100%, and fit-to-screen, plus a zoom level selector.
|===

=== Edit model and configuration

Click **Edit model** on the toolbar to open the model dialog. The **General** tab holds the model name and description; the remaining tabs edit the embedded configuration (target database, hashing, sentinel records, standard columns, target loading, and generated pipeline options).

image::images/data-vault-model-dialog.png[Edit Data Vault Model dialog — General tab,align="center"]

See link:datavault-configuration.adoc[Data Vault Configuration] for a full description of every setting and tab screenshot.

=== Check model and Debug

**Check model** runs the same validations used by the Data Vault Update action. It reports structural problems (missing business keys, unattached satellites, links with fewer than two hubs, duplicate names, references to sources or hubs that do not exist) and **source-to-target field type compatibility** before any load pipelines are generated.

==== Source-to-target type validation

For every mapped field the check compares the source column type to the target column type:

* **Hub** business keys (per record source on the hub)
* **Satellite** explicit attributes, auto-attributes (when no attribute list is defined), and driving keys
* **Link** hub-key mappings (`BusinessKeySource` entries)

Validation always uses **detailed data type checking** in the GUI: for database sources the plugin reads the live table schema. Stored `SourceField` metadata in the Data Vault Source is still used for target lengths and as a fallback when live resolution is unavailable.

Results use standard Hop check severities:

* **Error** — type mismatch; source string/binary length or numeric precision exceeds the target definition; target database is not Unicode-capable for EDW string storage when enforcement is enabled (SQL Server without a `_UTF8` collation, PostgreSQL non-UTF8 encoding, MySQL/SingleStore without `utf8mb4`; plain MySQL `utf8` is incomplete UTF-8). Snowflake VARCHAR is UTF-8 and is treated as capable without a collation probe. Enforcement is a global option under **Configuration → Data Vault 2.0** (default on; off softens to a warning for migrations). On **SQL Server**, length overflow is judged against the vault **UTF-8 byte capacity** (model character length ×3, matching generated `VARCHAR`), not the raw model number alone — so model length 50 (characters) is capacity 150, same as vault DDL.
* **Warning** — source length smaller than target (informational, character units); stored source metadata differs from the live schema (possible DDL drift); SQL Server physical type pairs that can sort differently in hub merge pipelines (for example source `NVARCHAR` vs target `VARCHAR`) — generated SQL auto-applies a bridge `COLLATE` on source and target ORDER BY when live metadata is available; vault `VARCHAR` uses a UTF-8 collation and expands character lengths to UTF-8 byte lengths (×3) so multi-byte data from `NVARCHAR` sources is not truncated
* **Comment** — fast-check mode notice, or live resolution skipped for non-database sources

The Data Vault Update action exposes the same validation with a **Detailed data type checking** checkbox on the Model tab (default: enabled). When model check logging is on, errors are written with `logError` and warnings with `logBasic`.

**Debug** generates the actual update pipeline(s) for the selected table(s) and opens them in Hop so you can review or run them manually. Use **Show update pipeline** from a table's context menu, or the toolbar **Debug** button when tables are selected. When the model defines a generated-pipeline folder, debug pipelines can be saved there as well.

== The Data Vault Update action

For production use you normally drive loads from a workflow using the **Data Vault Update** action. It:

* Loads the model from the `.hdv` file.
* Optionally runs the same model checks that the visual editor uses (with optional detailed data type checking).
* Can be configured to log issues or abort if errors are found (check errors are logged with `logError`).
* Optionally ensures unknown and invalid sentinel rows exist in hubs and links before loading.
* Generates CREATE/ALTER DDL for the single target database when schema changes are needed.
* Generates an update pipeline for every table in the model (optionally filtered by record source group).
* Stages generated pipelines and runs them through a parallel orchestrator (`parallelPipelineCopies`, optional staging folder).
* Runs all pipelines using the pipeline run configuration you specify.
* Uses one consistent load date for the entire batch.
* Collects row counts and error information from the generated pipelines.

image::images/action-data-vault-update.png[Data Vault Update action dialog,align="center"]

See link:datavault-update-action.adoc[Data Vault Update Action] for all options and tab descriptions.

== What you can configure

Each Data Vault Model embeds a **configuration** object that controls:

* Which database the Data Vault lives in (one target database per model).
* Hash algorithm (MD5, SHA-256, etc.) and how hash keys are stored (HEX by default; BINARY is compact and fully supported on Hop **2.19.0+** — see https://github.com/apache/hop/issues/7346[issue 7346]).
* Names for standard columns such as LOAD_DATE and RECORD_SOURCE.
* Whether business keys should be trimmed and upper-cased before hashing.
* A placeholder to use for NULL values during hashing.
* Unknown and invalid sentinel record generation and values.
* Target table batch size and optional folder/prefix settings for generated pipelines.

Most hashing and naming settings apply model-wide. Individual hubs, links, and satellites can still override specific column names (for example the hash key field name or record source field name on a hub) where the dialog provides that option.

== Sources

Before you can load a Hub, Link, or Satellite you need **Data Vault Source** metadata that describes where the data comes from and how rows should be tagged with a record source value.

* A Data Vault Source gives the feed a logical name, optional static or column-based record source indicator, and an optional **group** tag used to filter which sources are processed in a given workflow run.
* For database feeds, the source editor includes a **Database** tab with the connection, schema, table, and field layout (including primary-key flags). Physical source details are embedded in the Data Vault Source rather than maintained as a separate metadata type.

The Import button (in the source editor and on the model toolbar) can read the live column list from a database, which saves typing and helps ensure lengths and types are accurate.

Hubs have a dedicated **Record sources** tab where you attach multiple sources to a single hub table. Business keys on the hub can be tagged with a Source system so each source can use its own column names. Links and satellites reference a single default record source.

See link:datavault-source.adoc[Data Vault Source] and link:datavault-source-database.adoc[Database source details].

== Hubs, Links, and Satellites

Each definition has its own dialog with the fields relevant for that type:

* **Hubs** need one or more business keys and one or more record sources. Use **Load from source** on the Keys tab to pull business keys from a chosen source.
* **Satellites** attach to a Hub or a Link. Use **Load from source** on the Attributes tab to populate the attribute list from the source.
* **Links** connect two or more Hubs, with optional driving keys (role-playing), optional dependent child keys (transactional / non-historized grain), and explicit hub source key field mappings when column names differ from the hub definitions.

See link:dv-hub.adoc[Hubs], link:dv-link.adoc[Links], and link:dv-satellite.adoc[Satellites] for field-level reference.

== Plugin-wide GUI options

Under **Hop GUI → Configuration → Data Vault 2.0** you can set options that apply across all open models:

image::images/hopgui-configuration-perspecive-data-vault-options.png[Data Vault 2.0 options in the Hop configuration perspective,align="center"]

* **Draw hash keys in model** – When enabled, hash key column names are shown on table cards in the visual editor.
* **Remind to publish catalog feeds when saving a source model** – When enabled (default), saving a `.hsm` whose published catalog feeds lag the canvas asks whether to publish them. The dialog has **Don't remind me after save**; you can turn the option back on here.
* **Maximum undo/redo operations kept in memory** – Size of the snapshot undo stack for `.hdv` files (default 200).

== Business Vault

Business Vault models (`.hbv` files) build consumption-layer tables from raw Data Vault satellite history. The primary table type today is **functional SCD Type 2**: attribute timelines with `valid_from` / `valid_to` (or your column names) derived from a configurable functional timestamp, not only the technical load date.

* Link each `.hbv` file to a `.hdv` Data Vault model.
* Define SCD2 tables with one or more satellite derivatives.
* For multi-satellite merges (e.g. Customer 360), provide explicit field mappings and per-satellite configs.
* Use **Debug** / **Show build pipeline** to inspect generated pipelines; use the **Business Vault Update** workflow action for production rebuilds.

See link:business-vault-overview.adoc[Business Vault overview], link:business-vault-scd2.adoc[Business Vault SCD2], and link:business-vault-update-action.adoc[Business Vault Update action].

image::images/data-vault-model-customer-360.png[Customer 360 Data Vault model,align="center"]

image::images/business-vault-model-customer-360.png[Customer 360 Business Vault model,align="center"]

PIT tables are also modeled in `.hbv` files; pipeline generation uses the PIT prefix from Business Vault configuration.

== Integration modes

Hubs, links, and satellites can be **Hop managed** (default), **External read-only**, or **Custom pipelines**. External tables participate in Business Vault and catalog publish without Hop-generated DDL or update pipelines.

See link:dv-integration-modes.adoc[Data Vault integration modes].

image::images/data-vault-model-customer-360-external.png[External read-only satellites on the Data Vault canvas,align="center"]

== AI advisory

The **AI Help** toolbar button opens the Hop AI Assistant workbench bound to the vault model for source analysis, modeling suggestions, layout proposals, and troubleshooting. Proposals can be reviewed and applied selectively.

See link:ai-advisory.md[Data Vault AI Help and advisory].

== Getting started

Build from scratch: link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]. Tour the finished sample: link:getting-started-retail.adoc[Getting started — retail example]. Advanced fixtures: link:getting-started-integration-tests.adoc[integration test fixtures].

image::images/data-vault-model-retail-example.png[Retail example Data Vault model — customer, order, product, and warehouse entities,align="center"]

With an execution metrics profile and OPS database, the model canvas can show recent load durations per table:

image::images/data-vault-retail-360-model-with-duration-metrics.png[Retail 360 Data Vault model with load duration overview pane,align="center"]

Executives and architects can review link:presentations/hop-data-vault-overview.md[Data Hopper EDW overview slides].

== Current capabilities

Today the plugin supports:

*Raw Data Vault*

* Composite business keys and multi-active satellites.
* Role-playing hubs in links via driving keys.
* Transactional (non-historized) links via dependent child keys included in the link hash.
* Explicit source-to-hub key mappings for links.
* Static or column-based record source indicators and record source groups for partial loads.
* Unknown and invalid sentinel rows in hubs and links.
* Load end date and status tracking satellite patterns.
* Integration modes: Hop managed, external read-only, custom pipelines.
* Choice of hash algorithm and hash key storage format.
* Automatic creation or alteration of target tables (DDL) before loading.
* Model validation that catches structural problems and source-to-target type mismatches before you run a load.
* Parallel staged pipeline execution for faster multi-table updates.
* Visual debugging, DDL preview, clipboard editing, undo/redo, and production execution via workflow actions.
* Canvas annotation notes with typed styling and in-model navigation links.

*Business Vault*

* `.hbv` visual modeler linked to `.hdv` models.
* SCD2 build pipeline generation (single- and multi-satellite).
* PIT table type and Business Vault Update workflow action.
* Navigate from BV to DV tables in Hop GUI.

*Tooling*

* Data catalog integration and optional publish after DV/BV updates.
* AI advisory with review-before-apply proposals.
* **Project / Search Everywhere** (Hop 2.19): search `.hsm`, `.hdv`, `.hbv`, and `.hdm` content and plugin metadata (resource definition groups, catalog connections, metrics profiles, quality rule sets). See link:search.adoc[Project and metadata search].
* Architecture export, OpenLineage / Marquez export, execution maps, and multi-layer **Update resource definition group** loads.

Future work may deepen catalog record-definition search and further source-system modeling convenience.

If you are new to Data Vault 2.0, the plugin encourages good practices by making the key decisions (hashing, naming, source tracking, change detection) explicit and reusable through the model configuration and source metadata objects.

docs.content:
= Business Vault PIT
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

Point-in-time (PIT) tables accelerate **as-of** queries against raw Data Vault hub and satellite history. For each snapshot timestamp and hub grain key, the plugin stores the load timestamp of the satellite row that was effective at that moment.

PIT tables live in the **Business Vault** (`.hbv`) model alongside SCD2 tables. They read **raw** hub and satellite tables on the Data Vault target database and write the PIT table to the Business Vault target database. A **source query** can replace the satellite (same connection as the Data Vault target); the hub remains a DV alias. Cross-database PIT is not supported because the generated SQL joins hub and satellite in one statement.

== What PIT solves

Reporting and marts often need attribute values **as they were known at time T** (technical as-of). Without a PIT table, every query repeats effective-dating logic: for each hub key, find the latest satellite load timestamp `≤ T`, then join back to the satellite.

A PIT table materializes that lookup once:

* One row per `(hub_hash_key, snapshot_date)`
* One **pointer column** per participating satellite (default suffix `_ldts`) holding the load timestamp to join on

Consumers resolve attributes with a simple equi-join:

[source,sql]
----
SELECT pit.snapshot_date, sat.*
FROM pit_customer pit
JOIN sat_customer sat
  ON sat.customer_hk = pit.customer_hk
 AND sat.x_load_ts = pit.sat_customer_ldts
WHERE pit.snapshot_date = :as_of_timestamp
----

PIT complements SCD2: SCD2 collapses history into functional `valid_from` / `valid_to` intervals; PIT preserves **technical** as-of against raw satellite load timestamps.

== Relationship to raw vault and SCD2

image::images/diagrams/bv-pit-scd2.svg[PIT reads raw hub and satellite history; SCD2 is an independent sibling,align="center"]

PlantUML source: link:diagrams/bv-pit-scd2.puml[bv-pit-scd2.puml].

* PIT reads **raw** hub/satellite history — not SCD2 output
* SCD2 and PIT are independent siblings in the same Business Vault Update run (SCD2 tables run first, then PIT)

== Target table layout

For each PIT table the plugin creates:

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Column |Source

|Hub hash key
|From the hub derivative (e.g. `customer_hk`)

|`snapshot_date` (configurable)
|Snapshot timestamp on the spine (default column name `snapshot_date`)

|`{satellite_table}_ldts` per satellite
|Load timestamp pointer for that satellite at the snapshot (suffix configurable, default `_ldts`)
|===

Example: `pit_customer` with hub `hub_customer` and satellite `sat_customer` → `customer_hk`, `snapshot_date`, `sat_customer_ldts`.

== Snapshot schedule

Schedule settings are stored inline on `BvPitTable` (nested `BvPitSnapshotSchedule` in the `.hbv` XML).

=== Cadence and anchor

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Setting |Description

|Cadence
|`DAILY`, `WEEKLY`, or `MONTHLY`. **MVP:** only `DAILY` is implemented in pipeline generation; other cadences validate but emit a warning and fail at generation time.

|Snapshot anchor
|`END_OF_PERIOD` (e.g. daily at `23:59:59`) or `START_OF_PERIOD` (midnight). Default `END_OF_PERIOD`.
|===

=== Horizon

|Horizon days|Skips the most recent N calendar days when resolving the spine end date (late-arriving data buffer). Default `1`.

When range end is `NOW_MINUS_HORIZON`, the effective end date is `today − horizonDays`.

=== Range start and end

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Range start |Resolves the first snapshot date on the spine

|`FIXED_DATE`
|Use `rangeStartFixed` (ISO date, e.g. `2024-01-31`)

|`EARLIEST_PARTICIPATING_SATELLITE_LOAD` (default)
|Minimum load date across listed satellite derivatives

|`EARLIEST_HUB_LOAD`
|Minimum load date on the hub table
|===

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Range end |Resolves the last snapshot date on the spine

|`NOW`
|Current date (subject to anchor time-of-day)

|`FIXED_DATE`
|Use `rangeEndFixed` (ISO date)

|`NOW_MINUS_HORIZON` (default)
|Current date minus `horizonDays`
|===

=== Incremental loads

When the PIT target table already exists, the build pipeline appends only rows where `snapshot_date` is greater than the watermark from the BV table. At pipeline generation the plugin queries the **Business Vault** connection for `MAX(snapshot_date)` (null → sentinel in Java), puts the value in a `param_snapshot_watermark` **Generate Rows** transform (limit 1), and binds it into the DV-connected `TableInput` as a JDBC positional parameter (`spine.snapshot_date > ?`). That keeps DV and BV databases separated and SQL dialect-neutral. Re-runs are idempotent for dates already loaded.

== What gets generated

For each PIT table the plugin builds a Hop pipeline that:

1. Resolves the incremental watermark against the BV PIT table (when present)
2. Resolves snapshot spine bounds from the schedule (and optional MIN load queries on DV tables)
3. Generates daily snapshot timestamps via Postgres `generate_series` (end-of-day or start-of-day per anchor)
4. Cross-joins hub distinct hash keys with the snapshot spine
5. For each `(hash_key, snapshot_date)`, selects the latest satellite load timestamp `≤ snapshot_date` (insert-only satellites)
6. Filters to snapshot dates after the resolved watermark (incremental append)
7. Loads the Business Vault target table with `TableOutput` (append mode)

The pipeline is a single `TableInput` (SQL on the **Data Vault** connection) → `TableOutput` (on the **Business Vault** connection).

Use **Debug** or **Show build pipeline** on a PIT table in the `.hbv` editor to inspect the generated SQL before running a workflow.

== PIT table dialog (key fields)

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Field |Description

|Name
|Logical name of the PIT table in the `.hbv` model.

|Physical table name
|Target table in the Business Vault database.

|Derivatives
|Exactly one **hub** and one or more **satellite** references. MVP pipeline generation supports **one satellite** only.

|Snapshot date field
|Output column name for snapshot timestamps (default `snapshot_date`).

|Cadence / anchor / horizon
|Snapshot spine calendar settings (see above).

|Range start / range end
|How the spine bounds are resolved, with optional fixed dates.

|Satellite pointer suffix
|Suffix appended to each satellite table name for pointer columns (default `_ldts`).
|===

== Validation

**Check model** on the `.hbv` file validates PIT tables:

* Snapshot date field is non-empty
* Exactly one hub derivative; at least one satellite derivative
* Each satellite's parent hub matches the PIT hub derivative
* Data Vault and Business Vault target database connections resolve
* Non-daily cadence → warning (not yet implemented in pipelines)
* Optional INFO when the hub has satellites not listed on the PIT table

Multi-satellite PIT tables (more than one satellite derivative) fail at **pipeline generation** in MVP.

== Target databases

PIT pipeline generation requires:

* **Data Vault target database** — on the linked `.hdv` configuration (read hub and satellite history)
* **Business Vault target database** — on the `.hbv` configuration (write PIT table)

Both connection names must resolve in Hop project metadata. Generated SQL is dialect-aware: **PostgreSQL** (`generate_series`), **SQL Server**, **MySQL**, **SingleStore**, and **Snowflake** (`GENERATOR` + `DATEADD`, `TIMESTAMP_NTZ`).

If you change the linked `.hdv` file on disk, use **Reload DV model** on the Business Vault toolbar before generating pipelines.

== Single-satellite example (vault1)

`integration-tests/tests/basic/vault1.hbv` defines:

* `sat_customer_hb` — SCD2 from `sat_customer`
* `pit_customer` — PIT from `hub_customer` + `sat_customer`

The PIT table uses a **fixed date range** (`2024-01-31` → `2024-02-01`) for deterministic golden tests in CI. Production models typically use `EARLIEST_PARTICIPATING_SATELLITE_LOAD` and `NOW_MINUS_HORIZON`.

Workflow: `integration-tests/tests/basic/update-vault1.hwf` loads the raw vault, runs Business Vault Update (SCD2 then PIT), and validates with `validate-pit-customer.hpl` against `integration-tests/datasets/basic/pit-customer-golden.csv`.

== Running loads

* **Debug** — generate and open the PIT build pipeline in Hop GUI
* **Business Vault Update** — model check, optional DDL, generate, stage, and execute build pipelines

PIT tables run **after** all SCD2 tables in the same Business Vault Update action. See link:business-vault-update-action.adoc[Business Vault Update Action].

== MVP limits and roadmap

Current MVP scope:

* Hub PIT with **one satellite** derivative
* **Daily** cadence only in generated pipelines
* Insert-only satellites (latest load `≤ snapshot_date`; no load-end-date satellites)
* Incremental append by `MAX(snapshot_date)`
* Pointer columns: `{satellite_table_name}{suffix}` (default `_ldts`)
* Postgres-oriented SQL in `TableInput`

Planned follow-on phases:

* **PIT-2** — weekly/monthly cadence, multi-satellite PIT (one pointer column per sat)
* **PIT-3** — load-end-date satellites, link PIT
* **PIT-4** — range start `EARLIEST_SCD2_TABLE_LOAD`, dedicated PIT schedule dialog

Out of scope: raw-vault `DvPit` in `.hdv`, auto-PIT for every hub. Business Vault **bridge** tables are a separate canvas type; see link:business-vault-bridge.adoc[Business Vault bridge].

== GitHub issue #26

https://github.com/ProjectDataHopper/hopper-edw/issues/26[Issue #26] originally proposed `DvPit` metadata in the raw Data Vault model (`.hdv`) and execution via Data Vault Update.

**Resolution:** PIT is implemented in the **Business Vault** layer as `BvPitTable` in `.hbv` files, with build pipelines and Business Vault Update execution. Raw `.hdv` models stay focused on ingest; PIT accelerates consumption-layer as-of queries alongside SCD2.

Suggested issue comment when closing or rewriting #26:

[quote]
____
Implemented as Business Vault PIT (`BvPitTable` in `.hbv`), not raw-vault `DvPit`.

* Documentation: link:business-vault-pit.adoc[business-vault-pit] (and link:business-vault-overview.adoc[business-vault-overview])
* MVP: hub + one satellite, daily EOD snapshots, incremental append, Postgres SQL
* Sample: `integration-tests/tests/basic/vault1.hbv` → `pit_customer`, validated by `update-vault1.hwf`
* Execution: Business Vault Update runs SCD2 tables first, then PIT tables

Raw-vault PIT is superseded by this BV approach. Remaining work (weekly/monthly, multi-satellite, link PIT) is tracked in the doc roadmap section.
____

docs.content:
= Getting started — integration test fixtures
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

**Reference walkthrough** for advanced Data Vault and Business Vault patterns in the `integration-tests/` project: multi-satellite Customer 360, external read-only raw vault tables, and golden-dataset regression suites.

To **build** an EDW from scratch, start with link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]. To **tour** the finished retail sample (CSV → DV → BV → dimensional), see link:getting-started-retail.adoc[Getting started — retail example].

Estimated time: half a day with Hop GUI, or follow along read-only first.

== Prerequisites

. Register `integration-tests/` as a Hop project named **`hopper-edw`**.
. Configure database connections **`CRM`** and **`Vault`** in project metadata (`metadata/rdbms/CRM.json`, `metadata/rdbms/Vault.json`).
. Install **Data Hopper EDW** plugin in Apache Hop **2.20.0-SNAPSHOT**.
. Open the project in Hop GUI so `${PROJECT_HOME}` resolves.

Full environment details: link:../integration-tests/PROJECT.md[Integration tests Hop project].

== Chapter 1 — Data Vault concepts

Data Vault 2.0 uses three building blocks:

* **Hub** — a core business entity (Customer, Product) identified by business keys
* **Link** — a relationship between hubs
* **Satellite** — descriptive history attached to a hub or link; insert-only when attributes change

**Record sources** in the Data Catalog describe where staging data lives (connection, table, columns, record-source indicator).

The plugin stores hubs, links, and satellites in a **Data Vault model** (`.hdv` file) with embedded configuration (hashing, target database, column names).

== Chapter 2 — Explore sources and the basic model

. In Hop GUI, open `integration-tests/tests/basic/vault1.hdv`.
. Click **Edit model** and note the **target database** (`Vault`) and hashing settings.
. Inspect hubs, links, and satellites on the canvas.
. Open a hub dialog — review business keys and **Record sources**.

Sources for this model live in the data catalog under `catalog-data/hop/integration-tests/sources/` (CRM-customer, CRM-order, etc.).

Optional: run `integration-tests/run-tests.sh tests/basic/update-vault1.hwf` from the command line to see a full load without using the GUI.

== Chapter 3 — Validate and inspect pipelines

On the `vault1.hdv` toolbar:

. Click **Check model** — fix any errors before continuing.
. Click **Generate DDL** — preview CREATE/ALTER for the Vault database.
. Select `sat_customer`, then **Debug** (or **Show update pipeline**) — inspect the generated insert-only satellite pipeline.

The same generation logic runs in the **Data Vault Update** workflow action.

Reference: link:datavault-plugin.adoc[Plugin overview], link:datavault-update-action.adoc[Data Vault Update action].

== Chapter 4 — Run a raw vault load

. Open workflow `integration-tests/tests/basic/update-vault1.hwf`.
. Run it (or run via `integration-tests/run-tests.sh`).

The workflow creates CRM tables, loads CSVs, drops vault tables, runs Data Vault Update twice (initial + incremental), and validates against golden datasets.

You now have raw satellite **history** in the Vault database — the input for Business Vault.

== Chapter 5 — Introduce Business Vault (single satellite)

. Open `integration-tests/tests/basic/vault1.hbv`.
. Note **Data Vault model file** → `${PROJECT_HOME}/tests/basic/vault1.hdv`.
. Open the SCD2 table `sat_customer_hb` — it references satellite `sat_customer`.
. Click **Edit model** on the BV toolbar — target database, valid from/to defaults, sentinels.
. **Check model**, then **Show build pipeline** on the SCD2 table.

This is the simplest BV pattern: one satellite → one functional SCD2 table.

Reference: link:business-vault-overview.adoc[Business Vault overview], link:business-vault-scd2.adoc[Business Vault SCD2].

== Chapter 6 — Multi-satellite Customer 360

. Open `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/customer-360.hdv` — one hub, four satellites.

image::images/data-vault-model-customer-360.png[Customer 360 Data Vault model — hub and four satellites,align="center"]

. Open `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/customer-360.hbv`.

image::images/business-vault-model-customer-360.png[Customer 360 Business Vault model — customer_360_bv SCD2 table,align="center"]

. Open SCD2 table `customer_360_bv`:
** **Derivatives** — four satellites
** **Field mappings** — rename attributes to `cust_*` columns
** **Satellite configs** — per-satellite functional timestamp / source indicator

image::images/business-vault-scd2-table-dialog.png[SCD2 table dialog — General tab with derivatives,align="center"]

image::images/business-vault-scd2-table-dialog-field-mappings.png[SCD2 table dialog — Field mappings tab,align="center"]

image::images/business-vault-scd2-table-dialog-satellite-settings.png[SCD2 table dialog — Satellite settings tab,align="center"]

. **Check model** — multi-satellite rules require explicit mappings.
. **Reload DV model** (toolbar) if you edited the `.hdv` on disk.
. **Show build pipeline** — expect multiple `TableInput` branches, `SortedSchemaMerge`, `RepeatFields`, analytic validity, `TableOutput`.

Run `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/update-customer-360.hwf` for end-to-end DV load + BV rebuild + validation.

For incremental SCD2, open `customer-360-incremental.hbv` (same mappings, `buildMode=INCREMENTAL`) and run `update-customer-360-incremental.hwf`. That workflow runs the same DV load waves, then **Business Vault Update** with the incremental pipeline, and validates against the same golden current-state dataset.

For a large-table Full rebuild split, open `customer-360-partitioned.hbv` (`hashKeyPartitionCount=4`) and run `update-customer-360-partitioned.hwf`. Same golden current-state dataset; the target is truncated once, then four hash-key slices are loaded.

== Chapter 7 — External read-only raw vault tables

When dbt or another tool loads raw vault tables, Hop can still model them for Business Vault.

. Open `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/customer-360-external.hdv`.
. Open each satellite dialog → **Options** tab → **Integration mode** = *External read-only*.
. Canvas shows `(ext)` on those tables.

image::images/data-vault-model-customer-360-external.png[Customer 360 external Data Vault model — satellites marked ext,align="center"]
. Open `customer-360-external.hbv` — same BV SCD2 definition as the hop-managed variant.
. **Check model** and **Show build pipeline** — BV reads satellite history from the Vault database using metadata only; Data Vault Update skips DDL/pipelines for external tables.

Reference: link:dv-integration-modes.adoc[Data Vault integration modes].

== Chapter 8 — Production workflow pattern

Typical batch:

1. **Data Vault Update** on `.hdv` — load raw vault (skip external tables automatically)
2. **Business Vault Update** on `.hbv` — rebuild SCD2 tables

Configure pipeline run configuration, parallel copies, optional DDL and catalog publish on each action.

Reference: link:business-vault-update-action.adoc[Business Vault Update action].

== Chapter 9 — Troubleshooting

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Symptom |What to check

|Cannot load linked `.hdv`
|`${PROJECT_HOME}` set; path on `.hbv` correct; use **Reload DV model**

|SCD2 pipeline: target database required
|Vault connection in project metadata; **target database** on both `.hdv` and `.hbv`; run **Check model**

|Validation passes but pipeline fails
|Reload DV model before generate; stale cache was a common cause

|External satellite empty in BV
|Warehouse table must exist and match modeled attributes; Vault connection must read it

|Type check errors on hub/satellite
|Run **Check model** with detailed type checking; align source catalog with live CRM schema
|===

== Chapter 10 — Next steps

[cols="1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Topic |Document

|Primary tutorial (retail)
|link:getting-started-retail.adoc[getting-started-retail]

|Feature overview
|link:feature-overview.adoc[feature-overview]

|Plugin overview
|link:datavault-plugin.adoc[datavault-plugin]

|Business Vault reference
|link:business-vault-overview.adoc[business-vault-overview]

|CI / regression project
|link:../integration-tests/PROJECT.md[integration-tests/PROJECT.md]

|Executive summary
|link:presentations/hop-data-vault-overview.md[hop-data-vault-overview slides]
|===

Run the full test orchestrator when ready:

[source,bash]
----
cd integration-tests && ./run-tests.sh
----

docs.content:
= Getting started — retail example
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

This is a **tour of the finished retail sample**: source data → Data Vault → Business Vault → dimensional marts, including an incremental update wave. The project already has a source model, catalog feeds, models, and a resource definition group (`retail-sources`). You run the workflows; you do not build those artifacts from scratch here.

To **build an EDW from scratch** (source model → catalog → `.hdv` → resource definition group → load → BV/DM), see link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]. Architecture pictures: link:architecture.adoc[Architecture].

For Customer 360 and other regression fixtures, see link:getting-started-integration-tests.adoc[Getting started — integration test fixtures].

Estimated time: 2–3 hours with Hop GUI, or follow command-line steps only in under an hour.

== Prerequisites

. Install Docker with Compose v2 and Python 3 (stdlib only).
. Build or download the plugin for Apache Hop **2.20.0-SNAPSHOT** (see link:../README.md[repository README]).
. Register `retail-example/` as a Hop project named **`retail-example`**.
. Configure database connections **`CRM`** and **`Vault`** from project metadata.
. Start PostgreSQL: from repo root, `./scripts/run-postgres.sh up`.

If you previously used an older single-database layout, reset once:

[source,bash]
----
./scripts/run-postgres.sh reset
./scripts/run-postgres.sh up
----

Project details: link:../retail-example/README.md[retail-example/README.md].

== Chapter 1 — Understand the layout

Retail uses two databases on port **54320**:

* **CRM** (`test_source`) — landing tables mimicking a source system
* **Vault** (`test_edw`) — Data Vault, Business Vault, dimensional tables, retail load log

Key files:

[cols="2,3", options="header"]
|===
|Path |Purpose

|`work/edw-catalog/hop/retail-example/sources/`
|`DV_SOURCE` record definitions (namespace `hop/retail-example/sources`; gitignored runtime catalog)

|`fixtures/schema-gate-baseline/`
|Seed for schema-gate tag `v1.0.0` (copied into `work/edw-catalog/catalog-versions/`)

|`models/retail-360.hdv`
|Data Vault model

|`models/retail-360.hbv`
|Business Vault model (SCD2 Customer 360)

|`models/retail-warehouse.hdm`
|Dimensional mart model

|`workflows/run-retail-initial.hwf`
|Full initial load

|`workflows/run-retail-update.hwf`
|Incremental monthly-style update

|`work/execution-maps/*.hem`
|Generated execution maps (after a run; gitignored)
|===

== Chapter 2 — Tour the Data Catalog

. Open Hop GUI with project **retail-example**.
. Switch to the **Data Catalog** perspective.
. Expand `hop/retail-example/sources` — entries such as `E2E-customer-hub`, `E2E-order-header`.
. Open one source — note **physical table** on CRM, **record source** field, and column layout.

Sources are JSON under the FILE catalog root (`work/edw-catalog/` for retail); the namespace in each file must match its folder path (`hop/retail-example/sources`). Initial setup runs `workflows/bootstrap-retail-work.hwf` to create the `work/` folders, copy E2E DATABASE sources from `fixtures/catalog-sources/`, and seed COMPOSITE / JSON / PIPELINE feeds (`all-customer-info`, `feed_order_shipment_tracking`, `asn-package-lines`) that `retail-360.hdv` requires.

If entries appear in the tree but fail to open, press **F5** to refresh the catalog.

Reference: link:data-catalog.adoc[Data catalog], link:datavault-source.adoc[Data Vault sources].

== Chapter 2b — Source modeler (optional multi-table feeds)

Retail ships a **source model** of the CRM landing tables:

[source,text]
----
models/source-tables-crm.hsm
----

image::images/source-modeler-retail-example-with-query-dialog-generated-sql.png[Retail source modeler with All customer info query and generated SQL,align="center"]

. Open the `.hsm` file — table cards, relationship edges, a purple **query** card, and a teal **JSON** card.
. Open query **All customer info** — customer hub left-joined to address, contact, demo, and prefs.
. **Generate SQL** / **Preview data** (CRM connection required).
. **Publish to catalog** to create composite feed `feed_customer_enriched` (model **Catalog connection** should be `local-catalog`).

=== Kafka-style shipment events (Source JSON → vault)

Retail lands a simulated **Kafka consumer** table `order_shipment_event` (UUID `message_id`, JSON `payload`, topic/partition/offset). `pipelines/generate-retail-data.hpl` writes shipment-tracking events for a subset of orders during initial and update waves (statuses such as `LABEL_CREATED`, `PICKED_UP`, `IN_TRANSIT`, `DELIVERED`).

. On the same `.hsm`, open Source JSON **order_shipment_tracking** (parent = `order_shipment_event`, JSON field = `payload`).
. After CRM is loaded, use **Sample and propose fields** / **Preview data** / **Validate** on the JSON card.
. **Publish to catalog** as **`feed_order_shipment_tracking`** (type `JSON`) — already wired for the tutorial when you bootstrap / publish from the sample model.

The main retail vault still uses one catalog source per physical table for classic hubs/sats, **plus** this JSON feed for shipment tracking. Use the source modeler for **composed feeds** (SQL joins or JSON extractions). Full walkthrough: link:source-modeler-overview.adoc[Source modeler overview].

=== Advanced Shipping Notice XML (pipeline parse)

Alongside tracking **events** (JSON), retail includes nested **ASN** documents (what left the warehouse: packages and lines).

* Committed sample: `files/asn_demo.xml` (two ASNs, five package lines).
* Generated waves: `files/asn_${RETAIL_CSV_WAVE}.xml` from `pipelines/generate-retail-data.hpl` (subset of SHIPPED/DELIVERED orders).
* Parse pipeline: `pipelines/parse-asn-xml.hpl` — **Get data from XML** loops `/AdvancedShipmentNotices/ASN/Packages/Package/Lines/Line`, flattens parent attributes via relative XPath, adds `record_source=E2E-asn-line`, and ends on dummy **ASN lines** (preview / pipeline-source output).

Default parameter `RETAIL_CSV_WAVE=demo` reads the committed fixture. After a data generate, set the wave to `initial` or `2024-01` to parse the matching file. This path is meant for **pipeline sources** in the source modeler; it is not loaded into CRM by the default workflows.

== Chapter 3 — Explore the Data Vault model

. Open `models/retail-360.hdv`.
. Click **Edit model** — target database **Vault**, hashing and sentinel settings.
. Inspect hubs, links, and satellites on the canvas — including **`hub_order_shipment`**, **`lnk_order_shipment`**, and **`sat_order_shipment`** (record source `feed_order_shipment_tracking`).
. Click **Check model** — resolve any errors before loading.

image::images/data-vault-model-retail-example.png[Retail 360 Data Vault model — hubs, links, and satellites on the Hop canvas,align="center"]

Optional: select a satellite, **Show update pipeline** — same generation logic as **Data Vault Update**.

== Chapter 4 — Run the initial load

From the repository root:

[source,bash]
----
./scripts/run-hop.sh retail-example workflows/run-retail-initial.hwf
----

The workflow drops and recreates schemas, bootstraps `work/` (FILE catalog + schema-gate baseline `v1.0.0`), generates CSV source files (including shipment event CSVs), loads CRM, runs the **schema gate**, **measures source data quality and applies a quality gate** (blocking findings stop the load), then runs **Update resource definition group** for `retail-sources` (all DV → BV → DM models). That action manages vault metrics and writes load-overview reports under `work/reports/` (`retail-dv-initial-report` / `retail-dv-update-report` via `REPORT_BASE_NAME`). After the update it re-measures sources in **alert-only** mode.

In Hop GUI you can open `workflows/run-retail-initial.hwf` and run it with a configured pipeline run configuration.

== Chapter 4b — Schema gate and catalog versions

Retail wires **Validate resource definitions** in `workflows/run-retail-update-models.hwf` (shared by initial and update):

* Group: `retail-sources`
* Compare mode: `WORKING_VS_VERSION` against baseline tag **`v1.0.0`**
* Reports: `work/reports/retail-schema-validation.md` and `.html`
* Downstream impact enabled

Design-time: open metadata **Resource definition group** `retail-sources` for **Tag catalog version**, **List catalog versions**, and **Validate sources** (options dialog, then results + optional expand-from-catalog remediation). A sample multi-table remediation package for `address_line1` length 75 is under `workflows/schema-remediation/accept-address_line1/`.

image::images/resource-definition-group-editor.png[Resource definition group retail-sources with harvest, lineage, catalog version, and Validate sources buttons,align="center"]

image::images/resource-definition-group-validate-sources-dialog.png[Validate sources options dialog for baseline and check axes,align="center"]

image::images/validate-resource-definitions-action-dialog.png[Validate resource definitions workflow action as used in the retail schema gate,align="center"]

Full parameter reference, GUI issue dialogs, and sample HTML reports: link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation]. Content rules (nulls, domains) are separate — see link:data-quality.adoc[Data quality].

== Chapter 5 — Run an incremental update

[source,bash]
----
./scripts/run-hop.sh retail-example workflows/run-retail-update.hwf
----

Repeat to simulate monthly batches. Vault table `retail_load_log` stores each finished load. The next run sets `LOAD_DATE` to that date plus one month and writes the row only after the vault update succeeds.

== Chapter 5b — Transactional links: order lines

Open `models/retail-360.hdv` and inspect **`lnk_order_line`**:

* Participating hubs: `hub_order`, `hub_product`
* **Dependent child key:** `line_number` (source field `line_number`) on the link dialog **Dependent child keys** tab
* Link satellite **`sat_lnk_order_line`**: measures `quantity`, `unit_price`, `discount_pct` (no multi-active driving key — line identity is on the link)

image::images/data-vault-link-table-with-dependent-child-keys.png[Edit Link dialog for lnk_order_line — Dependent child keys tab with line_number, retail-360 model in the background,align="center"]

Grain is one vault link row per order line. The same product can appear on more than one line of the same order (different prices); the data generator plants this on the first order of each wave so you can verify two distinct `lnk_order_line_hk` values for the same order + product.

Contrast:

* **`lnk_order`** — standard relationship (customer ↔ order)
* **`lnk_order_line`** — transactional link (order ↔ product ↔ line number)
* **`lnk_warehouse_product`** — relationship + stock attributes over time

Reference: link:dv-link.adoc#transactional-links-dependent-child-keys[Transactional links].

== Chapter 6 — Business Vault and dimensional layers

. Open `models/retail-360.hbv` — linked to `retail-360.hdv`.
. Inspect SCD2 table **customer_360_bv** (multi-satellite merge).
. Open `models/retail-conformed-dims.hdm` for shared dimensions, `models/retail-f-orders.hdm` for `f_orders`, and `models/retail-f-order-lines.hdm` for `f_order_lines`.

image::images/dimensional-model-f-orders.png[Dimensional model — f_orders,align="center"]

The `f_order_lines` fact in `retail-f-order-lines.hdm` reuses conformed dimensions from `retail-conformed-dims` and adds role-playing date dimensions for order, shipping, and delivery dates. Facts are tagged with Business / process levels from metadata **retail-bus**; open the link:bus-matrix.adoc[bus matrix] from resource definition group **retail-sources**.

image::images/bus-matrix-of-the-retail-example.png[Bus matrix for retail-sources — inventory, order lines, and orders against conformed dimensions,align="center"]

Its source SQL reads `line_number` from **`lnk_order_line`** (dependent child key on the transactional link) and measures from the current row of `sat_lnk_order_line`:

image::images/dimensional-model-f-order-lines.png[Dimensional model — f_order_lines with conformed dimension roles,align="center"]

Reference: link:business-vault-overview.adoc[Business Vault overview], link:dimensional-modeler-overview.adoc[Dimensional modeler overview].

== Chapter 7 — Execution map (optional)

. Open a generated map under `work/execution-maps/` (for example `update-retail-dv-bv-dm.hem` or `simulate-6-months.hem` after a crawl/run).
. Explore the crawled graph: root workflow → nested workflows and pipelines → models → generated pipelines → source datasets.
. Drill into nodes (double-click) to focus on one layer at a time; use the breadcrumb bar to navigate back.

image::images/execution-map-in-hop-gui-simulate-six-months.png[Execution map — simulate-6-months workflow opened in Hop GUI,align="center"]

The **simulate-6-months** map crawls `workflows/simulate-6-months.hwf`: an initial load followed by `update-6-times.hpl`, which runs `run-retail-update.hwf` six times.

Reference: link:execution-maps.adoc[Execution maps].

== Chapter 7b — Hop Lineage View (optional)

. Start Marquez: `./scripts/run-marquez.sh up`.
. Export model-derived lineage: `./scripts/run-hop.sh retail-example workflows/send-lineage-to-marquez.hwf` (or enable the export hop on `run-retail-update-models.hwf`).
. Open `models/f_orders-upstream.hlv` — or click a fact such as `f_pit_inventory` / `f_orders` and choose **Show lineage**.
+
image::images/lineage-view-model-context-action.png[Show lineage on dimensional fact f_pit_inventory,align="center"]
. Walk **upstream** into BV/DV/source. Click a node to open the model, catalog record, or generated pipeline.
. Duration badges (when **Overlay OPS load times** is on) come from the Hop OPS database. Marquez “latest run” is the last *export*, not the last *load*.
. Click a node **name** to fill the right-hand Markdown details pane (**View as HTML** opens the same document in a browser).

image::images/lineage-view-with-information-pane.png[Hop Lineage View — lineage-f-order-lines with OPS badges and details for dm/retail-f-inventory/d_product,align="center"]

Backend `Marquez-Localhost` uses `${MARQUEZ_API}` (suffix stripped to the host). Prefer `${MARQUEZ_BASE_URL}` = `http://localhost:5001` on new backends. Namespaces must match the export (`${MARQUEZ_NAMESPACE_JOB}` / `${MARQUEZ_NAMESPACE_DATASET}`).

Reference: link:hop-lineage-view.adoc[Hop Lineage View], link:openlineage-export.adoc[OpenLineage export].

== Chapter 8 — Troubleshooting

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Symptom |What to check

|Connection errors
|Postgres running on 54320; `environments/local-docker-postgres.json` variables

|Catalog entry won't open
|Namespace matches folder; refresh catalog (F5)

|Model check type errors
|CRM tables exist; run initial workflow's CRM load first; validate catalog fields vs live schema

|`./scripts/run-postgres.sh reset` then `up`, rerun initial workflow

docs.content:
= Business Vault Update action
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

== Description

The **Business Vault Update** workflow action (`BUSINESS_VAULT_UPDATE`) rebuilds Business Vault tables from a saved `.hbv` model. It follows the same pattern as the Data Vault Update action: validate, optionally create schema, generate pipelines, stage, and run in parallel.

At runtime the action:

* Loads the `.hbv` model and resolves the linked `.hdv` Data Vault model
* Optionally validates both models before any work is done
* Optionally generates CREATE TABLE DDL for Business Vault tables on the BV target database
* Generates **build pipelines** for each selected SCD2, PIT, bridge, and SQL business table
* For SCD2 tables with **hash-key partitions**, generates a wrapper workflow (truncate once, then sequential partition loads; Staging file mode then bulk-loads each partition CSV) and runs it before the free-pipeline orchestrator
* Stages remaining pipelines and runs them through a parallel orchestrator
* Optionally publishes BV target table layouts to the data catalog
* Aggregates pipeline results into the workflow action result

== Dialog tabs

=== Model tab

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Business Vault model file
|Path to the `.hbv` file. Variables supported (e.g. `${PROJECT_HOME}/tests/multi-satellite-bv/customer-360.hbv`). Required.

|Pipeline run configuration
|Pipeline Run Configuration used to execute every generated build pipeline. Required when data load runs.

|Log model check failures
|When enabled (default), runs `BusinessVaultModel.check()` before generating pipelines or DDL.

|Abort on model check failures
|When enabled (default), stops immediately if any check returns an error.

|Parallel pipeline copies
|Number of parallel workers for staged pipelines (default `1`).

|Pipeline staging folder
|Folder where generated pipelines are written before execution. When empty, defaults to `${java.io.tmpdir}/bv/`.

|Metrics output folder
|Optional folder for per-run metrics JSON (same pattern as Data Vault Update).

|Publish to catalog
|When enabled, upserts record definitions for BV target tables into the configured data catalog.

|Data catalog connection
|Catalog connection used when publish is enabled.

|Selected table names
|Optional comma-separated list of BV table names to process. Empty = all tables.

|Do not update target database
|When enabled, skips data load pipelines (useful for DDL-only or catalog-only runs).
|===

=== DDL tab

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Update target database structure
|When enabled (default), generates and executes CREATE TABLE DDL on the Business Vault target database before running build pipelines.

|DDL SQL filename
|Optional path where generated DDL is written when schema changes are needed.

|Fail if DDL is needed
|Fails immediately if any DDL would be required — useful in CI/CD when schemas must already exist.
|===

== Prerequisites

* The `.hbv` **Data Vault model path** must resolve (set `PROJECT_HOME` in the Hop project)
* **Vault** (or your DV connection) and **BV target database** must exist in project metadata
* Raw vault hub and satellite tables must contain history to read — load them first with Data Vault Update (unless satellites are external read-only and already populated)

== Execution order

Within a single Business Vault Update run, the action processes tables in this order:

1. **SCD2** tables — functional timeline merges from satellite history
2. **PIT** tables — snapshot spine and satellite load-timestamp pointers from raw hub/satellite history

SCD2 and PIT read independent data paths (PIT does not consume SCD2 output). Ordering keeps logs predictable and matches the typical load sequence: collapse functional history, then refresh as-of helpers.

`BUSINESS_TABLE` types are skipped with a log message until pipeline generation is implemented.

== Related actions

* link:datavault-update-action.adoc[Data Vault Update Action] — loads the raw `.hdv` model first
* link:business-vault-scd2.adoc[Business Vault SCD2] — SCD2 build pipelines
* link:business-vault-pit.adoc[Business Vault PIT] — PIT build pipelines

Sample workflows:

* `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/update-customer-360.hwf` — multi-satellite SCD2 (full rebuild)
* `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/update-customer-360-partitioned.hwf` — same golden as full rebuild, SCD2 hash-key partitions = 4
* `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/update-customer-360-incremental.hwf` — multi-satellite SCD2 incremental build mode
* `integration-tests/tests/basic/update-vault1.hwf` — SCD2 + PIT on the introductory vault1 model

docs.content:
= Data Vault Source — Database tab
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

Database-backed feeds store their physical definition on the **Database** tab of the **Data Vault Source** metadata editor. This is not a separate Hop metadata type; it is embedded inside each Data Vault Source alongside the General tab (record source indicator and group).

The database definition tells the model what columns are available, which form the natural or primary key, and what their data types and lengths are.

== Why the field layout matters

Accurate column metadata is used throughout the plugin:

* **Load from source** (hub Keys tab and satellite Attributes tab) reads primary-key and attribute definitions from the source.
* Pipeline generation uses primary-key flags to build SELECT lists and hash inputs.
* Target table DDL uses length and precision so you get realistic column types (VARCHAR(50), DECIMAL(15,2), etc.) instead of generic large types.

== Options

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Database connection
|The Hop database connection (DatabaseMeta) for the source system. Required for Import and for generated pipelines to read data.

|Schema
|Optional schema or catalog that qualifies the table in the source database.

|Source table / view
|Physical table or view name. Can be left empty when the table name is supplied at runtime via variables or when you use the definition only for its field layout.

|Fields (row layout)
|Expected columns from this source. Each field includes:

* Field name (as in the source).
* Optional description.
* Source data type (VARCHAR, NUMBER, DATE, etc.).
* Length and precision.
* **Part of source primary key** – Fields marked as primary key become hub business keys and parent-hash inputs for satellites and links.
* Hop data type (used internally when building row layouts).

The Fields grid is the authoritative column metadata for this feed.
|===

== The Import button

The fastest way to populate the Fields list:

1. Select or enter a database connection.
2. Optionally enter schema and table name.
3. Click **Import**.

The editor connects to the database, reads column metadata, and attempts to detect primary key columns. It replaces the current Fields list with the imported layout. You can edit the grid afterwards; saved changes become the definition the model uses even if the live source table changes later.

The model editor toolbar **Import sources** action can create new Data Vault Source objects from database tables in bulk, using the same import machinery.

== How the chain works at load time

When a hub, link, or satellite loads data:

1. The table references a **Data Vault Source** by name (hub: Record sources tab; link/satellite: Default record source).
2. The source's **Database** tab supplies connection, table, and field layout.
3. Primary-key fields drive hash calculations; lengths and precisions flow into target DDL.

== Tips

* Import early and verify primary key flags. Wrong PK metadata is the most common cause of incorrect hash keys.
* Adjust lengths in the field grid when live database metadata is wider than you want in the vault.
* When the same physical table is loaded with different record source values, create one Data Vault Source per feed (duplicate and change General tab indicator/group settings) rather than sharing one logical name.
* Use meaningful source names on the General tab; the Database tab can point at the same connection and table for multiple feeds when needed.

docs.content:
= Project documentation (static HTML)
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

Generate a **self-contained HTML + CSS + JavaScript** documentation set for a Hop project (issue https://github.com/ProjectDataHopper/hopper-edw/issues/25[#25]). Open `index.html` in a browser — **no server**. Copy the folder as-is.

This is **not** Apache Hop's `hop doc` / **Generate documentation** action (Markdown). Data Hopper EDW adds models, tables, lineage, search, and theming.

== What is documented

* Pipelines (`.hpl`) and workflows (`.hwf`): description, parameters, transforms/actions, Markdown notes (links to other project files resolve to documentation pages), used metadata
* Source / Data Vault / Business Vault / dimensional models and execution maps (`.hsm` `.hdv` `.hbv` `.hdm` `.hem`)
* Tables with descriptions and **source-to-target lineage**
* Hop metadata objects (passwords redacted)
* Catalog record definitions (best-effort)
* Zoomable SVG diagrams (light + dark) with click-through to transforms, actions, and tables
* Kimball **bus matrices** (one page per resource definition group that lists `.hdm` files)
* Client-side search from the header

Skipped: `.hlv` session graphs, hidden folders, `.git`, `target`, `node_modules`, and the output folder if it sits inside the source tree.

== How to run

=== Workflow action

**Generate project documentation** (`GENERATE_PROJECT_DOCUMENTATION`):

* **Target folder** — output directory (default `'${PROJECT_HOME}'/work/documentation`)
* **Source folder** — optional; empty uses `'${PROJECT_HOME}'`
* **Scope** — `PROJECT` or `ENVIRONMENT` (also lists non-secret environment variables)
* **CSS theme** — `default`, `compact`, or `high-contrast`
* Include checkboxes: parameters, notes, metadata, catalog, lineage, dark SVG copies

=== Tools menu

**Tools → Generate project documentation…** uses the same options, shows a cancelable progress dialog, and opens `index.html` when generation finishes.

* **Hop GUI (desktop):** opens the site in the system browser (`file:` URL).
* **Hop Web:** shows a cancelable progress dialog, then opens `index.html` in the **regular browser** through the same RAP handler as plugin EDW docs (`servicehandler=hopperEdwDocs&file=index.html`). In the File explorer tree, **Open in browser** (and double-click on generated HTML) uses that handler too — not Hop's explorer HTML tab (`Browser.setText()` has no document base).

=== CLI

[source,bash]
----
hop project-doc -e retail-example-docker-pg \
  -t ${PROJECT_HOME}/work/documentation \
  --theme default
----

`-j` / `--project` or `-e` / `--environment` work like `hop-run`. Other flags: `--source-folder`, `--scope`, `--no-parameters`, `--no-notes`, `--no-metadata`, `--no-catalog`, `--no-lineage`, `--no-dark-svg`.

== Opening the set

Open `{target}/index.html`. Search and the search index use `assets/js/search-index.js` (`window.HOP_DOC_INDEX`) so they work from `file://` (browsers block `fetch()` of local JSON).

The left-hand navigation is a tree: **type** (Pipelines, Workflows, Source models, …), then the **relative project folder** for files, the **parent model** (under a layer folder) for tables, **metadata type plus virtual path**, and **catalog name plus namespace**. Type groups start collapsed; opening a page expands its ancestors and keeps **siblings** in the same folder. Expanded groups are remembered in the browser so going back does not collapse the tree. Items sort alphabetically, case-insensitive.

The header shows a breadcrumb (`project / Pipelines / folder / page`), with search and a **System / Light / Dark** combo on the right. **System** follows `prefers-color-scheme`. Diagrams swap `*.light.svg` / `*.dark.svg`.

== Output layout

[source,text]
----
{target}/
  index.html
  theming.html
  assets/css/hop-doc.css
  assets/css/themes/{default,compact,high-contrast}.css
  assets/css/print.css
  assets/js/{hop-doc,search,svg-viewer,search-index}.js
  assets/js/hits/{id}.js
  assets/images/{id}.light.svg
  assets/images/{id}.dark.svg
  pipelines/…
  workflows/…
  models/{source,data-vault,business-vault,dimensional,execution-maps}/…
  tables/{source,dv,bv,dm}/…
  metadata/{type}/…
  catalog/{namespace}/…
----

== Restyling (CSS contract)

See the generated `theming.html` (also copied conceptually here). Replace `assets/css/hop-doc.css` or regenerate with `--theme compact` / `high-contrast`. Custom properties and stable classes (`hop-doc-header`, `hop-doc-search`, `hop-doc-svg-viewport`, …) are listed on that page.

== Related

* link:architecture-export.adoc[Architecture export] (Draw.io, not this HTML set)
* link:source-to-target-lineage.adoc[Source-to-target lineage]
* link:feature-overview.adoc[Feature overview]
