docs.content:
= Resource definition validation
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

Beyond **Check model** on `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm` files, the plugin validates **Data Catalog record definitions** — especially `DV_SOURCE` feeds — and surfaces issues in the Hop GUI with optional remediation, acknowledgements, **downstream impact**, and **catalog version** baselines for CI/CD.

== When validation runs

* Explicit **Validate sources** on a **Resource definition group** metadata editor (design time)
* Workflow action **Validate resource definitions (schema gate)** before DV/BV/DM loads (CI/CD)
* Pipelines that depend on catalog layout (indirectly, via model checks and source resolution)

Model validation and catalog validation are complementary: a passing model check still requires accurate source definitions in the catalog.

== Resource definition group (design time)

Open metadata type **Resource definition group**. A group scopes which DV / BV / DM model files participate in validation and catalog-version tagging. Set **Default catalog connection** to your FILE catalog (retail: `local-catalog` → `work/edw-catalog`).

Bottom of the editor:

* **List catalog versions** — review tags already stored under the catalog’s `catalog-versions/` folder
* **Tag catalog version** — freeze current source contracts for a semantic tag (for example `v1.0.0`)
* **Validate sources** — open the **validation options** dialog (baseline + check axes), then run comparison and open the results dialog
* **Browse lineage…** — reverse source-to-target lineage browser (see link:source-to-target-lineage.adoc[Source-to-target lineage])

image::images/resource-definition-group-editor.png[Resource definition group editor for retail-sources with harvest actions, lineage, catalog version buttons, and Validate sources,align="center"]

Catalog version storage and scope are described in link:data-catalog.adoc#catalog-versions[Data Catalog — Catalog versions]. Versions can also be browsed **read-only** under **Versions** in the Data Catalog perspective.

=== Design-time validation options

**Validate sources** does not run immediately. An options dialog asks what is being compared:

image::images/resource-definition-group-validate-sources-dialog.png[Validate sources options dialog: baseline (working catalog or version tag), check axes, optional report path,align="center"]

* **Baseline (truth for this run)** — current working catalog (typical after automatic drift notification) or a **catalog version tag** (immutable snapshot)
* **What to check** — live source systems, working catalog vs version, target models (DV/BV/DM), target databases (DDL needed?), downstream impact/lineage
* **Parallel checks** — max concurrent live-source discoveries and target-table DDL checks (default **8**, range 1–64). Raise this when validating hundreds of database sources over a high-latency link (VPN); set **1** for serial debugging.
* **Optional report** — write HTML/Markdown under a Hop VFS path (same formatter as the CI gate)

Validation is always **read-only**. Catalog version snapshots are never modified by validation. The results banner restates the chosen baseline and axes.

== Workflow action (CI/CD schema gate)

Add **Validate resource definitions** to a workflow (category General) and place it **before** Data Vault / Business Vault / Dimensional update actions.

image::images/validate-resource-definitions-action-dialog.png[Validate resource definitions action dialog with WORKING_VS_VERSION, baseline v1.0.0, and report path under work/reports,align="center"]

|===
| Parameter | Purpose |

| Resource definition group | Required validation scope (for example `retail-sources`) |
| Target catalog version | Tag such as `v1.0.0` / `${TARGET_VERSION}`, or a ComboVar free-typed expression. **LIVE_SOURCE:** expected contract (empty = working tree). **VERSION_VS_VERSION:** the *actual* tag. **WORKING_VS_VERSION:** used as baseline if Baseline is empty. |
| Compare mode | `LIVE_SOURCE` (default), `WORKING_VS_VERSION`, `VERSION_VS_VERSION`, **`HARVEST_RUN`** |
| Baseline catalog version | **WORKING_VS_VERSION / VERSION_VS_VERSION:** expected/reference tag. **LIVE_SOURCE:** used as expected when Target is empty. ComboVar list is filled from tags in the group’s FILE catalog. |
| Harvest run id | **HARVEST_RUN:** run id (default `${DV_SCHEMA_HARVEST_RUN_ID}`); empty → latest harvest for the group |
| Harvest history database / schema | **HARVEST_RUN:** OPS connection holding `schema_harvest_*` (retail: `OPS` / `dv_ops`) |
| Report output path | Folder/path for Markdown and/or HTML (Hop VFS), for example `${PROJECT_HOME}/work/reports` |
| Report file base name | Optional base name without extension (defaults to a group/timestamp name) |
| Report format | `MARKDOWN`, `HTML`, or `BOTH` |
| Failure severity | `FAIL_ON_BLOCKING` (default), `FAIL_ON_WARNINGS`, `WARN_ONLY` |
| Fail on warnings (legacy) | Older workflows only; prefer **Failure severity** |
| Include downstream impact | Annotate issues with Source→DV→BV→DM blast radius |
| Check target databases | Compare model tables to the physical target database (CREATE/ALTER DDL needed) |
| Target tables are created automatically | When target DB checks are on: missing tables (CREATE that vault update will apply) are **not reported** — they are expected. Layout drift on **existing** tables stays a warning. |
| Parallel checks | Max concurrent live-source / target-DB checks (default `8`, supports `${VALIDATION_PARALLELISM}`). Independent of load `parallelPipelineCopies`. |
|===

=== Initial load and automatic table creation

On a first vault load, target tables often do not exist yet. Enable **Target tables are created automatically** on the workflow action (Y/N or a Hop variable such as `${EXPECT_AUTOMATIC_TARGET_TABLE_CREATION}`) and the same option in the GUI **Validate sources** dialog so pending CREATE findings are **omitted** from reports and the results dialog (not listed as INFO noise). The gate can keep **fail-on-warnings** without treating expected first-load CREATE as a defect. ALTER / layout drift on tables that already exist is still reported.

On **incremental update** runs, leave the option **off** (N) so missing or altered target tables fail the gate — the warehouse should already exist and drift is real. The retail sample sets `EXPECT_AUTOMATIC_TARGET_TABLE_CREATION=Y` from `run-retail-initial` and `N` from `run-retail-update` into shared `run-retail-update-models.hwf`.

=== Compare modes

|===
| Mode | Expected (baseline) | Actual | Typical use |

| `LIVE_SOURCE` | Working tree, or Target/Baseline tag | Live physical source discovery | Daily CI against CRM/source DB |
| `WORKING_VS_VERSION` | Baseline (or Target if Baseline empty) tag | Working-tree catalog | Detect catalog field length/type edits without a live DB |
| `VERSION_VS_VERSION` | Baseline tag | Target tag | Offline PR review between two frozen contracts |
| `HARVEST_RUN` | Contract already compared during harvest | Persisted harvest snapshot (OPS) | After **Harvest source metadata** — no second live discovery; see link:metadata-harvesting.adoc[Metadata harvesting] |
|===

Version fields support Hop variables (for example `${PROMOTED_TAG}`). Tag lists refresh when the resource definition group changes.

== Validation results dialog (GUI)

After **Validate sources**, the **Source validation** dialog uses a master-detail layout with a status banner (`PASS` / `WARNINGS` / `CRITICAL BLOCKED`) and the baseline/axes context from the options dialog:

image::images/resource-definition-group-validation-results-dialog.png[Source validation results dialog with CRITICAL BLOCKED, issue list, and expected vs actual length on address_line1,align="center"]

* **Top — issue summaries** (compact rows): Severity, Record definition, Field, Kind (for example `FIELD_TYPE_CHANGED`), Proposals count
* **BLOCKING** rows are highlighted in red; **WARNING** rows in amber
* **Bottom — selected issue details**: full message, downstream impact, and model usages
* Select a summary row to load details (no need to hunt for double-click)

Detail actions for the selected issue:

* **Open source in catalog** — jump to the source record definition in the Data Catalog perspective
* **Open target table** — open the selected model usage (hub, satellite, BV, or DM table)
* **Remediation proposals…** — open the proposals dialog (also available via double-click)
* **Acknowledge…** / **Revoke acknowledgement** — accept or clear a warning with a comment
* Footer: show acknowledged issues, re-validate (re-opens options), tag catalog version

image::images/resource-definition-group-validation-blocking-issue-found.png[Earlier screenshot: Source validation results dialog showing CRITICAL BLOCKED and length change with downstream impact,align="center"]

== Issue detail and remediation

Full issue text and blast radius stay in the **details pane** of the results dialog. Use **Remediation proposals…** for fixes.

=== How to read a finding (axis first)

Each issue message is structured so you can see **what was checked** before the severity label:

* **Axis** — which check produced the finding (live sources, working catalog vs baseline version, target database layout, …)
* **Compared** — expected vs actual sides for that axis
* **Found** — factual result (for example “source missing from baseline v1.0.0”, or “2 DDL statements required”)
* **Why it matters** — what to do next for *this* axis

The status banner also restates **compare mode** and **baseline** (current working catalog **or** a version tag such as `v1.0.0`). Selecting “current catalog” as baseline does **not** use a version tag; warnings can still appear from other axes (live discovery, target DB, models).

|===
| Kind | Typical meaning |

| `BASELINE_CONTRACT_MISSING` | Source is used by models and in the working catalog, but **not** in the frozen baseline version |
| `WORKING_CONTRACT_MISSING` | Models reference a source that is **not** in the working catalog yet (publish/generate first) |
| `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` | **Live** discovery failed or the source is not refreshable (connection, path, COMPOSITE model) |
| `TARGET_DDL_REQUIRED` | **EDW/target** table lags the model (often normal **before the first vault update** creates tables). Not a source-catalog field mismatch |
| `FIELD_*` / `MODEL_ATTRIBUTE_NARROWER` | Field contract or model attribute length/type drift |
|===

=== Catalog is never rewritten by length remediation

The **working catalog field length is the contract** used to expand models and target DDL. Remediation does **not** change the catalog. If the live source should define a new length, update the catalog yourself in the Data Catalog, then re-validate.

image::images/resource-definition-group-validation-remediation-proposals-dialog.png[Remediation proposals dialog: expand field length in target models and database schemas using the catalog,align="center"]

Primary proposal for length drift:

**Expand field length in target models and database schemas (using the catalog)**

* Catalog is **not** changed
* DV satellite attributes in git-versioned models are expanded to the **catalog** field length
* Downstream **BV SCD2** columns linked by explicit field mappings (e.g. `address_line1` → `cust_address` on `customer_360_bv`) are included for target DDL
* Downstream **DM** columns sourced via SQL that reads a BV table (e.g. `JOIN customer_360_bv sc` + attribute `cust_address` on `d_customer`) are included when field names match (SQL table-ref + BV-mediated lineage, confidence `DERIVED_VIA_BV`)
* You name the remediation package folder

image::images/resource-definition-group-validation-remediation-confirmation-dialog.png[Confirm remediation dialog explaining models and SQL are updated from catalog length; catalog not changed,align="center"]

=== Schema remediation package

Under the **Schema remediation folder** (Data Vault 2.0 plugin settings; default `${PROJECT_HOME}/workflows/schema-remediation/<name>/`) the plugin writes:

* a reviewable **SQL script** (always when DDL is needed), with sections per affected table
* a Hop **workflow** with **one SQL action per target table** (run later per DTAP environment — **not** executed immediately)
* HTML and Markdown **reports** of the catalog length used, each downstream target + lineage confidence, and that the catalog was not modified

image::images/resource-definition-group-validation-remediation-result-dialog.png[Remediation result listing BV and DM targets, SQL path, workflow path, catalog not modified,align="center"]

image::images/resource-definition-group-validation-remediation-workflow.png[Generated remediation workflow: Start to SQL actions for each target table to Success,align="center"]

Other issue kinds (field added/removed, primary key change) may still offer **Refresh catalog contract from source** — that path *does* update the catalog. It is separate from length expand.

Acknowledgements persist with the catalog record so teams can document conscious exceptions (for example known schema drift in a non-production feed).

== Retail example: address_line1 length expand

In the retail project, widening catalog field `address_line1` to **75** and applying expand produces a package under:

`retail-example/workflows/schema-remediation/accept-address_line1/`

|===
| File | Role |

| `accept-address_line1-report.md` / `.html` | What changed, downstream targets, confidence |
| `accept-address_line1-apply-ddl.sql` | Reviewable multi-table DDL (one section per table) |
| `accept-address_line1-apply-ddl.hwf` | Hop workflow: one SQL action per table → Success |
|===

Example Markdown report (checked-in sample; paths project-relative under the retail project):

----
# Schema remediation: expand models and schemas from catalog length

- **Remediation name:** accept-address_line1
- **Workflow:** `workflows/schema-remediation/accept-address_line1/accept-address_line1-apply-ddl.hwf`
- **SQL script:** `workflows/schema-remediation/accept-address_line1/accept-address_line1-apply-ddl.sql`

## What changed

- Expanding models and target DDL for field 'address_line1' to catalog length 75. The catalog was not modified.
- Downstream target BV customer_360_bv.cust_address (from catalog field address_line1, length 75, confidence EXPLICIT_MAP)
- Downstream target DM d_customer.cust_address (from catalog field address_line1, length 75, confidence DERIVED_VIA_BV)
- SQL script written (3 statement(s) for table(s) sat_customer_address, customer_360_bv, d_customer): ...
- DDL workflow written: ...
- Catalog was not modified by this remediation.
----

The companion SQL widens **three** physical tables on connection **Vault** — DV satellite, BV SCD2, and DM dimension — using dialect-specific length-change steps (PostgreSQL example uses a temporary column rename):

----
-- Connection: Vault  Table: sat_customer_address
ALTER TABLE sat_customer_address ADD COLUMN address_line1_KTL VARCHAR(75);
UPDATE sat_customer_address SET address_line1_KTL=address_line1;
ALTER TABLE sat_customer_address DROP COLUMN address_line1;
ALTER TABLE sat_customer_address RENAME address_line1_KTL TO address_line1;

-- Connection: Vault  Table: customer_360_bv
ALTER TABLE customer_360_bv ADD COLUMN cust_address_KTL VARCHAR(75);
...

-- Connection: Vault  Table: d_customer
ALTER TABLE d_customer ADD COLUMN cust_address_KTL VARCHAR(75);
...
----

Review the workflow/SQL on each DTAP environment before loads that need the wider columns. The workflow is **not** run automatically when you accept the proposal.

== HTML / Markdown gate reports

When the workflow action has a **Report output path**, it writes scannable artifacts via Hop VFS (local, S3, Azure, and similar). The HTML report title is **Data Vault Resource Definition Validation Report** and includes resource group, **baseline**, compare mode, status, issue table, downstream impact summary, and required action.

**Pass** (no schema drift vs the comparison baseline):

image::images/data-vault-ddl-validation-report-pass.png[HTML validation report with WORKING_VS_VERSION and Status PASS,align="center"]

**Critical blocked** (length/type drift with blast radius):

image::images/data-vault-ddl-validation-report-critical-blocked.png[HTML validation report CRITICAL BLOCKED with column drift table and downstream impact summary,align="center"]

Markdown siblings are intended for CI log scrapers and PR comments. Retail writes files such as `work/reports/retail-schema-validation.md` and `.html`.

== Practical design-time workflow

. Edit or import sources in the Data Catalog (or refresh contracts from the live system).
. Open the **Resource definition group** → **Validate sources** → choose baseline and axes.
. Fix errors; apply expand-from-catalog proposals where models/schemas lag the catalog.
. Acknowledge warnings that are accepted risk, with a short reason.
. **Tag catalog version** when the contract is ready for DTAP promotion.
. Run **Check model** on the `.hdv` file — detailed type checking uses live database schemas when enabled.

== Schema impact simulation (programmatic)

`SchemaImpactSimulationService` orchestrates catalog schema comparison and optional downstream impact enrichment for CI/CD and design-time dry-runs (same modes as the workflow action). Optional axes include target models and target database DDL readiness.

Results include a `ValidationReport`, optional `ImpactGraph` blast-radius labels on issues, and overall status (`PASS` / `WARNING` / `CRITICAL_BLOCKED`).

`SchemaValidationReportFormatter` emits log text, Markdown (CI artifact layout), and HTML. `SchemaValidationReportFileWriter` writes those artifacts via Hop VFS.

== DTAP promotion recipe

Use catalog versions and the schema gate to keep Development, Test, Acceptance, and Production aligned without “deploy and pray.”

. **DEV — approve schema change**
.. Import or refresh source definitions in the Data Catalog (set the catalog field length when the contract changes).
.. Run **Validate sources** on the resource definition group; review **downstream impact**.
.. Apply remediations (**expand models and database schemas from the catalog**) or acknowledge accepted warnings.
.. Review generated files under `workflows/schema-remediation/` and commit them with the model change when appropriate.
.. Run the generated DDL workflow against the **DEV** target database (or include it in the environment promotion package).
.. **Tag catalog version** (for example `v2.4.0` or `2026-Q3-Release`) after the contract is agreed.
. **Git promote**
.. Commit model files (`.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm`), schema-remediation workflow/SQL artifacts, and any **seeded** version fixtures. Prefer a gitignored runtime catalog (`work/edw-catalog/`) for working-tree and snapshot files generated on each machine.
.. Promote the same tag through DTAP branches or release artifacts; run the DDL workflow on each environment before loads that need the wider columns.
. **TEST / ACC / PROD — gate before load**
.. In the daily update workflow, place **Validate resource definitions** before Data Vault / Business Vault / Dimensional update actions.
.. Configure for example:
+
----
Resource definition group: ${RESOURCE_GROUP}
Target catalog version:    ${PROMOTED_TAG}   # empty = working tree only
Compare mode:              LIVE_SOURCE
Report output path:        ${PROJECT_HOME}/work/reports
Report format:             BOTH
Failure severity:          FAIL_ON_BLOCKING  # or FAIL_ON_WARNINGS
Include downstream impact: Y
----
.. On failure, open the Markdown/HTML report under `work/reports/` (or your CI artifact path) and fix DDL / mappings before re-running loads.
. **Offline design review** (optional)
.. `WORKING_VS_VERSION` — compare a tagged baseline to the current working-tree catalog without touching live sources.
.. `VERSION_VS_VERSION` — compare two tags when reviewing a PR that only changes frozen contracts.

=== Retail example

The retail project workflow `retail-example/workflows/run-retail-update-models.hwf` runs **Validate resource definitions** on group `retail-sources` with:

* Compare mode: **`WORKING_VS_VERSION`** — picks up catalog field edits (length/type) against a frozen tag
* Baseline catalog version: **`v1.0.0`** (seeded from `fixtures/schema-gate-baseline/` into `work/edw-catalog/catalog-versions/` by `workflows/bootstrap-retail-work.hwf` when that folder is missing)
* Report output path: `${PROJECT_HOME}/work/reports`
* Report base name: `retail-schema-validation`
* Format: Markdown and HTML
* Failure severity: fail on warnings (strict sample)
* Downstream impact enabled

To detect a length change from the tagged baseline, edit the working-tree source JSON (or catalog UI) and re-run the workflow. `LIVE_SOURCE` compares to the **physical** CRM table and will not see catalog-only metadata edits.

Design-time expand of `address_line1` to 75 is illustrated under `retail-example/workflows/schema-remediation/accept-address_line1/`. See also link:getting-started-retail.adoc[Getting started with the retail example].

=== Limitations

* Catalog version snapshots freeze **source record definitions**, not model files (models stay in Git).
* Free-form DM SQL field lineage is best-effort: BV-mediated name matching and `table` / `alias.*` resolution; complex SQL may remain table-level only in impact.
* Length remediation never rewrites the catalog; refresh-from-source remains a separate proposal for add/remove/PK issues.
* The validation action does **not** auto-apply DDL; pair with update-action `failIfDdlNeeded` for target-DB readiness.
* Content quality (nulls, ranges, allowed values) uses the separate Measure / Evaluate quality gate stack — see link:data-quality.adoc[Data quality].

docs.content:
= Business Vault SCD2
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

SCD2 tables are the primary Business Vault output today. They materialize **functional timelines** from raw Data Vault satellite history.

On the `.hbv` canvas, link **one parent hub** to the SCD2 table (drag a Linked Hub, or set **Parent hub** on the table dialog). That line is the grain: it shows which hub the timeline belongs to and where the business key(s) live. Satellite derivatives remain the history feeds. Optional **Include hub business keys** copies those keys onto the SCD2 stream/table; the hub link is still useful when keys stay on the hub.

The hash-key column type and length come from that hub's Data Vault configuration (`BINARY` + MD5 → `BINARY(16)` on SingleStore, not unbounded `VARBINARY`). A Linked Hub is enough to resolve the grain even when a satellite has no parent hub of its own.

== Type 1 vs Type 2 and hybrid attributes

Business Vault SCD2 tables are **pure SCD Type 2**: each functional change produces a version row with `valid_from` / `valid_to` (or your configured validity columns). The plugin does **not** support a per-column Type 1 mode that rewrites every historical version when a “current” value changes.

That is intentional. BV SCD2 is **organizational memory made consumable** (harmonized names, multi-satellite merge, business-effective intervals). Hybrid Type 1 + Type 2 presentation rules usually belong further downstream.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Need |Recommended approach

|Historized attributes (as-of correct)
|Map them on the SCD2 table (Type 2).

|Always-current attributes (e.g. current sales rep on old facts)
|Keep Type 2 history clean; resolve “current” at **mart or query** time by joining the open SCD2 row, a latest satellite, or a separate BV current table/view (see link:business-vault-sql-view.adoc[Business Vault SQL views and tables]). Prefer **hybrid SCD in the dimensional model** when product owners want Type 1 and Type 2 columns on one dimension.

|Mix Type 1 and Type 2 **in the same BV SCD2 table**
|Not a field-mapping feature. Mixing would make some columns look historical while they are not, weaken audit-friendly intermediate history, and is expensive under incremental watermarks.

|Type 1 / Type 2 modes **on a PIT table**
|Wrong layer. PIT tables store hub grain × snapshot dates with satellite load-timestamp **pointers** only. Compose attributes (including always-current ones) when joining raw or BV tables. See link:business-vault-pit.adoc[Business Vault PIT].
|===

In short:

1. Prefer **pure Type 2** BV SCD2 for mapped attributes.
2. Prefer a **separate current-state object** (or open-row filter) for always-current values.
3. Prefer **hybrid Type 1 + Type 2 in the dimensional / information mart layer** for reporting rules.
4. Treat hybrid Type 1 *inside* a historized BV SCD2 table as a last resort outside this builder, not core plugin behaviour.

Dialog help (Hop GUI **Help** on the SCD2 table dialog): link:help/bv-scd2-table-dialog.adoc[SCD2 table dialog].

== What gets generated

For each SCD2 table the plugin builds a Hop pipeline that:

1. Reads satellite history via `TableInput` SQL (grain + functional timestamp + attributes), `ORDER BY` hash key in **Java `String.compareTo` order** (Postgres `COLLATE "C"`, SQL Server `BIN2`, MySQL `BINARY`) so `SortedSchemaMerge` sees a stream that is already sorted the way Hop compares strings. Locale collations such as Postgres `en_US.utf8` sort `10-` before `1-` and would split the same key across satellite legs. The vault record-source / source-indicator column is **not** selected when a satellite has **Store record source indicator** off (VaultSpeed-style mono-source sats). Multi-satellite pipelines never read that physical column; merge identity is the synthetic `_bv_source` value.
2. Adds source indicators when multiple satellites feed one BV table. When a satellite omits the physical column, a Constant supplies the BV record-source value from the satellite config (or the satellite name).
3. Merges streams (multi-satellite) with `SortedSchemaMerge`
4. Repeats sparse attribute columns across merged rows
5. Computes validity bounds with `Analytic Query` (LAG/LEAD)
6. Applies open-interval sentinels with `If Null`
7. Collapses duplicate timestamps with `Group By`
8. Loads the Business Vault target table with `TableOutput` (full rebuild) or runs the incremental write path below

Use **Debug** or **Show build pipeline** on an SCD2 table in the `.hbv` editor to inspect the generated pipeline before running a workflow.

=== Hash-key partitions (large full rebuilds)

When a satellite is too large to `ORDER BY` hash key and load date in one pass, set **Hash-key partitions** to 4, 8, or 16 on the SCD2 table. Full rebuild then:

1. Truncates the BV target **once** with a workflow SQL action (`TRUNCATE TABLE` via the Hop database dialect).
2. Generates partition numbers `0 .. N-1` and runs the SCD2 pipeline once per part, passing `'${PARTITION_COUNT}'` and `'${PARTITION_NUMBER}'`.
3. Filters each satellite `TableInput` with a first-byte modulus of the parent hash key (BINARY: first octet; HEX: first two hex characters; STRING: first dash-separated token). Every version of a hub/link key stays in one partition. STRING/HEX hash keys still `ORDER BY` with a Java-matching binary collation inside each slice.
4. Writes with `TableOutput` **truncate off**, so later partitions append.

**Show build pipeline** opens the parameterized SCD2 pipeline, the partition driver, and the wrapper workflow. Running the inner pipeline alone with defaults loads partition 0 of N.

Constraints:

* Full rebuild only (Incremental already filters by watermark).
* Target load mode is honored: **Table Output** and **Native bulk** append after the SQL truncate; **Staging file** writes one CSV set per partition (`…-${PARTITION_NUMBER}-${Internal.Transform.CopyNr}.csv`) then bulk-loads those files in the wrapper workflow.
* Sequential partition execution (lower peak memory, not parallel wall-clock).

Integration test: `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/update-customer-360-partitioned.hwf` uses `customer-360-partitioned.hbv` (4 parts) and the same golden current-state dataset as the unpartitioned full rebuild.

=== Incremental build mode

Set **Build mode** to *Incremental* on the SCD2 table when you want to append new functional versions instead of truncating and reloading the BV table on every run.

Incremental pipelines extend the shared analytic tail with:

1. **Watermark resolve** — at pipeline generation time the plugin queries the **Business Vault** target with `SELECT MAX(watermark) …` (BV connection only; null → open-start sentinel in Java)
2. **Parameter Generate Rows** — `param_incremental_watermark` (Generate Rows, limit 1) holds the Timestamp value; `param_open_row_filter` holds the open-end sentinel (and watermark when DV/BV share a connection). Generate Rows is used instead of Constant because Constant only enriches incoming rows and would emit nothing as a pipeline start.
3. **Satellite filter** — each DV-connected `TableInput` uses JDBC positional parameters (`source_ts > ?`) with the watermark transform as its **Insert data from** stream. SQL stays dialect-neutral and never references BV tables
4. **Open target baseline** — BV-connected `TableInput` with `valid_to = ?` (open-end bound from the param transform). When DV and BV share the same Hop connection name, hash keys are further restricted with `IN (SELECT … FROM sat WHERE ts > ? UNION …)` — one watermark `?` **per satellite leg** (JDBC does not reuse bind values; the param transform repeats the same watermark once per leg). When connections differ, all open BV rows are read
5. **Watermark attach** — a stream `Constant` (after the analytic chain) adds `_incremental_watermark` to every computed row
6. **Incremental row filter** — `FilterRows` keeps computed rows where `functional_timestamp > _incremental_watermark`
7. **Append** — `TableOutput` with `truncate=false`
8. **Close open version** — `Update` sets `valid_to = valid_from` on the prior open row (match hash key + open `valid_to`) before new open versions are inserted

**Watermark field** resolution:

1. Per-table **Incremental watermark field** override (optional)
2. Per-table **Functional timestamp** field
3. Model-level functional timestamp default
4. Load-date fallback from Data Vault configuration

The watermark is always read from the **Business Vault target table** (`MAX(watermark_field)`), matching the PIT incremental pattern. DV satellite history may live on a **different** database connection than the BV target.

On the first incremental run against an empty BV table the sentinel (`1900-01-01 00:00:00`) applies, so behaviour matches a full rebuild. Later runs process only satellite deltas and close prior open rows in place.

Integration test: `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/update-customer-360-incremental.hwf` loads four DV satellite waves, runs **Business Vault Update** once on `customer-360-incremental.hbv`, then validates current open rows against the same golden dataset as the full-rebuild fixture. Multi-run close-and-append behaviour is covered by unit tests in `BvScd2PipelineSupportTest`. Hash-key partitioned full rebuild: `update-customer-360-partitioned.hwf` / `customer-360-partitioned.hbv` (4 parts, same golden).

== Calculations (SQL expressions)

After collapse, each SCD2 table can compute extra target columns with deterministic SQL scalars. This is the replacement for per-entity `CASE` / `COALESCE` / `CAST` in dbt-core SCD2 models.

* Expressions run **after** Group By collapse and **before** Table Output / incremental write.
* They do **not** create new versions. Mapped satellite attributes remain the grouping keys.
* Target names must be **new columns** (they cannot overwrite mapped attributes, hash keys, hub business keys, or validity fields). Raw mapped columns stay on the table so incremental runs can recompute expressions, unless **Load** is **No** on the mapping (calculation-only; full rebuild only).
* Optional **Include hub business keys** (General tab) left-outer Merge Joins parent-hub BK columns onto the collapsed stream **immediately before** SQL calculations. They are identity fields: available for calculations, but they do not open new versions. **Load hub business keys** (default on) writes them to the BV table; uncheck to keep them on the stream only. The SCD2 merge / repeat / incremental chain is unchanged. The Lineage tab lists every loaded column, including hub business keys when those are loaded.
* Syntax is SQL: `CASE WHEN …`, `COALESCE`, `CAST(x AS VARCHAR(n))`. `x :> VARCHAR(n)` and `x::TYPE` are accepted. MySQL / SingleStore-style `CONCAT`, `HEX`, `UNHEX`, `MD5`, `DATE_FORMAT`, and `TO_DATE` are available for migration.
* Not allowed: `NOW()`, `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, `RANDOM`, subqueries, aggregates, Jinja.

Configure them on the SCD2 table **Calculations** tab. **Add** / **Edit** opens the SQL expression editor (fields + `CASE` / `COALESCE` / `CAST` patterns, large SQL widget, type and description). Generated **production** pipelines insert an **SQL Expression** transform (`calculate_<table>`) after `collapse_*` with a copy of the expressions.

image::images/sql-expression-dialog.png[SQL Expression transform dialog — Keep input fields, optional Business Vault model and SCD2 table, expression list,align="center"]

The SQL Expression transform can also **link a Business Vault model file and SCD2 table**. When both are set, it loads calculations from that table at runtime (inline expressions are ignored). Production generate still copies expressions so load pipelines do not depend on opening the `.hbv` at run time. Help for the transform: link:help/sql-expression-dialog.adoc[SQL Expression].

Integration fixture: `integration-tests/tests/scd2-calculations/update-scd2-calculations.hwf` — deleted-flag `CASE` plus `CAST('Default value' AS VARCHAR(720))` on a single-satellite SCD2 table, golden current-state after initial and update loads. The same workflow also builds `sat_customer_calc_hub_bv` (issue #153): hub `customer_id` on the stream/table, `deleted_flag` mapped with **Load=No**.

=== Tests

When the table is ready, use **Generate calculation unit test** on the SCD2 table (canvas context menu or the **Tests** tab). That creates:

image::images/generate-calculations-unit-test-scd2-context-action.png[SCD2 table context menu — Generate calculation unit test on customer_360_bv,align="center"]

* A slim pipeline `Dummy collapse_sample` → **SQL Expression** (linked to this table) → `Dummy calculated_out`
* Input data set `bv-scd2-<table>-collapse` and golden data set `bv-scd2-<table>-calculated`
* A Hop **pipeline unit test** that injects at `collapse_sample` and compares golden output at `calculated_out`
* A **capture** pipeline: the SCD2 build up to Group By, then Reservoir Sampling (100 rows), then the linked SQL Expression. Optional: run it once against the warehouse to fill the data sets

image::images/generate-calculations-unit-test-scd2-confirmation-dialog.png[Sample warehouse rows confirmation — 100 reservoir-sampled collapsed rows,align="center"]

image::images/bv-scd2-calculations-pipeline-unit-test.png[Generated calculation unit-test pipeline — collapse_sample to SQL Expression (linked to the SCD2 table) to calculated_out,align="center"]

Production SCD2 loads are **not** reservoir-sampled. After capture, re-run the unit test from the pipeline Testing toolbar (no database).

image::images/generate-calculations-unit-test-scd2-completion-report.png[Calculation unit test completion report with pipeline, input data set, and golden data set names,align="center"]

Check model still compiles expressions. Legacy column-level / CSV tests stored on older `.hbv` files still run if present.

=== Migrating from dbt SCD2 SQL

Keep using link:dbt-import.adoc[Import dbt models] for arbitrary SQL business tables. For SCD2-like models:

. Model the raw satellites on `.hdv` (Hop-managed or External read-only).
. Create a BV SCD2 table with field mappings, including CASE inputs such as deleted flags.
. Copy SELECT-list expressions onto **Calculations**.
. Generate a Hop pipeline unit test and sample collapsed rows once.
. Optional: a BV SQL view that projects the calculated columns without the raw flags.

== Source queries (other tables, views, or SQL)

When a satellite-shaped input is **not** on the Data Vault target — for example a corrective view on another database — add a **Source query** on the BV canvas and hop it to the SCD2 table. The Data Vault model still has one target database; the source query is the BV-side exception.

Each generated `TableInput` uses that source's Hop connection. Table/view names are read directly. Authored SQL has `--` line comments and `/* */` block comments stripped, then is wrapped as a subquery so the plugin can add partition `WHERE` and hash-key/date `ORDER BY` outside the inner statement.

On the source query, set **Hash key (source column)** to the physical name (`burger_hkey`) and **Hash key (hub field)** to the hub grain name when they differ (`hub_burger_hkey`). The pipeline maps that with Select Values after Table Input; it does not rename columns in SQL.

SCD2 merges those streams with satellite history on the **same hub grain**. Set **Parent hub** on the SCD2 table. Origin does not matter.

Mixed SCD2 (DV satellites plus source queries) is supported; two or more inputs still require field mappings. The mapping **Source** column is the satellite name or the source-query name. **Suggest mappings** lets you pick one or more of those linked satellites and source queries, then fills unmapped fields from the selection.

== Identity, cutover, and survivorship pipeline

.Show the infographic
[%collapsible]
====
++++
include::diagrams/identity-cutover-survivorship-infographic.html[tag=embed]
++++
====



Three contracts, three homes, wired only by name. A blank pointer keeps today's `SortedSchemaMerge` pipeline:

image::images/diagrams/bv-identity-cutover-survivorship.svg[Business Vault SCD2 — Cutover, identity resolution, and survivorship pipeline,align="center"]

PlantUML source: link:diagrams/bv-identity-cutover-survivorship.puml[bv-identity-cutover-survivorship.puml].

== Identity maps

An **identity map** on the canvas resolves many raw hub hashes to one durable hash. Add it with **Add identity map**. An SCD2 table opts in with **Identity map**. Leave that blank and the timeline stays on the raw hub hash.

image::images/diagrams/bv-identity-map-freeze.svg[Identity map — Freezing hk_durable on first assignment,align="center"]

PlantUML source: link:diagrams/bv-identity-map-freeze.puml[bv-identity-map-freeze.puml].

The generated map pipeline reads the same-as link and the map rows already stored, then upserts. It does not truncate. A raw key that already has a durable key keeps it. A new duplicate in that cluster inherits it. A new cluster hashes the MDM id when one is present, otherwise the current master raw hash, and that value sticks. The preferred business key is updated in place and does not open an SCD2 version.

On each SCD2 leg the generator looks up the map as of the row timestamp, writes the durable hash into the grain column, and keeps the raw hash as `hk_raw`. The preferred business key is carried as `preferred_bk` and is not a version driver. The map `rule_version` is stored as `map_rule_version`, also not a version driver. Rows before the mapping starts follow the unmapped policy: `self` uses the raw hash, `quarantine` and `drop` leave the row out of the timeline. Partitions, when set, use the durable hash and stay a full rebuild. Hub business keys, when loaded, join on `hk_raw` so the durable grain still finds the raw hub.

Incremental build is allowed with a map. Rows after the watermark load as usual. A raw key whose `rule_version` no longer matches the open SCD2 row is read again from the earlier of that map row's `valid_from` and the watermark, and the open row for its durable key is closed. That extra read is generated only when the satellite uses the Business Vault database connection. Otherwise run a full rebuild after the map changes. Survivorship still forces a full rebuild.

Naming an effectivity satellite requires both the from and to columns. Empty effectivity means the same-as match applies for the whole timeline.

== Survivorship

Field mappings can name more than one source for the same target column. Give every one of those rows a **Rank**. `1` wins over `2`. Leave rank blank when the target has a single source. If any rank is set, that SCD2 table uses `SurvivorshipMerge` instead of `SortedSchemaMerge` and Repeat. A table with no ranks is unchanged.

image::images/diagrams/bv-survivorship-rules.svg[Survivorship — Field ranks, null policies, and delta semantics,align="center"]

PlantUML source: link:diagrams/bv-survivorship-rules.puml[bv-survivorship-rules.puml].

The merge reads the legs already sorted by hash key and functional timestamp. At each timestamp it keeps the best-ranked value. **Null policy** `inherit` skips a null and tries the next rank. `apply` writes the null. A blank null policy uses the leg default, then the calendar: a delta-only source inherits, a full or seed source applies. `seed` fills a gap and does not replace a value already held by an upsert source. `delete` withdraws that source. A row is emitted only when the surviving values change. The build is a full rebuild even if the dialog says Incremental.

**Present flag** is an optional source column on a mapping. When the flag is false, a null was left out of the message and does not change the stored value. When the flag is true, a null clears the value even if the null policy is `inherit`. Blank means the column arrived, so the null policy decides.

**Operation field** is an optional column on a satellite or source query.A row value of `upsert`, `delete`, or `seed` overrides the leg operation.A key that does not appear on a delta feed is not deleted.A source query lists either a functional timestamp or a load date, not both.

Calendar priority and the leg priority override are still stored.They are not the field rank.

[#_source_calendars]
== Source calendars

A **source calendar** says when each source system may contribute rows. Add it with **Add source calendar**. It is shared metadata, not a warehouse table. An SCD2 table opts in with **Source calendar**. Leave that blank and every satellite row is kept.

image::images/diagrams/bv-source-cutover-calendar.svg[Source calendar — Half-open cutover windows,align="center"]

PlantUML source: link:diagrams/bv-source-cutover-calendar.puml[bv-source-cutover-calendar.puml].

**Calendar system** is a name you choose, such as `ORACLE` or `KAFKA`. It is not a table name. On the SCD2 table, open **Satellite settings** and pick that name from the dropdown. Source queries are picked on the **Derivatives** tab. A row is kept when the leg's functional timestamp falls in a window for that name.

Oracle through February 2024, Kafka from 1 March 2024 onward:

[cols="1,2,2", options="header"]
|===
|Calendar system |Effective from |Effective to
|ORACLE |1900-01-01 |2024-03-01
|KAFKA |2024-03-01 |
|===

`2024-02-29 23:59:59` is Oracle. `2024-03-01 00:00:00` is Kafka. A date with no time means midnight at the start of that day. An empty effective to means the source is still in use. Dates are `yyyy-MM-dd` or `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`.

The worked example and the column tooltips are in link:help/bv-source-calendar-dialog.adoc[the source calendar help]. How an SCD2 satellite picks `ORACLE` or `KAFKA` is in link:help/bv-scd2-table-dialog.adoc#_satellite_settings[Satellite settings]. Priority and mode do not change this filter. Two SCD2 tables can share the calendar and still pick different calendar systems.

== Single-satellite SCD2

The simplest case: one DV satellite derivative → one BV table.

* Set the satellite as a **derivative** on the SCD2 table
* Configure **functional timestamp** (per table, or model default, or load-date fallback)
* Attribute columns pass through with DV names unless you add field mappings

Example: `integration-tests/tests/basic/vault1.hbv` builds `sat_customer_hb` from `sat_customer`.

== Multi-satellite SCD2

When an SCD2 table references **two or more** satellites (e.g. Customer 360 from demo, contact, address, and preference satellites), you must provide:

* **Field mappings** — map each `(satellite, source field)` to a BV target column name
* **Satellite configs** — optional per-satellite functional timestamp override and source indicator value

The generated **Table Output** / **native bulk loader** field list comes from the SCD2 target layout, which includes every mapping with **Load** enabled (satellite attribute type when known, otherwise a string fallback). You should not need **Get fields** on the bulk loader to pick up mapped columns.

Target **column names** must fit the Business Vault database identifier limit (PostgreSQL **63** characters, MySQL/SingleStore **64**, SQL Server **128**). **Suggest mappings** truncates collision prefixes to that limit; Check model errors if a name is still too long.

Validation enforces:

* All referenced satellites share the same hub (or link) parent, or the SCD2 table has a **Parent hub** / Linked Hub
* Every mapped source field exists on the satellite (or source-query column list)
* No duplicate BV target column from different sources
* Explicit mappings when multiple satellites are present
* Column names do not exceed the target identifier limit

Example: `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/customer-360.hbv` → table `customer_360_bv` with 11 field mappings across 4 satellites.

image::images/business-vault-model-customer-360.png[Customer 360 Business Vault model on the canvas,align="center"]

=== Functional timestamp resolution

Priority order:

1. Per-satellite override in **Satellite configs**
2. Per-table **functional timestamp** field on the SCD2 table
3. Model-level **functional timestamp** in Business Vault configuration
4. **Load date fallback** (typically `x_load_ts` from Data Vault configuration)

The functional timestamp drives SCD2 interval boundaries — not the technical load date unless you choose it explicitly.

=== Valid from / valid to

Defaults come from Business Vault configuration (`x_from_ts`, `x_to_ts` in the sample project). Override per table if needed.

Open intervals use sentinels from configuration (default `1900-01-01 00:00:00` and `9999-12-31 23:59:59`).

== SCD2 table dialog (key fields)

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Field |Description

|Name
|Logical name of the SCD2 table in the `.hbv` model.

|Physical table name
|Target table in the Business Vault database.

|Derivatives
|DV satellite references and/or source queries. At least one satellite or source query is required.

|Include hash key
|When enabled, the parent hash key column is included in the BV table.

|Include hub business keys
|When enabled, parent-hub business key columns are Merge Joined after collapse, before calculations. Identity only (not version drivers). Requires Include hash key and hub-parent satellites. Not supported for link satellites.

|Load hub business keys
|Enabled with Include hub business keys. Checked (default) writes hub BK columns to the BV table. Unchecked keeps them on the stream for calculations only.

|Suggest mappings
|Asks which linked satellites and source queries to fill, reloads the linked `.hdv`, and adds unmapped satellite attributes **and** source-query columns for that selection (hash key / timestamps on the source query are skipped). Reports a clear reason when sources are listed but no fields appear (stale or missing Data Vault model, unresolved satellite or source query, empty satellite Attributes tab, or source query without **Get fields**).

|Functional timestamp
|Column on the satellite stream used as the timeline (see resolution order above).

|Build mode
|`FULL_REBUILD` (default) truncates and reloads the BV table; `INCREMENTAL` filters satellite history and appends/closes versions.

|Hash-key partitions
|`None` (default), or `4` / `8` / `16` parts for a large full rebuild. See <<Hash-key partitions (large full rebuilds)>>.

|SQL Expression copies
|Number of parallel copies of the generated SQL Expression transform after collapse (default 1). A literal (`4`) or a Hop variable such as `'${SQL_EXPRESSION_COPIES}'` so DTAP environments can differ. Rows are round-robin distributed.

|Incremental watermark field
|Optional BV column used for `MAX(...)` watermark reads and incremental write filtering. Defaults to the resolved functional timestamp field.

|Valid from / Valid to
|Output column names for SCD2 interval bounds.

|Field mappings
|Required for multi-satellite tables. Maps satellite attribute → BV column.

|Satellite configs
|Per-satellite functional timestamp and source indicator for multi-satellite merges. The source indicator is the merge tag (`_bv_source`) and the BV record-source value when the satellite does not store a physical source-indicator column. Honor **Store record source indicator** on each DV satellite — SCD2 Table Input SQL never requests a column the satellite table does not have. When a source calendar is selected, **Calendar system** on this tab picks which name on that calendar the satellite uses. It is not a field on the Data Vault satellite.

|Source calendar
|Optional name of a `BvSourceCalendar` on this canvas. Empty means every leg is eligible. See <<Source calendars>>.
|===

The Customer 360 sample uses all three SCD2 dialog areas:

image::images/business-vault-scd2-table-dialog.png[SCD2 table dialog — General tab,align="center"]

image::images/business-vault-scd2-table-dialog-field-mappings.png[SCD2 table dialog — Field mappings,align="center"]

image::images/business-vault-scd2-table-dialog-satellite-settings.png[SCD2 table dialog — Satellite settings,align="center"]

== Target databases

SCD2 pipeline generation requires:

* **Data Vault target database** — on the linked `.hdv` configuration (read satellite history)
* **Business Vault target database** — on the `.hbv` configuration (write BV table)

Both connection names must resolve in Hop project metadata. **Check model** on the `.hbv` file validates this before pipeline generation.

If you change the linked `.hdv` file on disk, use **Reload DV model** on the Business Vault toolbar before generating pipelines.

== External satellites

Satellites marked **External read-only** in the `.hdv` model are skipped by Data Vault Update but remain fully visible to Business Vault generation. Ensure:

* Physical table names match the warehouse
* Attribute lists describe actual columns
* The vault database connection can read those tables

See `integration-tests/tests/multi-satellite-bv/customer-360-external.hdv` and `.hbv` for a working example.

image::images/data-vault-model-customer-360-external.png[External read-only satellites on the Customer 360 Data Vault canvas,align="center"]

== Running loads

* **Debug** — generate and open build pipeline(s) in Hop GUI (no data write unless you run the pipeline)
* **Business Vault Update** action — model check, optional DDL, generate, stage, and execute build pipelines

See link:business-vault-update-action.adoc[Business Vault Update Action].

docs.summary:
= Database Table Metadata
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

The **Database Table Metadata** transform discovers relational table **columns as Hop types** without reading data rows. It is designed for catalog migration and empty tables where **Table Input** + **Metadata structure of stream** cannot
docs.content:
= Database Table Metadata
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

The **Database Table Metadata** transform discovers relational table **columns as Hop types** without reading data rows. It is designed for catalog migration and empty tables where **Table Input** + **Metadata structure of stream** cannot run, and where **Get JDBC Metadata** returns raw database types instead of Hop type / length / precision.

Use it together with link:record-definition-output.adoc[Record Definition Output] (stream field mode) to publish catalog Fields with primary-key positions.

== What it produces

For each column of each selected table, the transform emits one output row with:

* Identity: database connection, schema, table  
* Field: name, **Hop type** (`String`, `Integer`, …), length, precision, ordinal position  
* Primary key: **1-based position** in the composite key (0 if not part of the PK)  
* Native `source_data_type` (JDBC/original column type name when available)  
* Optional foreign key attributes on child columns (constraint name, position, referenced schema/table/column)

Discovery reuses the same path as catalog/source import: `Database.getTableFieldsMeta` plus primary-key and imported-key JDBC metadata. **Empty tables are supported.**

== Dialog

=== General

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Database connection
|Hop relational connection used when not overridden by a connection field.

|Read schema and table from previous transform input?
|When enabled, each input row supplies table (and optionally schema/connection) to inspect. When disabled, a single fixed schema/table is used.

|Include foreign key columns?
|When enabled (default), adds FK columns on the output (denormalized on the child column; first matching imported FK wins if a column participates in multiple constraints).

|Database connection field / Schema field / Table field
|Input field names when reading from the previous transform. Table field is required in that mode.

|Schema / Table
|Fixed schema and table when not reading from input. Table is required.
|===

=== Output fields

Rename any output column. Defaults align with **Record Definition Output** stream field mappings (`field_name`, `field_type`, `field_length`, `field_precision`, `field_primary_key_position`).

== Example: bulk catalog import from a table list

1. Build a list of tables (SQL, CSV, or Get table names).  
2. **Database Table Metadata** — select from input; map schema/table fields; connection fixed or from stream.  
3. **Record Definition Output** — Fields from stream; field grouping = `table_name` (or a record key); map field name/type/length/precision/PK; Physical table from connection/schema/table fields.

== Tips

* Prefer this transform over Get JDBC Metadata when the consumer expects **Hop** types (catalog Fields, DDL transforms, RDO).  
* Unique/non-unique secondary indexes are not emitted yet; PK and imported FKs are.  
* Connection failures and missing tables fail the transform with a clear error for migration pipelines.

:toc: macro

docs.content:
= Resource definition group
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

A **resource definition group** is the project's list of warehouse models plus the default Data Catalog connection. It is the spine for harvest, the schema gate, catalog version tags, lineage browse, architecture / OpenLineage export, and the preferred load action **Update resource definition group**.

It is *not* a folder of catalog record definitions. Source feeds live in the catalog; the group *points at* the `.hdv` / `.hbv` / `.hdm` files that use those feeds.

Architecture picture: link:architecture.adoc#d3-rdg-spine[Architecture — D3]. Build order: link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW].

== When to create one

As soon as the first Data Vault model (`.hdv`) exists and checks clean. Business Vault and dimensional paths can stay empty.

Add `.hbv` and `.hdm` files to the **same** group when you author them. Create a second group only when teams need separate load waves — see link:enterprise-modeling-and-team-collaboration.adoc[Organizing large Data Vault programs].

Retail sample: metadata **`retail-sources`** (`retail-example/metadata/resource-definition-group/retail-sources.json`).

== Create and edit (Hop GUI)

. Open the Hop project so `${PROJECT_HOME}` resolves.
. Metadata perspective → **EDW** → **Resource definition group** → New.
. Set **Name** (for example `sales-edw`) and **Default catalog connection** (Configure EDW typically created `local-catalog`).
. On the **Data Vault models** tab, **Add models** and select the `.hdv` file(s). Prefer `${PROJECT_HOME}/models/….hdv`.
. Leave **Business Vault models** and **Dimensional models** empty until those files exist.
. Save.

image::images/resource-definition-group-editor.png[Resource definition group editor — model lists, harvest actions, lineage, catalog versions, and Validate sources,align="center"]

=== Fields

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Field |Purpose

|Name
|Metadata name used by workflow actions (for example `retail-sources`).

|Description
|Optional.

|Default catalog connection
|FILE catalog used when harvest, validate, tag, and Update RDG do not override it. Individual models may still name a catalog.

|Business process catalog
|Optional link:bus-matrix.adoc[bus matrix] taxonomy. Empty unions every **Business process catalog** in the project.

|Preview row limit
|Rows attempted for file-source readability checks during validation.

|Detailed data type checking
|When on, validation / model checks can compare live source metadata to stored catalog contracts (higher latency).

|Data Vault models tab
|`.hdv` paths. **List order is update order** within the DV layer.

|Business Vault models tab
|`.hbv` paths. Update order within the BV layer.

|Dimensional models tab
|`.hdm` paths. Update order within the DM layer.
|===

Layer order for **Update resource definition group** is always **all DV, then all BV, then all DM**. You cannot interleave layers by shuffling the three lists.

Use **Add models** to pick project files. Filter the path list when the project has many models.

=== Bottom button bar

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Button |What it does

|**Open in EDW Journey**
|Switch to the link:edw-journey.adoc[EDW Journey] perspective for this group (sources through outputs).

|**Bus matrix**
|Open the link:bus-matrix.adoc[Kimball bus matrix] for the group's dimensional models.

|**Generate .hsm from harvest…**
|Day-2: build or merge a source model from the latest harvest FK inventory. Not a greenfield first step.

|**Apply harvest to catalog…**
|Day-2: copy discovered FKs (and optionally field layouts) into working-tree `DV_SOURCE` contracts. Harvest alone never does this.

|**Harvest history…**
|Browse OPS `schema_harvest_*` runs for sources used by this group.

|**Browse lineage…**
|Reverse source-to-target lineage across models in the group.

|**List catalog versions**
|Review tags already stored under the catalog `catalog-versions/` folder.

|**Tag catalog version**
|Freeze **source** contracts currently referenced by the group's models (for example `v1.0.0`).

|**Validate sources**
|Design-time schema check: options dialog (baseline + axes), then results and optional remediation.
|===

== What the group scopes

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Surface |How it uses the group

|**Harvest source metadata** action
|Harvests every catalog source referenced by the listed models.

|**Validate resource definitions** action / **Validate sources**
|Schema gate scope (live, version, harvest run, target DDL, impact).

|**Update resource definition group** action
|Loads every listed model (layer includes on the action can skip BV or DM).

|**Tag / List catalog version**
|Source-contract snapshot for feeds used by the listed models.

|**Browse lineage…**
|Reverse browser across the group's models.

|**Export architecture** / **Export data lineage**
|Model file list for Draw.io and OpenLineage when the group is selected.

|Execution-map crawl
|Expands group models into the `.hem` graph.
|===

The group does **not** list catalog JSON paths. Putting `hop/{project}/sources/*.json` in a model tab is an anti-pattern.

== Catalog publish on update

When **Update resource definition group** (or a per-model Update) has **Publish target tables to catalog** enabled, each successful model write upserts:

* Target table layouts under `models/`, `business-vault/`, or `dimensional/`
* Lineage siblings under `lineage/`
* Model-registry entries used by BV/DM `ref('model', 'table')`

That is why an RDG update **changes the catalog** even though you never edited a source feed. Picture: link:architecture.adoc#d2-catalog-bus[Architecture — D2].

== Growing the group

. First `.hdv` only → first load (raw vault + publish `models/`).
. Author `.hbv` → add it on the Business Vault tab → update again.
. Author `.hdm` → add it on the Dimensional tab → update again.

Same group, same action, more layers. See link:getting-started-edw.adoc#after-first-load[Getting started — after the first load].

== Anti-patterns

* Listing the same model twice.
* Host-absolute paths instead of `${PROJECT_HOME}/models/…`.
* Putting catalog source JSON paths in the model arrays.
* One group per layer (DV group, BV group, DM group) when a single warehouse should load as one wave.
* Expecting harvest or **Validate sources** to create the group or the models — they only *use* the group.

== Related documents

* link:architecture.adoc[Architecture]
* link:getting-started-edw.adoc[Getting started — building an EDW]
* link:update-resource-definition-group-action.adoc[Update resource definition group action]
* link:resource-definition-validation.adoc[Resource definition validation]
* link:metadata-harvesting.adoc[Metadata harvesting]
* link:data-catalog.adoc#catalog-versions[Catalog versions]
* link:source-to-target-lineage.adoc[Source-to-target lineage]
* AI schema notes: link:ai-file-schemas/metadata/resource-definition-group.md[resource-definition-group.md]

docs.summary:
= Data Vault Hub
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

docs.content:
= Data Vault Hub
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

A Hub represents a core business concept that you want to track over time, such as Customer, Product, Supplier, Order, or Account. In Data Vault terms, the hub stores the natural business key(s) that uniquely identify an instance of that concept, plus a surrogate hash key that is derived from those business keys.

Hubs are the foundation of the model. Links and Satellites refer back to them.

== How hub updates work

When you load data into a hub (either from the visual model editor's Debug button or from the Data Vault Update action), Hop generates a pipeline that:

* Makes sure the target hub table exists (it can create or alter it for you).
* Reads the business key values (and the record source indicator) from the source you attached to the hub.
* For *composite* (single vault column) business keys, composes the stored BK string from ordered source parts using the model delimiter (see <<composite-hub-business-keys>>).
* Compares the incoming keys against what is already in the hub (on vault column names).
* Inserts only the rows that represent genuinely new business keys.
* Calculates the hash key for those new rows (by default from ordered parts for composite keys, with optional hash suffix — not written into the stored BK column).
* Writes the new rows together with the current load date and the record source value.

Only new keys are inserted. Existing keys are left untouched. This is the classic Data Vault 2.0 "insert-only" pattern for hubs.

== Options in the Hub dialog

The Hub dialog is organized into three tabs: **Options**, **Keys**, and **Record sources**.

[cols="1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Option |Description

|Name
|The name of this hub definition inside your Data Vault Model. It is also used as the default physical table name if you do not specify an explicit table name. The name must be unique within the model. Press CTRL-SHIFT-N or click **N** to apply a `dv-hub` naming scheme; see link:naming-schemes.adoc[EDW naming schemes].

|Physical table name
|The actual name of the table that will be created or loaded in your target Data Vault database. Leave this empty to use the Name above. This is useful when your metadata name is more business-friendly while the physical table follows a different naming convention.

|Description
|A short business description of what this hub represents. Helpful for documentation and for anyone who later maintains the model.

|Hash key field name (Options tab)
|The name of the surrogate hash key column that will be stored in the hub table. Satellites and Links that attach to this hub will normally reference this column.

If you leave it empty, the plugin will derive a name from the first business key (for example CUSTOMER_ID becomes CUSTOMER_ID_HK). Most teams prefer to set an explicit, consistent name such as CUSTOMER_HK.

|Record source field name (Options tab)
|Optional. Use this when you want the record source column in this particular hub to have a different name than the one defined in the Data Vault Configuration (for example you want HUB_CUSTOMER_SOURCE instead of the global RECORD_SOURCE).

The field supports variables. If left empty, the value from the active Data Vault Configuration is used.

|Business keys (Keys tab)
|One or more business key definitions that together uniquely identify an instance of the hub. Two multi-part styles are supported — see <<composite-hub-business-keys>>:

* *Multipartite vault columns* (default): several rows with different **Name** values → several physical hub columns; hash uses those column names in order.
* *Composite (single vault column)*: **Composite=Y** on one row → one physical hub column; ordered **source field name(s)** supply the parts.

For each business key you can specify:
* The **name** of the column in the hub table (always the physical vault column name).
* An optional description.
* Data type and length (used when the source definition does not provide them).
* **Composite** (Y/N) — single composed vault column from multiple source parts when Y.
* **Source field name(s)** — one source column, or comma-separated ordered parts when Composite=Y. If the source column name matches the hub name for a non-composite key, a single value is enough.
* **Source system** – the name of the Data Vault Source this business key mapping applies to. This column is the key to supporting multiple sources on one hub. When the same logical key (for example `CUSTOMER_ID` or composite `burger_bk`) comes from different source systems under different physical column names, you create separate rows in the business keys table and tag each with its Source system (same **Name**, same part *count* for composite keys).

Use the **Import keys from sources** button on the **Keys** tab to populate business keys automatically. Before using it, make sure you have added at least one source in the **Record sources** tab. The button reads the primary key fields from unmapped sources, creates multipartite-style business key rows (Composite=N), and fills the Source system column. To model a VaultSpeed-style single composed column, set **Composite=Y**, set the vault **Name** to the hub BK column (for example `burger_bk`), and list ordered source parts in **Source field name(s)**.

|Record sources (Record sources tab)
|A hub can be fed by one or more Data Vault Sources. List every source system or feed that will **load this hub** (insert business keys into the hub table).

Do **not** list feeds that only load satellites of this hub. Satellite feeds are independent in Data Vault 2.0; each satellite has its own record source. Parent hash keys on satellites are computed from parent identity *values* on the satellite feed (hub vault key names, or ordered source *parts* for composite hub keys — not a stored composed BK column on the satellite).

You can attach as many hub-load sources as you need. The generated load process will handle each source (typically producing one pipeline per source) but all of them write into the same physical hub table. This is the recommended way to handle a single business concept that receives identity from multiple upstream systems (for example a Customer hub that is populated from both a CRM system and an ERP system). It is also the cheapest way to prevent dangling hashes when a *child* feed (orders, invoices) arrives before the parent master: add that child feed as another hub record source (link dialog **Also load parent hubs...**, or the source-to-vault seed option). See link:datavault-configuration.adoc#_orphan_handling_tab[Orphan handling].
|===

== Integration mode

On the **Options** tab, **Integration mode** controls how Hop loads this hub:

* **Hop managed** (default) — Hop generates DDL, sentinel rows, and update pipelines.
* **External read-only** — the hub table exists elsewhere; Hop documents it for Business Vault and catalog only. Canvas shows `(ext)`.
* **Custom pipelines** — Hop runs `.hpl` files from `customUpdatePipelinePaths` instead of generating pipelines. Canvas shows `(custom)`.

See link:dv-integration-modes.adoc[Data Vault integration modes] for Data Vault Update behavior and validation differences.

== Using the Check model feature with hubs

When you click **Check model** on the model editor toolbar, the plugin validates every hub. Common issues it will report include:

* No business keys have been defined.
* One or more business keys have no name.
* The hub has no record sources listed in the Record sources tab.
* One or more of the listed record sources do not exist in the project.
* Business keys that reference a Source system that is not present in the Record sources list.
* Missing source part columns for composite business keys (or different part *counts* for the same vault BK name across multi-source mappings).
* **Source-to-target type mismatches** for each business key mapping (per record source / part): incompatible Hop types, or source column length/precision larger than the hub business key definition.
* Warning when **Hash composed business key** is enabled together with a non-empty hash content suffix on a hub that uses composite BKs (confirm the recipe intentionally hashes the composed string rather than ordered parts).

Type validation uses the live database schema when **detailed data type checking** is active (always in the GUI; configurable on the Data Vault Update action). A warning is raised when stored source field metadata in the Data Vault Source differs from the live schema.

These checks run before any pipelines are generated, so you catch problems early.

== What gets created in the target database

The plugin builds a target table layout that typically contains (in this order):

1. The hash key column (its type and length depend on the hash algorithm and hash key data type chosen in the configuration: HEX is the default; STRING is human-readable; BINARY is the most compact and is supported on the required Hop **2.19.0+** runtime — see https://github.com/apache/hop/issues/7346[Hop issue 7346]).
2. The business key columns: **one physical column per distinct business key name**, in definition order. Composite keys still contribute a *single* vault column (the composed string). Multipartite keys contribute one column per name. Length and precision come from the business key definition.
3. The record source column (name and length come from the configuration or the per-hub override; variables are supported).
4. The load date column (usually a timestamp, named LOAD_DATE or whatever you configured).

If the table does not exist yet, the generated pipeline will first run the necessary DDL to create it (or alter it if columns are missing). The final load step only writes the fields that belong in the hub (the internal "flag" column used during comparison is excluded).

== Multi-source hubs

A powerful feature of the plugin is that a single hub definition can receive data from multiple independent sources. All sources contribute rows to the same hub table. 

To use this:
1. On the **Record sources** tab, add every Data Vault Source that will feed the hub.
2. On the **Keys** tab, define your business keys. Use the **Source system** column (last column in the business keys table) to indicate which source a particular mapping belongs to.
3. Use **Load from source** once per source (after ensuring the desired source appears in the Record sources list) to pull the correct source column names for that system.

This approach keeps your hub modeling clean: one logical hub table, many places it can be populated from, with explicit control over which source columns map to which business keys.

For composite business keys, every source that maps the same vault **Name** must use the same number of source parts (only the field *names* may differ per source).

[[composite-hub-business-keys]]
== Composite hub business keys (single vault column)

Many warehouses (including VaultSpeed-style models) store a *single* hub business-key column built by concatenating several source fields, while still hashing from those parts under fixed rules.

=== Multipartite vs composite

[cols="1,2,2", options="header"]
|===
|Style |Hub table |Hash inputs (default)

|Multipartite vault columns
|One physical column per business key **Name** (for example `order_id`, `line_no`)
|Those vault column names / stream fields, in order

|Composite (this feature)
|One physical column (for example `burger_bk = IKL#12278170`)
|Ordered *source parts* (for example `num_seq_bkcc_bk`, `num_seq_bk`); optional trailing **hash content suffix** applies to the hash input only
|===

Do not confuse this with **composite catalog feeds** (multi-table `.hsm` queries): those describe *sources*, not hub BK composition.

=== Storage vs hash

* **Stored BK** = ordered parts joined with the model **business key delimiter**, with trim / null placeholder from configuration. The hash content **suffix** is *not* stored in the column (so you can match VaultSpeed: stored `IKL#12278170`, hash input `IKL#12278170#` when delimiter and suffix are both `#`).
* **Hash** (default): `DvHashKey` over ordered part fields, using delimiter, casing, prefix/suffix, trim, and null placeholder from configuration.
* Optional configuration flag **Hash composed business key**: hash the composed vault field only (simpler; may not match trailing-suffix recipes).

Satellites and links **do not store** the composed hub BK column. They map ordered source part columns on *their* feeds and compute the parent/hub hash using the hub definition and the same model hash settings.

=== Modeling example

[source,text]
----
Source parts:  num_seq_bkcc_bk = IKL ,  num_seq_bk = 12278170
Delimiter:     #
Hash suffix:   #
Stored BK:     burger_bk = IKL#12278170
Hash input:    IKL#12278170#   (parts + delimiter + suffix)
----

In the hub Keys tab: Name `burger_bk`, Composite `Y`, Source field name(s) `num_seq_bkcc_bk, num_seq_bk`, plus the Source system for that feed.

== Tips for hubs

* Start with good source definitions (Data Vault Database Source) that accurately declare primary keys and column lengths. This makes **Import keys from sources** work well and produces better target tables.
* When a hub has multiple sources, add them all on the Record sources tab first, then use **Import keys from sources** for each source in turn so the Source system column is populated correctly.
* Prefer composite single-column BKs when you need DDL/hash parity with existing VaultSpeed-style hubs; keep multipartite vault columns when each part is a true natural key column of equal stature.
* Be consistent with hash key naming across the model (either rely on the default suffix or set explicit names on every hub).
* Use the per-hub record source field name override sparingly; most of the time the model configuration's record source field name is sufficient.
* Hashing rules are defined once per model in the embedded configuration (Edit model dialog). Use consistent hash key naming across hubs rather than expecting per-table hashing overrides.

docs.content:
= Business Vault bridge tables
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 3

toc::[]

A **Business Vault bridge** (`BvBridge`) is a consumption-layer table of two or more hub hash keys. Typical uses:

* Many-to-many relationships already stored as a Data Vault link, flattened for reporting joins
* Same-as / hierarchy links (parent and child hash keys of the same hub)
* Optional allocation **weight**

This is **not** a Kimball dimensional bridge (`.hdm` `DmBridge`). Dimensional bridges resolve dimension surrogate keys; BV bridges resolve raw-vault hub hash keys.

== Canvas

On a `.hbv` model, **Add bridge table**. Edit:

* Name and physical table name
* Optional **weight field**
* Optional **load SQL**
* **Linked Data Vault hubs and links** (derivatives)

Bind a **link** whenever the grain already exists in the raw vault. Binding the participating hubs as well is optional; hash-key columns are taken from the link's hubs.

== Layout and DDL

The target layout is:

* One column per distinct hub hash key (from bound links, then bound hubs)
* Optional weight (`Number`)
* Optional load-cycle ID when the BV model stores it

Primary key is the composite of the hash-key columns. Foreign keys to parent hubs are emitted when BV and DV share a physical database and **Generate foreign keys** is on.

== Load pipeline

Business Vault Update includes bridges after SCD2 and PIT, before SQL business tables.

* **No SQL** — `SELECT` of hub hash keys from the first bound Data Vault link
* **SQL present** — Table Input runs the authoring SQL, then the standard BV target load (table output or staging file)

Pipeline names use `bridgePipelineNamePrefix` (default `bv-bridge-`).

== AI Help

On the BV canvas, AI Help can emit `ADD_BRIDGE` (name, optional `linkName` / `hubNames` / `weightField` / `sqlQuery`) and `BIND_DV_TABLE` / `SET_SQL_QUERY`.
